assertion_summary: HER2 amplification predicts sensitivity to Trastuzumab
assertion_description: HER2 amplification defines a clinically relevant subtype of breast cancer. HER2 amplification predicts sensitivity to various targeted therapies including the monoclonal antibody Trastuzumab. The use of Trastuzumab, often in combination with chemotherapy and/or endocrine therapy (depending on hormone receptor status), is now standard of care for HER2-positive breast cancer patients.

assertion_summary: Lung adenocarcinoma positive for ALK-FUSIONS have been found to be sensitive to crizotinib treatment
assertion_description: ALK-FUSIONS induce an active form of the receptor tyrosine kinase ALK. ALK-FUSIONS are found in 3-5% of non-small cell lung cancer and act as a targetable driver mutation. the ALK inhibitor crizotinib was found to be effective in lung cancer patients with ALK fusions and was granted accelerated FDA approval in 2011. The Vysis break-apart FISH assay is an FDA approved test for the presence of ALK fusion. Crizotinib has been approved as a first-line NSCLC treatment in the presence of ALK fusions but subsequently, alectinib has become the preferred first-line therapy (refer to civic.aid:34 for further details).

assertion_summary: R167Q (c.500G>A) is a pathogenic variant for Von Hippel-Lindau
assertion_description: R167Q is the most common mutation associated with Von Hippel-Lindau syndrome. This variant is very rare in the general population at 4.061e-6 in the gnomAD exomes (v2.0.2) proving ACMG code PM2. The variant occurs within the functional domain, disrupting VHL binding to elongin C (ACMG code PM1). Additional codes are provided by the following EIDs. 4913 (PS4), 5062 (PP4), 5264 (PS4), 5354 (PP4), 5487 and 4913 (PP1).

assertion_summary: Non-small cell lung cancer with EGFR L858R mutation is sensitive to erlotininib.
assertion_description: L858R is among the most common sensitizing EGFR mutations in NSCLC, and is assessed via DNA mutational analysis including Sanger sequencing and next generation sequencing methods. Tyrosine kinase inhibitor erlotinib is associated with improved progression free survival over chemotherapy in EGFR L858R patients (civic.EID:885).

assertion_summary: EGFR L858R positive NSCLC is sensitive to afatinib.
assertion_description: L858R is among the most common sensitizing EGFR mutations in NSCLC, and is assessed via DNA mutational analysis, including Sanger sequencing and next generation sequencing methods. Tyrosine kinase inhibitor afatinib is FDA approved as a first line systemic therapy in NSCLC with sensitizing EGFR mutation (civic.EID:2997).

assertion_summary: BRAF V600E mutant melanoma is sensitive to dabrafenib and trametinib combination therapy
assertion_description: Combination treatment of BRAF inhibitor dabrafenib and MEK inhibitor trametinib is recommended for adjuvant treatment of stage III or recurrent melanoma with BRAF V600E mutation detected by the approved THxID kit, as well as first line treatment for metastatic melanoma. The treatments are FDA approved based on studies including the Phase III COMBI-V, COMBI-D and COMBI-AD Trials. Combination therapy is now recommended above BRAF inhibitor monotherapy. Cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma and keratoacanthoma occur at lower rates with combination therapy than with BRAF inhibitor alone.

assertion_summary: NTRK1 Fusions predict sensitivity to Larotrectinib in solid tumors
assertion_description: NTRK1 Fusions predict sensitivity to Larotrectinib across cancer types (solid tumors) and patient ages. Objective response rates have been reported as high as 75% in adults and over 90% in children. NTRK1 forms fusions with multiple partner genes. Larotrectinib is FDA approved for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients with solid tumors characterized by an NTRK gene fusion and without an acquired resistance mutation. Eligible patients have metastatic disease, have progressed on the treatment they’re receiving, are without other treatment options, and are not candidates for surgical resection of their tumor.

assertion_summary: Supports diagnosis of diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma.
assertion_description: ACVR1 G328V mutations occur within the kinase domain, leading to activation of downstream signaling. Exclusively seen in high-grade pediatric gliomas, supporting diagnosis of diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma.

assertion_summary: BRAF V600E mutant melanoma is sensitive to vemurafenib and cobimetinib combination therapy
assertion_description: Vemurafenib and cobimetinib combination is an FDA approved first line treatment for BRAF V600E mutant metastatic melanoma based on clinical data including the Phase III coBRIM trial. The cobas 4800 BRAF V600 Mutation Test is approved as an FDA companion test for Cotellic (cobimetinib) in combination with Zelboraf (vemurafenib).

assertion_summary: BRAF V600K mutant melanoma is sensitive to vemurafenib and cobimetinib combination therapy
assertion_description: Vemurafenib and cobimentinb is an FDA approved first line treatment for BRAF V600K mutant metastatic melanoma based on clinical data including the Phase III coBRIM trial. The cobas 4800 BRAF V600 Mutation Test is approved as an FDA companion test for Cotellic (cobimetinib) in combination with Zelboraf (vemurafenib).

assertion_summary: BRAF V600K mutant melanoma is sensitive to dabrafenib and trametinib combination therapy
assertion_description: Combination treatment of BRAF inhibitor dabrafenib and MEK inhibitor trametinib is recommended for adjuvant treatment of stage III or recurrent melanoma with the less common BRAF V600K mutation detected by the approved THxID kit, as well as first line treatment for metastatic melanoma. This treatment combination was FDA approved based on the (COMBI-v) trial, where 68 V600K metastatic melanoma patients had either a 65 percent response rate to dabrafenib and trametinib combination therapy, or a 44 percent with vemurafenib alone (civic.EID:4181), as well as the COMBI-D (civic.EID:6939), and COMBI-AD (civic.EID:6179) Trials, which also showed superiority of combination therapy.

assertion_summary: VHL E70K (c.208G>A) is Likely Pathogenic
assertion_description: E70K missense variant occurs at a very low allele frequency in the general population (0.00001489 allele frequency in ExAC, 4.365e-6 allele frequency in gnomAD) and was previously identified in several unrelated individuals with VHL disease symptoms (see evidence statements). PM1 (6860); PM2 (per above); PP1 (5805); PP4 (5805;6742).

assertion_summary: Patients with PML-RARA fusions have improved outcomes following ATRA treatment.
assertion_description: The most recent WHO classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia changed the definition of APL from the cytogenetic criteria of t(15;17) to the molecular definition of “APL with PML-RARA” to be inclusive of complex or cryptic rearrangements that lead to a functional transcription factor. The incorporation of all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) and the use of risk stratification (based on WBC counts) in the management of APL has largely improved outcomes for patients with this subtype.

assertion_summary: Adult Patients With De Novo Acute Myeloid Leukemia and t(9; 11)(p22; q23) Have a Superior Outcome to Patients With Other Translocations Involving Band 11q23: A Cancer and Leukemia Group B Study (PMID:9373264)
assertion_description: AML with t(9;11)(p21.3;q23.3) has an intermediate survival, superior to that of AML with other 11q23.3 translocations (PMID:9373264) (WHO 2016)

assertion_summary: The inframe variant, F76del, is pathogenic for Von Hippel-Lindau Disease.
assertion_description: EID5682 shows a large family with the variant cosegregating with affected individuals (PP1). However, confirmed de novo mutations are also described EID5340 (PS2). Both are supported by several other reports with familial and sporadic VHL and this variant. This inframe deletion is not in a repetitive region (PM4) and absent from gnomAD v2.1 (PM2).

assertion_summary: VHL nonsense variant Q195* (c.583C>T) is pathogenic for Von Hippel Landau Disease
assertion_description: VHL variant Q195* (c.583C>T) introduces an early stop codon resulting in a truncated protein. Loss of function VHL variants have been implicated with pathogenicity for Von Hippel Landau disease (PVS1), and this variant has been observed in patients with symptoms and family history highly characteristic of Von Hippel Landau disease (PP4). The variant does not appear in the gnomAD population database (PM2).

assertion_summary: EBF1-PDGFRB is associated with Ph-like ALL and predicts sensitivity to TKIs
assertion_description: The EBF1-PDGFRB fusion is associated with Philadelphia-like molecular subtype of B-ALL. B-ALLs characterized by this fusion show poor response to conventional chemotherapy, with an increased proportion of cases being completely resistant, showing residual disease at the end of induction or relapsing. However, a very good response of EBF1-PDGFRB-positive B-ALL to ABL-class tyrosine kinase inhibitors (imatinib and dasatinib) in combination with standard chemotherapy has been shown in a small number of cases. Clinical trials for ph-like ALL are ongoing.

assertion_summary: BRAF V600E indicates poor prognosis in advanced colorectal cancer
assertion_description: BRAF V600E was associated with worse prognosis in Phase II and III colorectal cancer, with a stronger effect in MSI-Low or MSI-Stable tumors. In metastatic CRC, V600E was associated with worse prognosis, and meta-analysis showed BRAF mutation in CRC associated with multiple negative prognostic markers.

assertion_summary: HEY1::NCOA2 fusions are pathognomonic for and may aid in the diagnosis of mesenchymal chondrosarcoma
assertion_description: The HEY1::NCOA2 fusion results in a chimeric transcription factor. A FISH assay used to detect HEY1::NCOA2 fusion demonstrates it is highly recurrent in mesenchymal chondrosarcoma. Multiple studies find the fusion in 100% of mesenchymal chondrosarcoma samples, but absent in tumor samples from cancer types with overlapping clinical presentations, leading the authors to suggest HEY::NCOA2 has diagnostic utility for mesenchymal chondrosarcoma. Professional guidelines (WHO) list the HEY1::NCOA2 fusion as a desirable diagnostic criteria for mesenchymal chondrosarcoma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: BRAFi + MEKi + EGFRi combination is recommended for BRAF V600E mutation positive colorectal cancer
assertion_description: Encorafenib + binimetinib + (Cetuximab or Panitumumab) or Dabrafenib + Trametinib + (Cetuximab or Panitumumab) are recommended as subsequent therapy for BRAF V600E mutation positive colorectal cancer.

assertion_summary: DNAJB1::PRKACA fusion is highly sensitive and specific for diagnosis of fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma
assertion_description: A head-to-tail in-frame fusion between exon1 of DNAJB1 and exon2 of PRKACA, resulting from a ~400kb genomic deletion, has been reported as highly recurrent in fibrolamellar HCC. Detection of this fusion by RNAseq, RT-PCR and FISH has subsequently shown this fusion to be highly sensitive and specific for diagnosis of fibrolamellar HCC and mixed fibrolamellar HCC. Several hundred fibrolamellar HCC, non-FL HCC or non-malignant tissues have now been assayed to demonstrate this. WHO lists the DNAJB1::PRKACA fusion as a desirable diagnostic criteria for fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: KIAA1549-BRAF fusion supports diagnosis of pilocytic astrocytoma.
assertion_description: The KIAA1549-BRAF fusion includes the entire BRAF kinase domain, leading to constitutive activation of the BRAF kinase, and is the most common genetic alteration in pilocytic astrocytoma. The molecular mechanism is tandem duplication (approximately 1.9 Mb) in the chromosome 7q34 region with breakpoints at the KIAA1549 and BRAF genes. This fusion can be detected with next-generation sequencing (NGS), RNA-Seq, chromosomal microarray analysis, or other PCR-based breakpoint methods that capture the main 16-9, 15-9, and 16-11 breakpoints between KIAA1549 and BRAF.

assertion_summary: Expression of the KIAA1549-BRAF fusion in pilocytic astrocytoma exhibits resistance to vemurafenib due to paradoxical activation of the MAPK pathway.
assertion_description: Vemurafenib is a first-generation BRAF inhibitor, which has received FDA approval for the treatment of advanced BRAF V600-positive skin cancer. Similar to BRAF V600E/K mutations, the KIAA1549-BRAF fusion results in constitutive activation of BRAF, leading to sustained activation of the MEK-MAPK signaling pathway. In contrast to the BRAF V600E monomer, the KIAA1549-BRAF fusion signals as a dimer to activate MAPK signaling and exhibits resistance to vemurafenib. While vemurafenib can bind and inhibit one BRAF molecule in the dimer, it causes the other remaining BRAF to paradoxically activate the downstream MAPK pathway. Therefore, cells expressing KIAA1549-BRAF are resistant to first-generation BRAF inhibitors, like vemurafenib; however, they are responsive to second-generation inhibitors, such as PLX PB-3.

assertion_summary: IKZF1 deletions (both intragenic/partial and large deletions involving the entire gene) are associated with a poor prognosis in pediatric B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL), in terms of increased risk of relapse (RR) and decreased event‐free survival (EFS).
assertion_description: IKZF1 deletions (both focal and non-focal) have been shown to confer a poor prognosis in pediatric B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL), in terms of increased risk of relapse (RR) and decreased event-free survival (EFS). IKZF1 deletions occur in about 15% of pediatric and 40%-50% of adult B-ALL patients; they are enriched in certain high-risk molecular subtypes, including BCR-ABL1 (Ph)-positive and BCR-ABL1 (Ph)-like B-ALL, where they occur in more than 70% of the cases . IKZF1 deletion represents one of the strongest independent predictors of inferior treatment outcome (increased RR and decreased EFS) in childhood B-ALL. However, the presence of co-occurring gene lesions may either enhance or negate the prognostic value of IKZF1 deletions. For instance, IKZF1 deletions occur in approximately 40% of the cases the B-ALLs characterized by deregulation of transcription factors DUX4 (caused typically by DUX4/IGH rearrangement) and ERG, but the outcome of these leukemias remains favorable even in the presence of IKZF1 abnormalities. IKZF1 deletions in B-ALL may include the whole gene (exons 1-8), resulting in decrease or loss (in case of bi-allelic deletions) of IKZF1 expression. Partial gene deletions including exons 4-7 function by creation a dominant-negative (DN) isoform known as IK6. In mouse models, DN Ikaros isoforms have a more severe leukaemic phenotype than mice with low expression of Ikaros. Other common deletion variants include exons 2-3, 2-7 and 4-8. In most cases IKZF1 deletions are monoallelic, although biallelic deletions also occur. In addition to deletions, nonsense, frameshift and missense mutations represent ~7% of IKZF1 alterations in B-ALL.

assertion_summary: PDX models of MLL-r Leukemia showed reduction of leukemia burden when treated with VTP50469
assertion_description: VTP50469 is an orally bioavailable small molecular inhibitor targeting a subset of MLL fusion target genes and significantly improves survival in PDX models of MLL-rearranged leukemia

assertion_summary: CTNNB1 mutations and or monosomy 6 are characteristic genetic aberrations in WNT-activated medulloblastomas.
assertion_description: WNT-activated tumors account for approximately 10% of all medulloblastomas. The WNT pathway activation can be demonstrated by detection of a CTNNB1 mutation (DNA sequencing) or monosomy 6 (chromosomal microarray or FISH), in addition to the accumulation of beta-catenin immunoreactivity in tumor cell nuclei. Approximately 90% of WNT-activated medulloblastomas harbor a somatic mutation in exon 3 of CTNNB1 and or demonstrate monosomy 6. WNT-activated medulloblastomas have a markedly better prognosis relative to the other subtypes, regardless of age at diagnosis.

assertion_summary: HER2 amplification predicts sensitivity to Neratinib.
assertion_description: HER2-receptor positive breast cancer is associated with a poor prognosis and makes up about 20% of a breast cancers. FDA approved companion diagnostic tests to confirm HER2 amplification include IHC, FISH, and CISH. Neratinib, an irreversible tyrosine kinase inhibitor that targets HER2, HER3, HER4, and EGFR, has been approved by the FDA to treat HER2 positive breast cancer as a monotherapy and in combination with chemotherapy based on the results from two Phase III clinical trials (ExteNET & NALA).

assertion_summary: FLT3 tyrosine kinase domain mutations at residue D835 in relapsed / refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) are sensitive to Gilteritinib, a Type I FLT3 inhibitor.
assertion_description: Mutations in the FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3) gene are the most common mutations in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). 5 to 10% of AML is associated with activating point mutations in the FLT3 tyrosine kinase domain (TKD), particularly at the D835 residue. FLT3 D835 mutations are a common mechanism of clinical resistance to type II FLT3 inhibitors (sorafenib, quizartinib and ponatinib), which bind only the inactive kinase conformation. However, gilteritinib, a type I oral inhibitor of FLT3 and AXL, demonstrated preclinical activity against type II FLT3 inhibitor resistance-conferring D835 mutations and clinical activity as monotherapy in Relapsed/Refractory (R/R) FLT3-mutated AML in multiple clinical trials. The 2017 FDA approved FLT3 mutation companion diagnostic assay can detect a D835 or I836 mutation, but cannot distinguish which of these residues is mutated. In 2018, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved gilteritinib as the first FLT3 inhibitor indicated for use as monotherapy for R/R AML with FLT3 D835.

assertion_summary: ALK fusion positive NSCLC is sensitive to alectinib
assertion_description: ALK fusions are found in approximately 5% of NSCLC patients. These fusions act as driver mutations through ligand-independent dimerization of ALK and constitutive downstream pathway activation. Alectinib in ALK-positive metastatic NSCLC has shown superior performance compared to first-line crizotinib in two phase 3 trials (civic.eid:8657 and civic.eid:7284). The VENTANA ALK (D5F3) CDx assay is FDA approved as companion diagnostic.

assertion_summary: Loss of the SMARCB1 gene product INI1 is diagnostic for Atypical Teratoid Rhabdoid Tumors
assertion_description: Loss of the SMARCB1 gene product INI1, assessed by monoclonal antibody is used to for diagnosis of Atypical Teratoid Rhabdoid Tumors (AT/RT). If loss of SMARCB1 or more rarely SMARCA4 is not observed, then WHO guidelines only a recommend a descriptive diagnosis of CNS embryonal tumour with rhabdoid features.

assertion_summary: Non-small cell lung cancer positive for ROS1 fusions are sensitive to crizotinib
assertion_description: ROS1 fusions occur in approximately 1-2% of NSCLC patients. Chromosomal rearrangements involving ROS1 have been found in multiple cancer types including NSCLC, spitzoid melanoma, cholangiocarcinoma, ovarian cancer, gastric cancer, and glioblastoma multiforme. While the mechanism of action of ROS1 fusions remains unknown and may differ based on the fusion partner gene, these fusions cause constitutive downstream pathway activation resulting in sensitivity to tyrosine kinase inhibitors. The Ion Torrent Oncomine Dx Target Test is FDA approved as companion diagnostic for crizotinib.

assertion_summary: FLT3 internal tandem duplication (ITD) mutations in relapsed / refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) are sensitive to Gilteritinib, a Type I FLT3 inhibitor.
assertion_description: The constitutively activating FLT3 internal tandem duplication (ITD) mutation appears in approximately 20-30% of AML patients and are associated with high risk, high relapse rates and poor clinical outcome. The type I selective second-generation oral inhibitor, gilteritinib, received initial global approval for use to treat adults with relapsed or refractory (R/R) FLT3 ITD positive AML in Japan in September 2018. Based on interim results of the ADMIRAL trail (Perl AE, et al., 2019), the FDA approved the drug for treatment of adult R/R AML with FLT3 ITD mutations in November 2018. The FDA approved companion diagnostic, LeukoStrat CDx FLT3 Mutation assay.

assertion_summary: ETV6-NTRK3–positive B-cell lymphoblastic leukemia patients can be sensitive to larotrectinib
assertion_description: An ETV6-NTRK3 gene fusion can be seen in ∼1% of “Philadelphia-like” B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) cases. The TRK pathway has been implicated in the pathogenesis of many cancer types, with NTRK fusions being the best characterized. Larotrectinib and entrectinib are NTRK inhibitors that are FDA approved for patients with NTRK fusion-positive solid tumors, including tumors with ETV6-NTRK3 fusions, and are reported to have durable NTRK inhibition. Evaluating response of ETV6-NTRK3 fusion in B-ALL cases to larotrectinib is difficult due to the rarity of the fusion in this cancer type. However, in a limited number of clinical cases of ETV6-NTRK3 in B-ALL, patients harboring these fusions have responded to larotrectinib. One patient demonstrated a response to treatment that was lost on discontinuation of therapy but showed durable response achieving remission on restarting laroterctinib [civic.eid:8917]. The functional impact of ETV6-NTRK3 has been demonstrated through increased tumorigenic properties in mice, which mimic human B-ALL [civic.eid:8931] and enhanced sensitivity to Larotrectinib both in vivo and in vitro [civic.eid:6930]. These pre-clinical and limited clinical studies show that ETV6-NTRK3 fusion-positive B-ALL may demonstrate response to larotrectinib with minimal adverse effects similar to solid tumors for which these are FDA-approved.

assertion_summary: FLT3 tyrosine kinase domain mutations at residue I836 in relapsed / refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) are sensitive to Gilteritinib, a Type I FLT3 inhibitor.
assertion_description: Mutations in the FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3) gene are the most common mutations in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Activating point mutations in the FLT3 tyrosine kinase domain (TKD) through autophosphorylation occur in 5 to 10% of AML and include the I836 residue. The type I selective second-generation oral inhibitor, gilteritinib, received FDA approval in November 2018 based on interim results of the ADMIRAL trail (Perl AE, et al., 2019) for monotherapy treatment of adult R/R AML with FLT3 I836 mutations. The FDA approved companion diagnostic, LeukoStrat CDx FLT3 Mutation assay, which notably uses EcoRV restriction digest to detect TKD mutations, but is unable to specify which TKD mutation (D835 or I836) is present.

assertion_description: The L184P variant is not found in the general population in the gnomAD exomes (v2.0.2) supporting ACMG code PM2. assertion_summary: VHL R167W (c.499C>T) is a pathogenic rare germline variant that predisposes individuals to von-Hippel Landau disease.
assertion_description: VHL R167W has been observed in a de novo context (both parents confirmed) in a patient with the disease and negative family history (ACMG code PS2) [civic:EID8469]. R167 is an established germline hotspot in VHL (ACMG code: PM1). The variant is not found in the general population: gnomAD exome allele frequency = 0.00001 (ACMG code: PM2). R167W (c.499T>C) was observed co-segregating with VHL disease in multiple affected family members within several unrelated families. Unaffected family members did not harbor the variant (ACMG code: PP1) [civic:EID4912]. The phenotypes and family histories associated with this variant are highly specific for VHL disease (particularly VHL type 2) with a single genetic etiology. [civic:EID8991], [civic:EID5184], [civic:EID5769], [civic:EID6519], [civic:EID5468]. Futhermore, multiple lines of computational evidence support a deleterious effect on the gene or gene product (ACMG code: PP3). This variant is predicted to be pathogenic by at least 7 different programs [civic:EID5184] and has a Revel score of 0.868. Of note, this variant is classified as pathogenic by ClinVar with a two star review status (criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts).

assertion_summary: SNX2-ABL1 fusions are associated with Ph-like B-lymphoblastic leukemia
assertion_description: SNX2-ABL1 fusions in B-ALL are rare based on large retrospective studies. Few cases have been described but when available, microarray expression signatures from patients harboring these fusions, show a Ph-like signature. Co-occurrence with IKZF1 deletions has been described in 2 patients. Relatively short overall survival has also been implied in these rare patients, consistent with the poor outcomes associated with Ph-like B-ALL.

assertion_summary: FLT3-ITD/D839G confers resistance to Ponatinib
assertion_description: FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3) encodes a class III receptor tyrosine kinase expressed in hematopoietic cells. Mutations in the FLT3 gene are the most common mutations in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), occurring in approximately 30% of all AML cases. FLT3-ITD (internal tandem duplication) mutation is the most common type of FLT3 mutation (~25% of all AML cases), and FLT3-TKD mutations (FLT3 mutations in the tyrosine kinase domain, including the D839 residue) have a lower incidence in AML (~7-10% of all cases). Quizartinib is a type II FLT3 TKI (tyrosine kinase inhibitor) with high selectivity and potency that stabilizes the inactive conformation of FLT3 and blocks FLT3-ITD-dependent cell proliferation. However, FLT3 gatekeeper mutant (FLT3-F691L) still shows resistance to Quizartinib. In a preclinical study (PMID: 23430109), Ponatinib is identified as a type II FLT3 TKI exhibiting activity against Quizartinib-resistant FLT3-ITD/F691 gatekeeper mutations. However, Compared to control cells with native FLT3-ITD mutant (IC50: 3.0nM), cells with double mutants (FLT3-ITD/D839G) show resistance to ponatinib (IC50: 54nM). Cell proliferation assay and immunoblots evaluating phosphorylation of FLT3 and its downstream target (STAT5) confirmed such resistance. In addition, a case study also identified the FLT3-ITD/D839G variant in a FLT3-ITD AML patient at diagnosis, with variant not observed at relapse (PMID: 26438511).

assertion_summary: FLT3-ITD/D839G confers resistance to Pexidartinib
assertion_description: FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3) encodes a class III receptor tyrosine kinase expressed in hematopoietic cells. Mutations in the FLT3 gene are the most common mutations in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), occurring in approximately 30% of all AML cases. FLT3-ITD (internal tandem duplication) mutation is the most common type of FLT3 mutation (~25% of all AML cases), and FLT3-TKD mutations (FLT3 mutations in the tyrosine kinase domain, including the D839 residue) have a lower incidence in AML (~7-10% of all cases). Quizartinib is a type II FLT3 TKI (tyrosine kinase inhibitor) with high selectivity and potency that stabilizes the inactive conformation of FLT3 and blocks FLT3-ITD-dependent cell proliferation. However, FLT3 gatekeeper mutant (FLT3-F691L) still shows resistance to Quizartinib. A new potential type 2 FLT3 inhibitor – Pexidartinib (PLX3397) is identified in preclinical studies (PMID: 25847190) with in vitro activity against FLT3 gatekeeper mutants like FLT3-F691L (inhibit proliferation for cells expressing FLT3-ITD and FLT3-ITD/F691L). An in vivo study using MV4;11 exnograft model confirmed the anti-FLT3-ITD activity of pexidartinib. A phase 1/2 study of pexidartinib also showed the clinical activity of Pexidartinib in FLT3-ITD AML patients (PMID: 32330242). However, cells expressing quizartinib-resistant activation loop mutants (at residues D835 and Y842) demonstrated substantial relative resistance to pexidartinib suggesting that PLX3397 may be particularly vulnerable to activation loop substitutions. An in vitro saturation mutagenesis screen was utilized to identify KD mutations that might confer clinical resistance to pexidartinib, and FLT3-D839G was identified in this in vitro saturation mutagenesis screen. FLT3-ITD/D839G (mean IC50 =4.1μM) confer resistance to pexidartinib in Ba/F3 cells when compared with FLT3-ITD alone (mean IC50 =0.15μM). Immunoblots also confirmed such resistance to pexidartinib by evaluating phosphorylation of FLT3 and its downstream target (STAT5) (PMID: 25847190). In addition, a case study also identified the FLT3-ITD/D839G variant in a FLT3-ITD AML patient at diagnosis, with variant not observed at relapse (PMID: 26438511).

assertion_summary: FGFR3 S249C is a predictive biomarker for use of erdafitinib in patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma.
assertion_description: FGFR3, fibroblast growth factor receptor 3, is a receptor tyrosine kinase which, upon binding of the FGF ligand, activates signaling pathways that include the PI3K/AKT and MAPK pathways (PMID: 20094046, 22388515). The FGFR3 p.Ser249Cys variant occurs in the extracellular domain of the receptor and results in constitutive activation and ligand-independent phosphorylation (PMID: 16338952). FGFR3 is altered in 27.8% of urothelial carcinoma patients (PMID: 17668422, 23175443, 31340094, COSMIC), with FGFR3 S249C present in 15.16% of all urothelial carcinoma patients (PMID: 28572459). Patients with FGFR3-altered advanced urothelial tumours, as well as other tumors at other disease sites, have been shown to respond to FGFR inhibitors (PMID: 31340094, 29848605, 31088831, 28341788). Erdafitinib, an FGFR kinase inhibitor that targets FGFR2 and FGFR3, has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of adults with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma which has susceptible FGFR2 and FGFR3 genetic alterations (including S249C), based on the results from the open-label, phase 2 study, BLC2001 (NCT02365597). It should be noted that of the 99 patients in the selected-regimen group who received erdafitinib, only a proportion harbored the S249C variant. The FDA also approved a companion diagnostic test available from Qiagen (Therascreen FGFR RGQ RT-PCR kit) for the detection of this mutation, along with other FGFR3 mutations.

assertion_summary: CD44v6 is a predictive factor of resistance to cisplatin.
assertion_description: Three in vitro studies including gastric and ovarian cancer cell lines show that CD44v6 expression involves resistance to cisplatin. Moreover, a clinical study including 21 patients with cervical cancer shows that patients with low expression of CD44v6 prior to NAC treatment responded to the treatment.

assertion_summary: The somatic G530D variant in DDX41 has been recurrently reported in AML and MDS, including as an acquired variant in patients with germline nonsense/frameshift variants, leading to a classification of Likely Oncogenic by ClinGen/CGC/VICC 2022 Guidelines. However, the lack of sufficiently strong evidence leads to a classification of Tier III by AMP/ASCO/CAP 2017 Guidelines.
assertion_description: The NM_016222.4(DDX41)c.1589C>A variant results in a substitution of glycine with aspartic acid at codon 530 (p.G530D). This G530 residue is highly conserved (PMID: 27502187; UCSC Genome Browser) and is located in the RecA-like helicase C domain (PMID: 26712909; PMID: 26944477; PMID: 27721487), just outside of the VI motif, which is necessary for hydrolysis of ATP (PMID: 28547672; PMID: 27174803) [OM1]. Missense predictors agree on a deleterious effect (REVEL score=0.901, CADD score=25.5, FATHMM score=0.98, MutationAssessor = high) [OP1]. The variant is absent from population databases (gnomAD v2 and v3, ESP, 1000 Genomes) [OP4]. Although the somatic variant is absent from cancerhotspots.org and cBioPortal.org, it has been reportedly acquired in 10 cases (EID10340; EID10341; EID10344; EID10345; EID10346; EID10347 | cited by EID10348); of these cases, the methodology by which the variant was confirmed somatic was apparent (i.e., testing also performed in skin fibroblasts/oral epithelial tissue) in 6 cases (EID10344; EID10345; EID10346) [OM3]. It is also of note that G530D was acquired in 5 of those cases subsequent to a germline nonsense/frameshift variant, which is a typical mechanism for the associated cancer susceptibility disorder (EID10344; EID10345; EID10346). This variant has also been detected in the germline of 5 members from the same family (extensive family history of AML and one MDS), 3 of whom had a diagnosis of AML (EID10339 | cited by EID10342 and EID10343) [PP1?]. OM1+OM3+OP1+OP4(+PP1) = 6 points or Likely Oncogenic (PMID: 35101336) | PS4+PM1+PM2+PP3(+PP1) = Likely Pathogenic (PMID: 34125426)

assertion_summary: Tazemetostat has been withdrawn for treatment of follicular lymphoma with EZH2 Y646F
assertion_description: EZH2 Y641F mutations confer a gain-of-function effect that promotes lymphomagenesis in germinal center–derived B-cell malignancies, including follicular lymphoma, through increased H3K27 trimethylation (H3K27me3) and epigenetic reprogramming (civic.EID:9517, civic.EID:10394). These mutations are recurrently observed in follicular lymphoma and germinal center B-cell–like diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, supporting their role in oncogenesis (civic.EID:433). Functionally, EZH2 Y641F alters PRC2 substrate specificity, leading to accumulation of H3K27me3 and chromatin remodeling (civic.EID:9517). Clinically, patients with EZH2-mutant follicular lymphoma demonstrate higher response rates to the EZH2 inhibitor tazemetostat compared to wild-type cases, supporting mutation-dependent therapeutic sensitivity (civic.EID:9709). Early-phase clinical data further support that activating EZH2 mutations may confer increased sensitivity to EZH2 inhibition (civic.EID:9377). After accelerated FDA approval in 2020, Tazemetostat (Tazverik) was voluntarily withdrawn from all markets and indications on March 9, 2026, after an independent data monitoring committee identified cases of secondary hematologic malignancies in the SYMPHONY-1 trial. In addition, the FDA issued a Drug Alert detailing the increased rate of hematologic secondary primary malignancies (SPMs) associated to the drug. It was reported that 18 out of 318 (5.7%) of patients treated with Tazemetostat developed hematologic SPMs, with no SPM events in the control arm. Most of the SPMs were myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukemia.

assertion_summary: KANK1::NTRK2 positive tumors demonstrate sensitivity to larotrectinib.
assertion_description: Larotrectinib has been approved by the FDA to treat NTRK fusion-positive solid tumors who meet FDA label criteria. Two KANK1::NTRK2 fusion-positive central nervous system tumors in two different individuals demonstrated response to adjuvant larotrectinib treatment. In both reports, NTRK2 was the 3' partner, in-frame, and had the tyrosine kinase domain retained.

assertion_summary: EML4::NTRK3 fusion-positive solid tumors are reported to show objective response to entrectinib therapy.
assertion_description: Entrectinib, a tropomycin receptor kinase (TRK) inhibitor, is an FDA-approved drug for patients with solid tumors positive for NTRK fusions who meet FDA label criteria. The EML4::NTRK3 fusion retains the EML4 basic region and the entire protein tyrosine kinase domain of NTRK3. Multiple EML4::NTRK3 fusion-positive patients with solid tumors treated with entrectinib have demonstrated complete or partial responses.

assertion_summary: KRAS R164Q is a likely benign variant.
assertion_description: KRAS R164Q is not located in a hotspot or critical functional domain, and frequency in gnomAD (1.99e-5) is not low enough to indicate a rare variant. Multiple computational algorithms classify R164Q as deleterious (OP1) but in cell culture, the variant did not induce transformation in the presence of positive controls (SBS2, civc.EID:7935), which results in an oncogenicity score of -3, likely benign.

assertion_summary: FGFR3 S249C is classified as Oncogenic according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.
assertion_description: In vitro studies indicate that the S249C variant affects normal FGFR3 function in a manner consistent with oncogenic activation. The S249C variant results in constitutive FGFR3 activation, ligand-independent signaling, cellular transformation, tumor formation in vivo, and oncogene dependence in bladder cancer models (civic.EID:8855, civic.EID:10386, civic.EID:8811) (OS2). FGFR3 codon 249 is identified as a statistically enriched hotspot in the Cancer Hotspots database. The Cancer Hotspots dataset contains 50 or more samples with a somatic variant at this codon, with the S249C variant present in 10 or more samples (OS3). The S249C variant has a score of 0.902 from the REVEL in silico prediction tool (OP1). The FGFR3 c.746C>G (p.S249C) variant is absent in the gnomAD database (OP4). These codes lead to an Oncogenicity score of 10 (OS2 [4]; OS3 [4]; OP1 [1]; OP4 [1]). Therefore, the FGFR3 S249C variant is classified as Oncogenic according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.

assertion_summary: ETV6::NTRK3- positive infantile fibrosarcoma tumors are sensitive to larotrectinib.
assertion_description: Larotrectinib, a tropomyosin receptor kinase (TRK) inhibitor is an FDA approved drug for those who meet FDA label criteria and an age- and tumor-agnostic therapy for solid tumors with NTRK fusions. Over 90% of patients with NTRK fusion positive infantile fibrosarcoma show response to treatment with larotrectinib.

assertion_summary: KANK1::NTRK2 is classified as an Oncogenic NTRK fusion.
assertion_description: KANK1::NTRK2 has been reported in greater than three published cases (CA1) with most being brain tumors. NTRK2 is the 3’ partner gene in each case (FG1). Additionally, the fusion junctions reported are predicted to retain an intact NTRK2 tyrosine kinase domain (TKD) (FG2) and the TKD to be in-frame (FG3). KANK1 has been reported as a 5’ fusion partner in other kinase gene fusions in cancers (CA2). More than one KANK1::NTRK2 positive tumor has demonstrated response to NTRK targeted (larotrectinib) treatment (CV). Expression of the fusion has been detected by Pan-Trk immunohistochemical staining (FS2). Collectively, FG1+FG2+FG3+CA1+CA2+CV+FS2, results in an Oncogenic classification for KANK1::NTRK2 via the ClinGen NTRK SC-VCEP fusion oncogenicity rules.

assertion_summary: The EML4 (EMAP Like 4)::NTRK3 (Neurotrophic receptor tyrosine kinase) fusion is one of the diagnostic criteria for congenital (infantile) fibrosarcoma.
assertion_description: The EML4 (EMAP Like 4)::NTRK3 (Neurotrophic receptor tyrosine kinase) fusion formed through a reciprocal t(2;15)(p21;q25). The chimeric fusion results from joining the 5′ part of EML4 with the 3′ exons of NTRK3. The EML4::NTRK3 fusion preserves a small portion of the EML4 basic region and the entire protein kinase portion of NTRK3. Cytogenetics, array CGH and RNA analysis verified the EML4::NTRK3 fusion. This fusion is one of the diagnostic criteria for infantile fibrosarcoma.

assertion_summary: ETV6::NTRK3 is one of the diagnostic criteria for congenital (infantile) fibrosarcoma.
assertion_description: Congenital (infantile) fibrosarcoma is a malignant fibroblastic tumor occurring in infancy (typically < 3 years of age) and most frequently is characterized by an ETV6::NTRK3 fusion (civic.eid:11276), (civic.eid:11277). The ETV6::NTRK3 fusion t(12;15)(p13;q25)results from joining the 5′ part of ETV6 encoding the helix–loop–helix (HLH) dimerization domain with the 3′ exons of NTRK3 encoding the protein tyrosine kinase (PTK) domain. Consensus professional guidelines (WHO) list detection of ETV6::NTRK3 or other rearrangements involving NTRK1, BRAF, and MET as part of the diagnostic criteria for infantile fibrosarcoma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 3).

assertion_summary: ETV6::NTRK3 is an oncogenic fusion in multiple cancer types.
assertion_description: ETV6::NTRK3 fusion transcripts include the helix-loop-helix (HLH) protein dimerization domain of ETV6 fused to the tyrosine kinase domain of NTRK3. The fusion has been observed in multiple tumor types including breast secretory carcinoma, congenital fibrosarcoma, mesoblastic nephroma, and other hematologic and solid tumors. Oncogenicity assessment utilizing ClinGen NTRK SC-VCEP Guidelines meets multiple criteria. NTRK3 is 3' partner, retains kinase domain, and is in frame (FG1, FG2, and FG3, civicEID:10502). The fusion is described in > 100 tumor cases (CA1, civicEID:8332, civicEID:6474, civicEID:10841) ETV6 is found in other cancer associated fusions (CA2, civicEID:8599). ETV6::NTRK3 induces transformation in cells and tumors in mice (FS1, civicEID:8931), expression of ETV6 in tumors is verified (FS2, civicEID:10504), and the fusion responds to therapeutic inhibition (CV1, civicAID:39, civicEID:6099).

assertion_summary: ETV6::NTRK3 positive mesoblastic nephroma is responsive to larotrectinib in a pediatric case study.
assertion_description: ETV6::NTRK3 results from t(12;15)(p13;q25) translocation, and is associated with the cellular subtype of congenital mesoblastic nephroma (CMN)(civicEID:10841). The efficacy of NTRK inhibitors against NTRK fusion-positive solid tumors was assessed in patients enrolled on the clinical trial NCT02637687, including CMN that made up about 2% of study participants. The NTRK inhibitor larotrectinib is now approved for use in patients with ETV6::NTRK3 positive solid tumors, including CMN, who meet FDA label criteria. One report in a single 23 month old male patient with CMN (civicEID:10840) showed response.

assertion_summary: SCP2::NTRK1 is classified as a Likely Oncogenic NTRK fusion
assertion_description: SCP2::NTRK1 has been reported in one published breast cancer case. In this case, NTRK1 was listed as the 3’ partner (FG1). Additionally, the fusion breakpoint has been demonstrated to include the NTRK1 tyrosine kinase domain (TKD) (FG2). The fusion and NTRK1 TKD were stated to be in-frame according to the cBioportal sample (P-0044467) report (FG3). Expression of the fusion was detected by pan-TRK immunohistochemical staining (FS2). Collectively, the application of FG1+FG2+FG3+FS2, results in a classification of Likely Oncogenic for SCP2::NTRK1.

assertion_summary: EML4::NTRK3 is classified as an oncogenic NTRK fusion.
assertion_description: The EML4 (EMAP Like 4)::NTRK3 (Neurotrophic receptor tyrosine kinase) fusion formed through a reciprocal t(2;15)(p21;q25). The chimeric fusion results from joining the 5′ part of EML4 (exon 2) with the 3′ exons of NTRK3 (exon 14) (FG1). The EML4::NTRK3 fusion preserves a small portion of the EML4 basic region and the entire protein kinase portion of NTRK3 (FG2). Whole genome sequencing and RNA seq reads identified in-frame EML4::NTRK3 fusion in these cases (FG3; civic.eid:10484). This fusion is documented in more than three solid tumor cases including cervical sarcoma, pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, colon adenocarcinoma, glioblastoma, and poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma (CA1). In vitro studies showed evidence of oncogenic activation of the MAPK/ERK signaling pathway by the EML4::NTRK3 chimeric protein. Both in vitro and in vivo studies indicated tumorigenic phenotype of EML4::NTRK3 fusion gene (FS1; civic.eid:10638, civic.eid:10379). The IHC results using Pan-TRK positivity confirmed the diagnosis of NTRK fusion in all the cases, and sarcoma (FS2; civic.eid:10508, civic.eid:10485). Entrectinib (NTRK inhibitor) therapy decreased the disease burden in more than one case (CV). Collectively, FG1+FG2+FG3+CA1+FS1+FS2+CV, results in a classification of Oncogenic for EML4::NTRK3.

assertion_summary: Case studies suggest Ph-like B-ALL with ZMIZ1::ABL1 responds to dasatinib
assertion_description: ZMIZ1::ABL1 is a fusion which contains in frame ABL1 with kinase domain. A ZMIZ1 proline rich domain is also contained in the fusion, and is thought to drive dimer formation, allowing for ABL1 kinase activation. The fusion has been reported in multiple patients with BCR::ABL1-like ALL. Transfection of ZMIZ1::ABL1 into Ba/F3 cells drives growth factor independent proliferation. In Ba/F3, ZMIZ1::ABL1 cells responded to tyrosine kinase inhibition from imatinib and dasatinib, and an 11 year old patient with Ph-like leukemia and poor response to conventional therapy demonstrated a possible response to treatment with dasatinib and chemotherapy. Clinical trial AALL1131 (NCT02883049) includes post induction dasatinib treatment for Ph-like HR B-ALL with ABL class fusions.

assertion_summary: ALK fusion positive NSCLC is sensitive to ceritinib
assertion_description: ALK fusions are found in approximately 5% of NSCLC patients. These fusions act as driver mutations through ligand-independent dimerization of ALK and constitutive downstream pathway activation. The second generation ALK/ROS1 inhibitor ceritinib was FDA-approved for ALK-positive metastatic NSCLC based on the phase 3 trial ASCEND-4 (NCT01828009) (civic.eid:11190) and the phase 1 trial ASCEND-1 (NCT01283516) (civic.eid:1175). The NCCN Guidelines list ceritinib as an "other recommended" option with the ALK inhibitors alectinib, brigatinib, and lorlatinib as the preferred first-line therapy for ALK rearranged metastatic NSCLC and recommend ceritinib as a subsequent therapy option for patients who progress on crizotinib (NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2023, Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer). The Ventana ALK (D5F3) CDx (an IHC assay detecting ALK protein expression) and FoundationOne Liquid CDx (an NGS assay detecting ALK rearrangements) are FDA approved as companion diagnostics for ceritinib.

assertion_summary: ALK fusion positive NSCLC is sensitive to brigatinib
assertion_description: ALK fusions are found in approximately 5% of NSCLC patients. These fusions act as driver mutations through ligand-independent dimerization of ALK and constitutive downstream pathway activation. The second generation ALK/ROS1 inhibitor brigatinib was FDA-approved for ALK-positive metastatic NSCLC based on the phase 2 trial ALTA (NCT02094573) (civic.eid:4835) and the phase 3 trial ALTA-1L (NCT02737501) (civic.eid:11121). The NCCN Guidelines list brigatinib as well as alectinib and lorlatinib as preferred first-line therapy for ALK rearranged metastatic NSCLC and recommend brigatinib as a subsequent therapy option for patients who progress on crizotinib or who do not tolerate crizotinib (NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2023, Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer). Vysis ALK Break Apart FISH Probe Kit is FDA approved as companion diagnostics for brigatinib.

assertion_summary: ALK fusion positive NSCLC is sensitive to lorlatinib
assertion_description: ALK fusions are found in approximately 5% of NSCLC patients. These fusions act as driver mutations through ligand-independent dimerization of ALK and constitutive downstream pathway activation. The third generation, brain penetrant ALK/ROS1 inhibitor lorlatinib with activity against resistance mutations that arise with first and second generation ALK inhibitor treatment was FDA-approved for ALK-positive metastatic NSCLC based on the phase 2 trial NCT01970865 (civic.eid:7286, civic.eid:7590) and the phase 3 trial NCT03052608 (civic.eid:11191, civic.eid:11192). The NCCN Guidelines list lorlatinib as well as alectinib and brigatinib as preferred first-line therapy for ALK rearranged metastatic NSCLC and recommend lorlatinib as a subsequent therapy option for patients who progress on crizotinib or who do not tolerate crizotinib (NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2023, Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer). Ventana ALK (D5F3) CDx (an IHC assay detecting ALK protein expression) is FDA approved as companion diagnostics for lorlatinib.

assertion_summary: NTRK2 Fusions predict sensitivity to Larotrectinib in solid tumors
assertion_description: Larotrectinib is FDA approved for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients with solid tumors characterized by an NTRK gene fusion and without an acquired resistance mutation. Eligible patients have metastatic disease, have progressed on the treatment they’re receiving, are without other treatment options, and are not candidates for surgical resection of their tumor.

assertion_summary: NTRK3 Fusions predict sensitivity to Larotrectinib in solid tumors
assertion_description: Larotrectinib is FDA approved for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients with solid tumors characterized by an NTRK gene fusion and without an acquired resistance mutation. Eligible patients have metastatic disease, have progressed on the treatment they’re receiving, are without other treatment options, and are not candidates for surgical resection of their tumor.

assertion_summary: RET fusion positive NSCLC is sensitive to selpercatinib
assertion_description: RET fusions are found in 1-2% of NSCLC and shown to be responsive to the selective RET inhibitor selpercatinib. Based on NCT03157128, the FDA has approved selpercatinib for RET fusion positive advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. Oncomine Dx Target Test has been FDA-approved for detecting RET fusions for selpercatinib use in NSCLC.

assertion_summary: ETV6::NTRK3 is one of the diagnostic criteria for the cellular subtype of congenital mesoblastic nephroma
assertion_description: Congenital mesoblastic nephroma is a spindle cell renal tumor occurring in infancy (generally < 1 year of age). The cellular subtype is most frequently characterized by an ETV6::NTRK3 fusion (civic.eid:11279), (civic.eid:11280), (civic.eid:10841). The ETV6::NTRK3 fusion t(12;15)(p13;q25)results from joining the 5′ part of ETV6 encoding the helix–loop–helix (HLH) dimerization domain with the 3′ exons of NTRK3 encoding the protein tyrosine kinase domain (TKD). Consensus professional guidelines (WHO) list the detection of ETV6::NTRK3 fusion as one of the diagnostic criteria for the cellular subtype of mesoblastic nephroma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: Loss of the SMARCB1 is an essential diagnostic criteria for renal medullary carcinoma
assertion_description: SMARCB1-deficient renal medullary carcinoma is a high grade adenocarcinoma which occurs mainly in patients with sickle cell trait. SMARCB1 loss is largely due to inactivating intergenic rearrangements or deletions. Consensus professional guidelines (WHO) list SMARCB1 deficiency as an essential diagnostic criteria of renal medullary carcinoma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: Loss of the SMARCB1 is an essential diagnostic criteria for poorly differentiated chordoma
assertion_description: Poorly differentiated chordoma is an aggressive pediatric and young adult cancer originating from notochordal tissue and characterized by a loss of SMARCB1 staining. SMARCB1 loss is largely due loss of chromosome 22q (including the SMARCB1 locus) or more focal SMARCB1 gene deletion. Consensus professional guidelines (WHO) list loss of SMARCB1 expression as essential diagnostic criteria for poorly differentiated chordoma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: ETV6::NTRK3 is one of the diagnostic criteria for breast secretory carcinoma.
assertion_description: Breast secretory carcinoma is a rare breast cancer with a characteristic histology, associated with ETV6::NTRK3 fusions in the majority of cases (civicEID11343),(civicEID11344),(civicEID11345). The ETV6::NTRK3 fusion t(12;15)(p13;q25) results from joining the 5′ part of ETV6 encoding the helix–loop–helix (HLH) dimerization domain with the 3′ exons of NTRK3 encoding the protein tyrosine kinase domain (TKD). Consensus professional guidelines (WHO) list detection of ETV6 rearrangement or ETV6::NTRK3 as one of the diagnostic criteria for breast secretary carcinoma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 2).

assertion_summary: SS18::SSX fusions are diagnostic for synovial sarcoma with SS18::SSX1 and SS18::SSX2 most common.
assertion_description: Synovial sarcoma is a malignant mesenchymal neoplasm that typically occurs around the joints and is most common in adolescents and young adults. Nearly all cases have an SS18::SSX translocation with the SS18::SSX1 found in two thirds of cases (civic.eid:1065), SS18::SSX2 in one third of cases (civic.eid:1066), and SS18::SSX4 seen more rarely (civic.eid:1074). Professional guidelines (WHO) list the SS18::SSX gene fusion or positive IHC for the SS18:SSX fusion protein as diagnostic criterion for synovial sarcoma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: EWSR1::WT1 is diagnostic for desmoplastic small round cell tumor
assertion_description: Desmoplastic small round cell tumor is a rare, aggressive mesenchymal cancer that primarily affects male children and young adults, characterized by a pathognomonic EWSR1::WT1 fusion. Professional guidelines (WHO) list the EWSR1::WT1 fusion as a desirable diagnostic criteria for desmoplastic small round cell tumor (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: Select RET mutations in medullary thyroid cancer are sensitive to selpercatinib
assertion_description: Activating mutations in RET (e.g. M918T, V804M/L, mutations at extracellular cysteines) are found in 70% of medullar thyroid cancer. The highly selective RET inhibitor selpercatinib has been FDA-approved for RET mutation-positive advanced or metastatic medullary thyroid cancer based on a high rate of durable responses in NCT03157128 (civicEID8851). NCCN lists selpercatinib as a preferred regimen for RET mutation positive thyroid medullary carcinoma (NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2023, Thyroid Carcinoma). Oncomine Dx Target Test has been FDA-approved for detecting RET mutations for selpercatinib use in medullary thyroid cancer.

assertion_summary: RET fusion positive thyroid cancer is sensitive to selpercatinib
assertion_description: Activating RET fusions are found in a range of thyroid cancers with CCDC6::RET and NCOA4::RET being two of the most common fusions reported. The highly selective RET inhibitor selpercatinib is highly effective and has been FDA-approved for RET fusion positive advanced or metastatic thyroid cancer that is radioactive iodine-refractory based on NCT03157128 (civicEID8852). Oncomine Dx Target Test has been FDA-approved for detecting RET fusions for selpercatinib use in thyroid cancer.

assertion_summary: CIC::DUX4 is a desirable diagnostic criteria for CIC-rearranged sarcoma
assertion_description: Previously described as a Ewing-like round cell sarcoma, CIC-rearranged sarcoma is now designated as a separate entity (ICD-O 9367/3). CIC rearrangements are characteristic of this high-grade round cell sarcoma with the CIC::DUX4 fusion found in 95% of cases. Professional guidelines (WHO) list CIC gene rearrangements as desirable diagnostic criteria for CIC-rearranged sarcoma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: BCOR ITD is a desirable diagnostic criteria for clear cell sarcoma of kidney
assertion_description: Clear cell sarcoma of the kidney is a rare renal cancer in children with the majority harboring an internal tandem duplication in BCOR (BCOR ITD) associated with BCOR overexpression. Professional guidelines (WHO) list BCOR ITD, BCOR::CCNB3, or YWHAE::NUTM2 as desirable diagnostic criteria for clear cell sarcoma of the kidney (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: Tazemetostat has been withdrawn for treatment of follicular lymphoma with EZH2 Y646N
assertion_description: EZH2 Y646N is in the SET domain and found in somatic mutations in follicular lymphoma. Y646N mutation leads to widespread deregulation of H3K27me3, a chromatin mark associated with transcriptional repression, and subsequent chromatin structure reorganization. In a preclinical study, EZH2 Y646N–mutant KARPAS-422 cell line showed strong sensitivity to tazemetostat (250 nmol/L), with marked cytotoxicity and increased apoptosis, in contrast to EZH2–wild-type cell lines (civic.EID:11049). Tazemetostat showed higher anti-tumor activity in relapsed/refractory follicular lymphoma patients with activating (gain-of-function) EZH2 mutations (objective response rate 69%; cobas EZH2 Mutation Test) compared to EZH2–wild-type patients (ORR 35%) (civic.EID:9709), supporting its use in patients with prior systemic therapy or those without satisfactory alternative treatment options. These findings are supported by clinical efficacy data from two open-label, single-arm cohorts: in Japanese adult FL patients with EZH2 activating mutations, tazemetostat at 800 mg twice daily achieved an ORR of 76.5%, including complete and partial responses (civic.EID:11109), while in DLBCL patients with EZH2 mutations, tazemetostat also showed partial responses (civic.EID:11110). Early-phase studies in relapsed or refractory B-cell lymphomas demonstrated that tazemetostat treatment is generally well tolerated and shows promising antitumor activity, including patients with EZH2 mutations (civic.EID:11220, civic.EID:11107, civic.EID:11108). After accelerated FDA approval in 2020, Tazemetostat (Tazverik) was voluntarily withdrawn from all markets and indications on March 9, 2026, after an independent data monitoring committee identified cases of secondary hematologic malignancies in the SYMPHONY-1 trial. In addition, the FDA issued a Drug Alert detailing the increased rate of hematologic secondary primary malignancies (SPMs) associated to the drug. It was reported that 18 out of 318 (5.7%) of patients treated with Tazemetostat developed hematologic SPMs, with no SPM events in the control arm. Most of the SPMs were myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukemia.

assertion_summary: Tazemetostat has been withdrawn for treatment of follicular lymphoma with EZH2 Y646H.
assertion_description: The mutation leads to widespread deregulation of H3K27me3, a chromatin mark associated with transcriptional repression, resulting in altered chromatin structure and gene expression programs. Follicular lymphoma patients harboring EZH2 Y646H mutations are predicted to be sensitive to tazemetostat, with clinical evidence supporting increased overall response rates in EZH2-mutant cohorts compared to EZH2 wild-type cohorts (civic.EID:9709, civic.EID:11109, civic.EID:11110). Across multiple phase I/II studies, tazemetostat demonstrated durable and clinically meaningful responses in relapsed/refractory B-cell lymphomas, particularly in genetically defined EZH2-mutant populations, with generally manageable safety profiles (civic.EID:11220, civic.EID:9377, civic.EID:11107, civic.EID:11108). After accelerated FDA approval in 2020, Tazemetostat (Tazverik) was voluntarily withdrawn from all markets and indications on March 9, 2026, after an independent data monitoring committee identified cases of secondary hematologic malignancies in the SYMPHONY-1 trial. In addition, the FDA issued a Drug Alert detailing the increased rate of hematologic secondary primary malignancies (SPMs) associated to the drug. It was reported that 18 out of 318 (5.7%) of patients treated with Tazemetostat developed hematologic SPMs, with no SPM events in the control arm. Most of the SPMs were myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukemia.

assertion_summary: Tazemetostat has been withdrawn for treatment of follicular lymphoma with EZH2 Y646S
assertion_description: EZH2 Y646S is an activating mutation that confers a neomorphic protein function with oncogenic potential, contributing to the development of B-cell malignancies, including follicular lymphoma. This alteration leads to aberrant trimethylation of H3K27, a chromatin mark associated with transcriptional repression, resulting in widespread epigenetic dysregulation and altered chromatin structure. Patients with EZH2-mutant follicular lymphoma are predicted to be responsive to tazemetostat, which has demonstrated clinically meaningful and durable activity with higher response rates in EZH2-mutant compared to wild-type cohorts (civic.EID:9709). Additional clinical studies further support the efficacy and tolerability of tazemetostat in relapsed or refractory B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, particularly in EZH2-mutant disease (civic.EID:11109; civic.EID:11220). After accelerated FDA approval in 2020, Tazemetostat (Tazverik) was voluntarily withdrawn from all markets and indications on March 9, 2026, after an independent data monitoring committee identified cases of secondary hematologic malignancies in the SYMPHONY-1 trial. In addition, the FDA issued a Drug Alert detailing the increased rate of hematologic secondary primary malignancies (SPMs) associated to the drug. It was reported that 18 out of 318 (5.7%) of patients treated with Tazemetostat developed hematologic SPMs, with no SPM events in the control arm. Most of the SPMs were myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukemia.

assertion_summary: Tazemetostat has been withdrawn for treatment of follicular lymphoma with EZH2 Y646C
assertion_description: EZH2 Y646C is an activating mutation that confers a neomorphic protein function with oncogenic potential, contributing to the development of B-cell malignancies, including follicular lymphoma. This alteration leads to aberrant trimethylation of H3K27, a chromatin mark associated with transcriptional repression, resulting in widespread epigenetic dysregulation and chromatin reorganization. Patients with EZH2-mutant follicular lymphoma are predicted to be responsive to tazemetostat, which has demonstrated clinically meaningful and durable activity, with higher response rates observed in EZH2-mutant compared to wild-type cohorts (civic.EID:9709). Additional clinical studies further support the efficacy and tolerability of tazemetostat in relapsed or refractory B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, including EZH2-mutant disease (civic.EID:11109; civic.EID:11220). After accelerated FDA approval in 2020, Tazemetostat (Tazverik) was voluntarily withdrawn from all markets and indications on March 9, 2026, after an independent data monitoring committee identified cases of secondary hematologic malignancies in the SYMPHONY-1 trial. In addition, the FDA issued a Drug Alert detailing the increased rate of hematologic secondary primary malignancies (SPMs) associated to the drug. It was reported that 18 out of 318 (5.7%) of patients treated with Tazemetostat developed hematologic SPMs, with no SPM events in the control arm. Most of the SPMs were myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukemia.

assertion_summary: KIT D816V is resistant to imatinib in systemic mastocytosis
assertion_description: KIT D816V is located within the activation loop of the KIT kinase domain and is a recurrent somatic hotspot mutation in systemic mastocytosis (civic.EID:12913, civic.EID:12917). D816V constitutively activates KIT, promoting ligand-independent signaling and uncontrolled mast cell proliferation (civic.EID:12411). D816V disrupts interactions within the activation loop and weakens JMR–kinase domain interactions, destabilizing the inactive KIT conformation and reducing effective imatinib binding (civic.EID:12915). Consistent with this mechanism, systemic mastocytosis patients harboring KIT D816V exhibit resistance to imatinib, with diminished clinical responses compared with patients harboring wild-type KIT (civic.EID:8360, civic.EID:11160, civic.EID:11369). Thus, imatinib is not expected to provide clinical benefit in systemic mastocytosis patients harboring KIT D816V, and alternative therapeutic approaches are recommended. The KIT D816V Assay (ARUP Laboratories, Inc.) received an FDA-companion diagnostic approval on December 18, 2015.

assertion_summary: QKI::NTRK2 is an oncogenic fusion seen in CNS tumors.
assertion_description: QKI::NTRK2 has been found in gliomas and astrocytomas, The fusion transcript contains the Qua1 dimerization domain of QKI fused to the tyrosine kinase domain of NTRK2. Oncogenicity assessment utilizing ClinGen NTRK SC-VCEP Guidelines yields the following criteria: FG1, FG2, and FG3, since NTRK2 is the 3' partner, retains the tyrosine kinase domain (TKD), and the TKD is in-frame (civicEID:11449)(civicEID:11438). The fusion is described in at least 3 cases (CA1). QKI is found in other cancer associated fusions such as QKI::RAF1 (PMID: 30517658, 28806393) (CA2). QKI::NTRK2 induces transformation in cells and tumors in mice (civicEID:11450, FS1). Collectively, the application of FG1+FG2+FG3+CA1+FS1, results in a classification of Oncogenic for QKI::NTRK2.

assertion_summary: ZFTA fusions are essential diagnostic criteria for supratentorial ependymoma, ZFTA fusion–positive
assertion_description: Supratentorial ependymoma, ZFTA fusion–positive is a circumscribed supratentorial glioma with a ZFTA (formerly C11orf95; HGNC:28449) fusion that occurs in both children and adults. The majority of cases (~70%) harbor ZFTA::RELA fusions with a smaller number harboring alternative ZFTA fusions such as ZFTA::NCOA1, ZFTA::NCOA2, and ZFTA::MAML2. Professional guidelines (WHO) list ZFTA fusions as essential diagnostic criteria for supratentorial ependymoma, ZFTA fusion–positive and a DNA methylation profile meeting the appropriate calibrated score thresholds for supratentorial ependymoma, ZFTA fusion–positive as desirable diagnostic criteria (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7). Of note, this tumor type was previously designated supratentorial ependymoma, RELA fusion–positive.

molecular_profile: DICER1 RNase IIIb Mutation AND DICER1 Loss-of-function
assertion_summary: The combination of a DICER1 loss-of-function mutation and a DICER1 RNase IIIB mutation is a desirable diagnostic criteria for anaplastic sarcoma of the kidney.
assertion_description: Anaplastic sarcoma of the kidney is an extremely rare pediatric kidney tumor described as a multi-patterned cystic and solid sarcoma with anaplasia driven by DICER1 mutations. Consistent with other tumors associated with the DICER1 tumor predisposition syndrome, anaplastic sarcomas of the kidney typically have a truncating loss-of-function DICER1 mutation (that is often but not always germline) and a somatic RNase IIIb missense mutation with altered miRNA processing activity. Professional guidelines (WHO) list biallelic DICER1 pathogenic sequence variants as a desirable diagnostic criteria of anaplastic sarcoma of the kidney (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

molecular_profile: DICER1 RNase IIIb Mutation AND DICER1 Loss-of-function
assertion_summary: The combination of a DICER1 loss-of-function mutation and a DICER1 RNase IIIb mutation is a desirable diagnostic criteria for gynandroblastoma
assertion_description: Gynandroblastoma is a composite sex cord–stromal tumour with elements of of Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor and granulosa cell tumor and a subset of cases are associated with mutations in DICER1 (civicEID:11478), (civicEID:11480), (civicEID:11481). Professional guidelines (WHO) list DICER1 RNase IIIb domain mutations as a desirable diagnostic criteria of gynandroblastoma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

molecular_profile: DICER1 RNase IIIb Mutation AND DICER1 Loss-of-function
assertion_summary: DICER1 alterations (most often a a DICER1 RNase IIIB mutation coupled with a DICER1 loss-of-function mutation) are an essential diagnostic criteria for pituitary blastoma.
assertion_description: Pituitary blastoma is a rare embryonal neoplasm of the sellar region that occurs in infants < 2 years of age. Consistent with other tumors associated with the DICER1 tumor predisposition syndrome, pituitary blastomas typically have a truncating loss-of-function DICER1 mutation (that is often germline) and a somatic RNase IIIb domain missense mutation. Professional guidelines (WHO) list DICER1 alterations as an essential diagnostic criteria of pituitary blastoma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: PAX5 p.P80R as essential diagnostic criteria of the provisional B lymphoblastic leukaemia with PAX5 p.P80R subtype of B-lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma with other defined genetic alterations (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).
assertion_description: PAX5 missense variant p.Pro80Arg defines a genetic subtype of B-lymphoblastic leukemia characterized by a distinctive expression profile and recognized in the WHO and ICC classification. PAX5 P80R B-ALL accounts for approximately 2% of childhood B-ALLs. All cases feature the universal P80R (p.Pro80Arg) mutation and a deletion or mutation of the remaining PAX5 allele. Mutations in RAS and JAK signaling genes are common as secondary changes.

assertion_summary: The NTRK3::SCAPER fusion has uncertain oncogenic significance.
assertion_description: The novel NTRK3::SCAPER fusion was seen in a case of a 4 year old girl with a scalp lesion diagnosed as pigmented epithelioid melanocytoma (PEM). This fusion consisted of NTRK3 exons 1 to 7 and SCAPER exons 13 to 31 formed by an interstitial deletion in Chromosome 15q24.3q25.3 region. In this novel case, the 3’ end of NTRK3 was deleted along with the 5’ end of SCAPER eliminating the likelihood of the presence of a reciprocal functional fusion. NTRK3 is not the 3’ partner and the fusion does not include the NTRK3 tyrosine kinase domain (FG1, FG2, and FG3 are not met). This fusion has no known other cancer association or functional assessment. Due to not meeting FG1, FG2, or FG3, NTRK3::SCAPER is unlikely to activate NTRK, but its unknown if the fusion impacts on tumor biology through alternative means and is therefore categorized as a fusion of unknown significance (FUS).

assertion_summary: FOXR2 activation by structural rearrangement is a diagnostic criterion for CNS neuroblastoma, FOXR2-activated.
assertion_description: CNS neuroblastoma, FOXR2-activated, is a rare pediatric embryonal tumor characterized by activation of the FOXR2 gene. This activation typically results from structural rearrangements involving upstream regions of FOXR2, including inter- and intra-chromosomal rearrangements with other genomic loci. These alterations retain the full FOXR2 coding sequence and lead to elevated FOXR2 expression, likely driven by enhancer hijacking or promoter switching. According to the 5th edition of the WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, FOXR2 activation through gene fusions or structural rearrangements is a molecular feature of CNS neuroblastoma, FOXR2-activated. While high FOXR2 expression is a feature of this entity, it may be observed in a subset of other tumors, including certain high grade gliomas and, rarely, medulloblastomas. Importantly, FOXR2-activated CNS neuroblastoma forms a distinct DNA methylation cluster, making methylation profiling a valuable tool for its accurate diagnosis.

disease: Central Nervous System Tumor With BCOR Internal Tandem Duplication
assertion_summary: BCOR internal tandem duplication is an essential diagnostic criterion for CNS tumor with BCOR ITD (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 6).
assertion_description: CNS tumor with BCOR ITD are characterized by BCOR exon 15 ITD (internal tandem duplication). Professional guidelines (WHO) list an ITD in exon 15 of BCOR as an essential diagnostic criterion with a DNA methylation profile aligned with CNS tumor with BCOR ITD as essential for unresolved cases. BCOR ITDs are present in 3% of CNS high grade neuroepithelial tumors, with variable morphological features including a oval to spindle shaped cells, in solid growth patterns or with perivascular pseudorosettes. Gene expression of BCOR has been shown to be increased in CNS tumor with BCOR ITD. BCOR immunohistochemistry is a sensitive marker for CNS tumor with BCOR ITD.

assertion_summary: EWSR1::FLI1 is pathognomonic for and supports the diagnosis of Ewing sarcoma
assertion_description: Ewing sarcoma is a small round cell sarcoma of soft tissue or bone typically found in children and young adults that harbors a gene fusion involving one member of the FET family of genes (EWSR1, FUS, TAF15) and a member of the ETS family of transcription factors (FLI1, ERG, ETV1, ETV4, FEV). EWSR1::FLI1 t(11;22)(q24;q12) is the most common FET::ETS fusion found in 85-90% of Ewing sarcoma cases. Consensus professional guidelines (WHO) list detection of a FET::ETS fusion (such as EWSR1::FLI1) as a desirable diagnostic criteria of Ewing sarcoma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: EWSR1::ERG is pathognomonic for and supports the diagnosis of Ewing sarcoma
assertion_description: Ewing sarcoma is a small round cell sarcoma of soft tissue or bone typically found in children and young adults that harbors a gene fusion involving one member of the FET family of genes (EWSR1, FUS, TAF15) and a member of the ETS family of transcription factors (FLI1, ERG, ETV1, ETV4, FEV). EWSR1::ERG t(21;22)(q22;q12) is the second most common FET::ETS fusion found in 5-10% of Ewing sarcoma cases. Of note, multiple studies have reported difficulty detecting EWSR1::ERG rearrangements by karyotyping or FISH due to the complexity of the rearrangment and recommend other methods such as RT-PCR for greater sensitivity. Consensus professional guidelines (WHO) list detection of a FET::ETS fusion (such as EWSR1::ERG) as a desirable diagnostic criteria for Ewing sarcoma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: LMNA::NTRK1 is one of the diagnostic criteria for lipofibromatosis-like neural tumors (LPF-NTs).
assertion_description: Lipofibromatosis-like neural tumors (LPF-NTs) are an emerging type of spindle cell tumor typically defined by the presence of an infiltrative, lipofibromatosis-like pattern, CD34 and S100 positivity, negative for SOX10, and typically involving the subcutaneous soft tissue. This tumor type is most often observed in the pediatric and young adult population. Neurotrophic receptor tyrosine kinase 1 (NTRK1) is frequently rearranged in this cancer type with LMNA::NTRK1 being one of the most common fusions found in LPF-NT, observed in about 40% of NTRK1 rearranged cases. LMNA::NTRK1 is one of the diagnostic criteria for lipofibromatosis-like neural tumors (LPF-NTs).

assertion_summary: LMNA::NTRK1 positive tumors demonstrate response to entrectinib
assertion_description: Entrectinib, a TRK inhibitor, is an FDA-approved drug for patients with solid tumors positive for NTRK fusions who meet FDA label criteria. The LMNA::NTRK1 fusion results from an intrachromosomal deletion on chromosome 1 that brings LMNA adjacent to NTRK1 with the NTRK1 tyrosine kinase domain retained. Multiple LMNA::NTRK1 fusion-positive patients with solid tumors treated with entrectinib have demonstrated complete or partial responses. Additionally, multiple in vitro studies have shown cell lines transduced to express LMNA::NTRK1 show sensitivity to entrectinib treatment.

assertion_summary: LMNA::NTRK1 is classified as an Oncogenic NTRK fusion.
assertion_description: The LMNA::NTRK1 fusion results from an intrachromosomal deletion on chromosome 1 that brings LMNA adjacent to NTRK1 with NTRK1 as the 3’ partner gene in each case (FG1). Additionally, the fusion junctions reported are predicted to retain the intact NTRK1 tyrosine kinase domain (TKD) (FG2) and the TKD to be in-frame (FG3). This fusion has been reported in over five individual cases (CA1). The LMNA::NTRK1 fusion has demonstrated response to NTRK targeted treatments (entrectinib and larotrectinib) in multiple cases (CV). Patient-derived xenograft and lentiviral mediated overexpression of LMNA::NTRK1 in cell lines demonstrated increased fusion phosphorylation and downstream activation of kinase targets (FS1). Expression of the fusion has been detected by pan-Trk immunohistochemical staining (FS2). Collectively, FG1+FG2+FG3+CA1+CV+FS1+FS2, results in an Oncogenic classification for LMNA::NTRK1 via the ClinGen NTRK SC-VCEP fusion oncogenicity rules.

assertion_summary: TPM3::NTRK1 positive solid tumors are reported to show objective response to larotrectinib therapy.
assertion_description: Larotrectinib, a TRK inhibitor, is an FDA-approved drug for patients with solid tumors positive for NTRK fusions who meet FDA label criteria. Multiple patients with TPM3::NTRK3 fusion-positive solid tumors treated with larotrectinib have demonstrated complete or partial responses including patients with infantile fibrosarcoma (civic.EID:6101), spindle cell sarcoma (civic.EID:7419), papillary thyroid carcinoma (civic.EID:8042) and lung carcinoma (civic.EID:11692).

assertion_summary: TPR::NTRK1 Fusions are oncogenic in multiple cancer types
assertion_description: TPR::NTRK1 was seen in a pediatric patient with a lipofibromatosis-like tumor. NTRK1 was the 3 prime partner (FG1), contained the full kinase domain (FG2), and was in frame (FG3) in the tumor cells (civic.EID:11704). The TPR::NTRK1 fusion has subsequently been in observed in over 5 tumors (CA1) including mesenchymal tumors, spindle cell neoplasms, thyroid cancer, and glioma. A case study showed considerable response to larotrectinib (CV) in a TPR::NTRK1 positive microsattelite instability-high colorectal cancer patient (civic.EID:11706). The listed evidence indicates the fusion to be oncogenic utilizing the ClinGen NTRK Fusion Somatic Cancer Variant Curation Expert Panel criteria (FG1+FG2+FG3+CA1+CV).

assertion_summary: Tazemetostat has been withdrawn for treatment of follicular lymphoma with EZH2 A692V
assertion_description: EZH2 A692V is an activating mutation that confers a neomorphic enzymatic function, resulting in increased H3K27 trimethylation (H3K27me3) and altered chromatin regulation, which contributes to oncogenic potential and supports the development of B-cell malignancies (civic.EID:11700). Functional studies in B-ALL models further demonstrate that cells harboring analogous EZH2 activating mutations exhibit strong dependency on EZH2 activity and enhanced sensitivity to EZH2 inhibition, supporting a targetable vulnerability (civic.EID:11707). Clinically, EZH2 mutations are associated with improved response to the EZH2 inhibitor tazemetostat in relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma, with higher objective response rates observed in mutant compared to wild-type cases, indicating therapeutic relevance of EZH2 mutation status (civic.EID:9709). After accelerated FDA approval in 2020, Tazemetostat (Tazverik) was voluntarily withdrawn from all markets and indications on March 9, 2026, after an independent data monitoring committee identified cases of secondary hematologic malignancies in the SYMPHONY-1 trial. In addition, the FDA issued a Drug Alert detailing the increased rate of hematologic secondary primary malignancies (SPMs) associated to the drug. It was reported that 18 out of 318 (5.7%) of patients treated with Tazemetostat developed hematologic SPMs, with no SPM events in the control arm. Most of the SPMs were myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukemia.

assertion_summary: Non-small cell lung cancer with EGFR L858R mutation is sensitive to gefitinib.
assertion_description: L858R is among the most common sensitizing EGFR mutations in NSCLC, and is assessed via DNA mutational analysis including Sanger sequencing and next generation sequencing methods. Tyrosine kinase inhibitor gefitinib is associated with improved progression free survival over chemotherapy in EGFR L858R patients.
