phenotypes: Adult onset,Early young adult onset,Childhood onset,Young adult onset
assertion_summary: ASPSCR1::TFE3 is diagnostic for alveolar soft part sarcoma
assertion_description: Alveolar soft part sarcoma (ASPS) is a rare malignant soft tissue tumor affecting children and adults, most frequently seen in young adults. ASPS is characterized by a nonreciprocal chromosomal translocation, der(17)t(X;17)(p11.2;q25) resulting in a ASPSCR1::TFE3 gene fusion. Professional guidelines (WHO) list strong and diffuse nuclear TFE3 expression by IHC as essential diagnostic criteria and TFE3 rearrangement or ASPSCR1::TFE3 fusion detection as a desirable diagnostic criteria for alveolar soft part sarcoma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

disease: Renal Cell Carcinoma With MiT Translocations
assertion_summary: TFE3 fusions are diagnostic for renal cell carcinoma with MiT translocations and correspond to those with a Xp11 translocation
assertion_description: Renal cell carcinomas with MiT translocations (tRCC) are rare kidney tumours associated with either a chromosome 6p21 or Xp11 translocation and occur in both children and adults, but are more common in children. TRCC with a Xp11 translocation are associated with oncogenic activation of TFE3, driven by fusions with multiple gene partners including SFPQ, ASPSCR1, PRCC, among others. Professional guidelines (WHO) list strong nuclear labelling of TFE3 or identification of TFE3 fusion as essential diagnostic criteria for TFE3-rearranged renal cell carcinoma (Xp11 translocation renal cell carcinoma), a subtype of renal cell carcinoma with MiT translocations (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

disease: Renal Cell Carcinoma With MiT Translocations
assertion_summary: TFEB fusions are diagnostic for renal cell carcinoma with MiT translocations and correspond to those with a 6p21 translocation
assertion_description: Renal cell carcinomas with MiT translocations (TRCC) are rare kidney tumours associated with either a chromosome 6p21 or Xp11 translocation and occur in both children and adults, but are more common in children. TRCC with a 6p21 translocation are associated with oncogenic activation of TFEB, most frequently driven by fusions with Alpha (MALAT1). Professional guidelines (WHO) list strong nuclear labelling of TFEB or identification of TFEB fusion as essential diagnostic criteria for TFEB-rearranged renal cell carcinoma (6p21 translocation renal cell carcinoma), a subtype of renal cell carcinoma with MiT translocations (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: YAP1::TFE3 fusion is diagnostic for a subtype of epithelioid haemangioendothelioma
assertion_description: Epithelioid haemangioendothelioma (EHE) is a rare vascular infiltrative tumor that mainly develops in young through to older adulthood. EHE harbor either the WWTR1::CAMTA1 or a YAP1::TFE3 gene fusion. YAP1::TFE3 EHE are associated with unusual histopathologic features and clinical characteristics compared to conventional EHE, which is driven by the WWTR1::CAMTA1 fusion. Professional guidelines (WHO) list TFE3 immunoreactivity as an essential diagnostic criteria and molecular detection of the YAP1::TFE3 fusion as a desirable diagnostic criteria for the subtype of epithelioid haemangioendothelioma with YAP1::TFE3 fusion (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: The presence of TCF3::PBX1 fusion is required for the diagnosis of B-lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma with TCF3::PBX1 fusion
assertion_description: The chimeric oncoprotein from the TCF3::PBX1 fusion, resulting from t(1;19)(q23;q13.3) rearrangement, brings together the N-terminal transactivation domain of TCF3 and the C-terminal DNA-binding domain of PBX1, leading to altered gene regulations that contribute to the development of B-ALL. TCF3 NM_003200.3 exon 16 is typically fused to PBX1 NM_002585.3 exon 3. Of note, the TCF3::PBX1 fusion gene could be found in 0.6% of healthy newborns suggesting that it originates prenatally and is thus likely an early, initiating oncogenic event. B-ALL/LBL with TCF3::PBX1 presents distinct clinical features and prognostic implications and is more common in children than in adults. Professional guidelines (WHO) list demonstration of the TCF3::PBX1 rearrangement as essential diagnostic criteria for B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with TCF3::PBX1 fusion (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: Solid tumors with TPR::NTRK1 fusion are responsive to Larotrectinib
assertion_description: Larotrectinib has been approved by the FDA to treat NTRK fusion-positive solid tumors that meet FDA label criteria. Responses to adjuvant larotrectinib treatment have been reported in patients with TPR::NTRK1 associated tumors including: infant-type hemispheric glioma (civic.EID:11746). advanced-stage papillary thyroid carcinoma in pediatric and adult patients (civic.EID:11748) (civic.EID:11747), non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (civic.EID:11744), and colorectal cancer (civic.EID:11706).

assertion_summary: MET exon 14 skipping alterations in NSCLC are sensitive to the MET inhibitor tepotinib
assertion_description: Alterations that result in the loss of transcription of MET exon 14 due to point mutations, insertions, deletions, or large-scale whole-exon deletions are found in 3-4% of NSCLC patients and lead to impaired MET ubiquitination and degradation, resulting in increased MET signaling . As a result of the phase 2 trial NCT02864992, the FDA approved the MET inhibitor tepotinib in 2021 for adults with metastatic NSCLC harboring exon 14 skipping MET alterations. Of note tepotinib has shown significant clinical benefit in both treatment-naive and pre-treated patients and shown activity against brain metastases.

assertion_summary: MYB rearrangements, mainly MYB::QKI fusions, are desirable diagnostic criteria for angiocentric glioma
assertion_description: Angiocentric glioma is a rare, CNS WHO grade 1 glioma with a diffuse growth pattern and a focal angiocentricity. Almost all angiocentric gliomas have a MYB::QKI gene fusion, and the remainder generally have another MYB alteration. MYB is a transcription factor that is upregulated when structural rearrangements result in truncation of its C-terminal negative-regulatory domain. Professional guidelines (WHO) list the presence of a MYB alteration or a DNA methylation profile meeting the appropriate calibrated score thresholds for diffuse glioma, MYB- or MYBL1-altered as desirable diagnostic criteria for angiocentric glioma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: A rearrangement involving MYB or MYBL1 is an essential diagnostic criterion for diffuse astrocytoma, MYB- or MYBL1-altered
assertion_description: Diffuse astrocytoma, MYB- or MYBL1-altered, is a rare, CNS WHO grade 1, diffusely infiltrative astroglial neoplasm with genetic alterations in MYB or MYBL1 associated with epileptic seizures in children and adults. MYB and MYBL1 are closely related transcriptional transactivators that become upregulated when structural rearrangements result in truncation of their C-terminal negative-regulatory domain. Professional guidelines (WHO) list the presence of a structural MYB or MYBL1 variant or a DNA methylation profile meeting the appropriate calibrated score thresholds for diffuse astrocytoma, MYB- or MYBL1-altered as essential diagnostic criteria for diffuse astrocytoma, MYB- or MYBL1-altered (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: A rearrangement involving MYB or MYBL1 is an essential diagnostic criterion for diffuse astrocytoma, MYB- or MYBL1-altered
assertion_description: Diffuse astrocytoma, MYB- or MYBL1-altered is a rare, CNS WHO grade 1, diffusely infiltrative astroglial neoplasm with genetic alterations in MYB or MYBL1 associated with epileptic seizures in children and adults. MYB and MYBL1 are closely related transcriptional transactivators that become upregulated when structural rearrangements result in truncation of the C-terminal negative-regulatory domain. Professional guidelines (WHO) list the presence of a structural MYB or MYBL1 variant or a DNA methylation profile meeting the appropriate calibrated score thresholds for diffuse astrocytoma, MYB- or MYBL1-altered as essential diagnostic criteria for diffuse astrocytoma, MYB- or MYBL1-altered (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

molecular_profile: YWHAE::NUTM2A Fusion OR YWHAE::NUTM2B Fusion OR YWHAE::NUTM2E Fusion
assertion_summary: YWHAE::NUTM2 fusions are a desirable diagnostic criteria for a subset of clear cell sarcoma of kidney
assertion_description: Clear cell sarcoma of the kidney is a rare renal cancer in young children that most frequently harbors an internal tandem duplication in BCOR (BCOR ITD) with a smaller percentage of cases harboring BCOR::CCNB3 or YWHAE::NUTM2B/E fusions which also upregulate BCOR levels. Professional guidelines (WHO) list BCOR ITD, BCOR::CCNB3, or YWHAE::NUTM2 as desirable diagnostic criteria for clear cell sarcoma of the kidney (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: FGFR3 K508M is classified as Likely Benign according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.
assertion_description: In vitro studies indicate that the K508M is a kinase-dead variant that renders the receptor catalytically inactive while preserving its ability to bind ligand, dimerize, and traffic to the cell membrane. Across multiple independent studies, six disease/cell models (PC12, multiple myeloma, pancreatic cancer, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, cervical cancer, chondrocytes), and multiple independent signaling readouts (phosphorylation, adaptor recruitment, MAPK, PI3K, STAT activation, proliferation, transformation, morphological differentiation), K508M has been uniformly demonstrated to be biologically inert with no oncogenic or transforming potential (civic.EID:11796, civic.EID:11797, civic.EID:11799, civic.EID:11806, civic.EID:11807) (SBS2). The K508M variant has a score greater than 0.7 (0.98) from the REVEL in silico prediction tool (OP1). The K508M variant is absent in the gnomAD database or present at a minor allele frequency of less than 0.0001 (Grpmax Filtering AF, 95% confidence) (OP4). These codes lead to an Oncogenicity score of -2 (SBS2 [-4]; OP1 [1]; OP4 [1]). Therefore, FGFR3 K508M is classified as Likely Benign according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With T(8;21); (q22; Q22.1)
assertion_summary: RUNX1::RUNX1T1 fusion, typically resulting from a reciprocal t(8;21)(q22;q22), is an essential diagnostic criterion for a subtype of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) designated as AML with t(8;21)/RUNX1::RUNX1T1
assertion_description: AML with t(8;21)/RUNX1::RUNX1T1 accounts for approximately 1–5% of AML cases. It is characterized by a fusion of the RUNX family transcription factor 1 gene (RUNX1) located in 21q22 and the RUNX1 partner transcriptional co-repressor 1 gene (RUNX1T1) located in 8q22. The fusion is typically formed by a reciprocal translocation t(8;21)(q22;q22). The translocation joins the 5' portion of the RUNX1 to the 3' portion of RUNX1T1 oriented from telomere to centromere on the der(8) chromosome. AML with t(8;21) shows some characteristic morphologic and immunophenotypic findings. It is associated with a favorable outcome. Professional guidelines (WHO) list the detection of RUNX1::RUNX1T1 as an essential diagnostic criteria and detection of t(8;21)(q22;q22) as desirable diagnostic criteria for acute myeloid leukemia with RUNX1::RUNX1T1 fusion (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: YAP1 fusions are essential diagnostic criteria for supratentorial ependymoma, YAP1 fusion-positive
assertion_description: Supratentorial ependymoma, YAP1 fusion–positive is a circumscribed supratentorial glioma with a YAP1 fusion that occurs predominantly in young children. The majority of cases harbor YAP1::MAMLD1 fusions with a smaller number harboring alternative YAP1 fusions such as YAP1::FAM118B. Professional guidelines (WHO) list YAP1 fusions as essential diagnostic criteria for supratentorial ependymoma, YAP1 fusion–positive and a DNA methylation profile meeting the appropriate calibrated score thresholds for supratentorial ependymoma, YAP1 fusion–positive as desirable diagnostic criteria (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: BCOR internal tandem duplication (ITD) is a desirable diagnostic criteria for sarcoma with BCOR genetic alterations
assertion_description: Sarcoma with BCOR genetic alterations is a rare pediatric sarcoma harboring BCOR fusions or internal tandem duplications (ITD). BCOR ITDs are present in >50% of undifferentiated round cell sarcomas and primitive myxoid mesenchymal tumors of infancy. The size of the ITD varies within this tumor type, with the most common sizes being 66 and 96 bp. Professional guidelines (WHO) list the presence of a genetic abnormality of BCOR (BCOR fusion or BCOR ITD) as a desirable criterion for the diagnosis of sarcoma with BCOR genetic alterations (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7). Immunohistochemical expression of BCOR is a sensitive marker for sarcoma with BCOR genetic alterations.

assertion_summary: BCOR fusion (most commonly BCOR::CCNB3) is diagnostic criterion for sarcoma with BCOR genetic alterations.
assertion_description: Sarcoma with BCOR genetic alterations is a rare pediatric sarcoma harboring BCOR fusions or internal tandem duplications (ITD). BCOR::CCNB3 is the most common fusion, although rare cases have been reported with other partners such as BCOR::MAML3. Professional guidelines (WHO) list the presence of a genetic abnormality of BCOR (BCOR fusion or BCOR ITD) as a diagnostic criterion for sarcoma with BCOR genetic alterations (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: BCOR::CCNB3 fusions are a desirable diagnostic criteria for a subset of clear cell sarcoma of kidney
assertion_description: Clear cell sarcoma of the kidney is a rare renal cancer in young children that most frequently harbors an internal tandem duplication in BCOR (BCOR ITD) with a smaller percentage of cases harboring BCOR::CCNB3 or YWHAE::NUTM2B/E fusions which also upregulate BCOR levels. Professional guidelines (WHO) list BCOR ITD, BCOR::CCNB3, or YWHAE::NUTM2 as desirable diagnostic criteria for clear cell sarcoma of the kidney (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: UFD1::NTRK2 e6::e7 is classified as a benign NTRK fusion.
assertion_description: The rare and novel UFD1::NTRK2 e6::e7 was found in a single case of osteosarcoma with lung metastases. In this case, NTRK2 is the 3’ partner (FG1) and the breakpoint allows for the inclusion of the NTRK2 tyrosine kinase domain (TKD) (FG2). However, sequencing predicted a frameshift that would introduce a premature stop codon upstream of the NTRK2 TKD, thereby interrupting the TKD’s translation. Furthermore, RNA sequencing demonstrated a lack of NTRK2 expression, and immunohistochemistry for pan‐TRK was negative in the tumor sample, indicating a lack of protein expression (FSN). Therefore, given the limited evidence (FG1+FG2+FSN) UFD1::NTRK2 e6::e7 is classified as a benign NTRK fusion.

assertion_summary: RALGPS2::NTRK3 e1::e4 is classified as a benign NTRK fusion.
assertion_description: The rare RALGPS2::NTRK3 fusion e1::e4 was found in a single case of osteosarcoma. NTRK3 is the 3’ partner (FS1), but the fusion sequence does not support the creation of a chimeric protein. Sequencing analysis determined this fusion contained an in‐frame start codon just after the breakpoint, but lacked an endogenous start codon. Additional analysis with RNA-seq demonstrated the absence of transcription of the NTRK3 tyrosine kinase domain and lack of pan-TRK immunohistochemical expression in the tumor sample (FSN). In summary, given the limited evidence (FS1+FSN) RALGPS2::NTRK3 e1::e4 is classified as a benign NTRK fusion.

assertion_summary: WWTR1::CAMTA1 fusion is diagnostic for the majority of epithelioid hemangioendothelioma
assertion_description: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma (EHE) is a rare vascular infiltrative tumor that develops across a wide age range. The majority of EHE harbor the WWTR1::CAMTA1 fusion (-90%), and in the remaining cases a YAP1::TFE3 gene fusion is frequently detected. Professional guidelines (WHO) list immunoreactivity for CAMTA1 as essential diagnostic criteria and confirmation of WWTR1::CAMTA1 fusion as desirable diagnostic criteria for epithelioid hemangioendothelioma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: NUTM1 fusion is an essential diagnostic criteria for NUT carcinoma
assertion_description: NUT carcinoma is a rare aggressive carcinoma with a rearrangement of the NUTM1 gene. In the majority (>75%) of cases, NUTM1 is fused with BRD4, but fusions with other BRD4-interacting proteins such as BRD3, NSD3, ZNF532, and ZNF592 have been reported. Professional guidelines (WHO) list NUTM1 IHC staining or detection of a NUTM1 rearrangement by a molecular technique as essential diagnostic criteria and demonstration of the NUT carcinoma–related partner gene as desirable diagnostic criteria for NUT carcinoma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: SQSTM1::NTRK1 fusion-positive tumors demonstrate sensitivity to larotrectinib.
assertion_description: Larotrectinib has been approved by the FDA to treat NTRK fusion-positive solid tumors in patients that meet FDA label criteria. Patients with SQSTM1::NTRK1 fusion-positive solid tumors of different histologies have demonstrated significant clinical response to larotrectinib. These include a patient with congenital fibrosarcoma, one patient with papillary thyroid carcinoma, and a patient with lung adenocarcinoma.

assertion_summary: EWSR1::CREB3L1 is desirable diagnostic criteria for sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma.
assertion_description: Sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma (SEF) is a rare aggressive type of sarcoma with the EWSR1::CREB3L1 detected in approximately 50-60% of cases. Professional guidelines (WHO) list EWSR1::CREB3L1 as desirable diagnostic criteria for sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: FUS::CREB3L2 is desirable diagnostic criteria for low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma.
assertion_description: Low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma (LGFMS) is a rare type of sarcoma with molecular and morphological overlap with sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma that harbors the FUS::CREB3L2 fusion in >90% of cases. Professional guidelines (WHO) list FUS rearrangements as desirable diagnostic criteria for low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: EGFR T790M predicts sensitivity to osimertinib in non-small cell lung cancer
assertion_description: The EGFR T790M mutation occurs in approximately 50-60% of EGFR mutated non small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients treated with first or second-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs). The third-generation EGFR TKI osimertinib has been shown to inhibit proliferation signaling and growth in cell line and xenograft models (civic.EID:963) and human cell lines (civic.EID:967) with EGFR T790M. Case study reports indicate benefit from osimertinib for NSCLC patients with primary sensitizing EGFR mutations who progressed on first line TKI treatment with the emergence of T790M (civic.EID:12946). Osimertinib was given accelerated approval for treatment of T790M positive NSCLC patients who had progressed on previous TKI therapy based on results from a Phase I study showing a 59% objective response rate to osimertinib in these patients (civic.EID:965), and then granted regular approval after the confirmatory phase 3 trial (AURA3) further indicated benefit with a 71 percent overall response rate in T790M patients who had progressed on TKI therapy versus 31 percent response rate with chemotherapy (civic.EID:1867).

assertion_summary: BCR::NTRK2 fusion-positive tumors demonstrate sensitivity to entrectinib.
assertion_description: Entrectinib has been approved by the FDA to treat NTRK fusion-positive solid tumors in patients who meet the FDA label criteria. For example, a BCR::NTRK2 fusion-positive central nervous system tumor, specifically a high-grade glioma in an adult patient, demonstrated a partial response to entrectinib. Alternatively, a pediatric patient with a low-grade glioma of the spine demonstrated stable disease on treatment; however, the follow-up period was short (2.5 months) and no further information was provided. Overall, NTRK2 fusions in central nervous system tumors have demonstrated a response to entrectinib.

assertion_summary: MN1 rearrangements are essential diagnostic criteria for Astroblastoma, MN1-altered
assertion_description: Astroblastoma, MN1-altered is a rare primary CNS tumor characterized by distinctive histological features including astroblastic pseudorosettes and vascular hyalinization, and defined by the presence of MN1 gene rearrangements that predominantly affect children and young adults . MN1 fusions most frequently involve MN1 and BEND2 genes fused in-frame. Professional guidelines (WHO) list MN1 alterations or a DNA methylation profile meeting the appropriate calibrated score thresholds for astroblastoma, MN1-altered as essential diagnostic criteria for astroblastoma, MN1-altered (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: Solid tumors with high TMB show increased sensitivity to pembrolizumab
assertion_description: Patients with solid tumors who have increased TMB have shown increased sensitivity to pembrolizumab (civic.EID:12083, civic.EID:12086). KEYNOTE-158 was a prospectively-planned retrospective analysis of patients with previously treated unresectable or metastatic TMB-H solid tumors, and found increased response rates of 29% to permbolizumab in patients with greater than 10 mutations per MB, and 6% in patients below (civic.EID:12082). Pembrolizumab is FDA approved in adults and children with unresectable or metastatic solid tumors with TMB >= 10 mutations/MB, where TMB is measured via an approved next generation sequencing oncology panel based on tissue whole exome sequencing. High TMB calculated from measuring circulating tumor DNA in the blood (H-bTMB) has also been shown to correlate to improved patient outcomes (civic.EID:12724).

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With CBFA2T3::GLIS2 Fusion
assertion_summary: CBFA2T3::GLIS2 fusion, resulting from a cryptic chromosome 16 inversion inv(16)(p13.3q24.3), is an essential diagnostic criterion for an emerging AML subtype designated as acute myeloid leukemia with CBFA2T3::GLIS2 fusion by the WHO Classification of Tumours Online
assertion_description: CBFA2T3::GLIS2 fusion is frequently detected in non-down syndrome acute megakaryoblastic leukemia (AMKL), but it is not restricted to AMKL and can also be observed in other French-American-British (FAB) subtypes. However, this fusion is exclusively observed in pediatric AML patients. It is characterized by a fusion of CBFA2T3, a member of the ETO family of nuclear corepressors, to GLIS2, a member of the GLI family of transcription factors. The fusion is formed by a cryptic inversion of chromosome 16, inv(16)(p13.3q24.3). The presence of CBFA2T3::GLIS2 identifies a subgroup of patients with significantly worse overall survival. Professional guidelines (WHO) list CBFA2T3::GLIS2 fusion or inv(16)(p13q24) as essential diagnostic criteria for the emerging AML subtype designated acute myeloid leukemia with CBFA2T3::GLIS2 fusion (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With MNX1::ETV6 Fusion
assertion_summary: MNX1::ETV6 fusion or t(7;12)(q36;p13) are diagnostic criteria for an emerging subtype of acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) referred to as acute myeloid leukemia with MNX1::ETV6 fusion by the WHO Classification of Tumours Online.
assertion_description: MNX1::ETV6 fusion is primarily detected in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) of infancy and very young childhood. The fusion is formed by a translocation of chromosomes 7q and 12p, t(7;12)(q36;p13). The oncogenic mechanism appears to be overexpression of the MNX1 gene. Cases are frequently associated with a gain of chromosome 19. Professional guidelines (WHO) list MNX1::ETV6 fusion or t(7;12)(q36;p13) as diagnostic criteria for the emerging acute myeloid leukemia subtype known as AML with MNX1::ETV6 fusion (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: BCR::ABL1 fusion is the result of a chromosomal translocation involving 9q and 22q, t(9;22)(q34;q11). BCR::ABL1 fusion is a diagnostic criterion for B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with BCR::ABL1 fusion (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).
assertion_description: BCR::ABL1 fusion is the result of a chromosomal translocation involving 9q and 22q, t(9;22)(q34;q11), which fuses the 5' portion of the BCR (BCR Activator Of RhoGEF And GTPase) gene in 22q11 with the 3'portion (including the entire kinase domain) of the ABL1 (ABL Proto-Oncogene 1, Non-Receptor Tyrosine Kinase) gene in 9q34. The fusion is expressed from the derivative chromosome 22, which is also known as Philadelphia (Ph) chromosome. The BCR::ABL1 fusion is more commonly associated with chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML), however, is also detected in approximately 5% of pediatric and 25% adult B-lymphoblastic leukemia patients. There are two major isoforms of BCR-ABL1, the long isoform (p210) and the short isoform (p190), but the entire ABL1 kinase domain is always included. The p190 isoform is more common in B-lymphoblastic leukemia. Professional guidelines (WHO) list BCR::ABL1 fusion as a diagnostic criterion for B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with BCR::ABL1 fusion (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: Professional guideline (WHO) recognize AML with DEK::NUP214 fusion as a distinct diagnostic entity, with the presence of t(6;9)(p22.3;q34.1) and/or DEK::NUP214 fusion listed as an essential diagnostic criterion (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).
assertion_description: The DEK::NU214 fusion originates from a t(6;9)(p23;q34) and is observed in approximately 0.6–1.7% of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cases in children and 1% of the cases in adults. The fusion junction is typically between exon 2 of the DEK gene and exon 6 of the NUP214.DEK encodes a protein involved in DNA replication and mRNA processing and NUP214 encodes a nuclear pore complex protein necessary for the cell cycle and for transport of material between the nucleus and cytoplasm. . AML cases with the DEK::NUP214 fusion gene are characterized by marrow basophilia, preceding myelodysplasia and a poor prognosis. ~70% of AMLs with the fusion gene exhibit internal tandem duplications of the tyrosine kinase FLT3 (FLT3-ITD).

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With NPM1::MLF1 Fusion
assertion_summary: NPM1::MLF1 fusion or t(3;5)(q25;q35) is a diagnostic criterion for an emerging subtype of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) referred to as acute myeloid leukemia with NPM1::MLF1 fusion by the WHO Classification of Tumours (5th ed.).
assertion_description: NPM1::MLF1 is a rare gene fusion detected in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The fusion is formed by a translocation of chromosomes 3q and 5q, t(3;5)(q25;q35). The translocation joins the 5' portion of the NPM1 (Nucleophosmin 1) in 5q35.1 to the 3' portion of the MLF1 gene (Myeloid Leukemia Factor 1) localized in 3q25.2. Professional guidelines (WHO) list NPM1::MLF1 or t(3;5)(q25;q35) as a diagnostic criterion for the AML with NPM1::MLF1 subtype of AML with other defined genetic alterations (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: The FLT3 N841I mutation is classified as Oncogenic.
assertion_description: The FLT3 N841I has demonstrated the ability to induce IL3 independent cell growth in BaF3 cells, constitutive activation of FLT3, and downstream pathway activation (OS2). This amino acid change occurs within the tyrosine kinase domain (TKD) of FLT3 (OM1). This variant has been observed in 9 myeloid malignancy samples in the cBioportal database along with 5 published cases (14 total) (OM3). The missense predictor, ClinPred, supports a deleterious effect with a score of .998 (OP1). The variant is absent from gnomAD v4.1 and in a region with >20x coverage (OP4). N841I has an oncogenicity classification of Oncogenic based on the following FLT3 SC-VCEP specified codes of the ClinGen/CGC/VICC criteria: OS2 (4) + OM1 (2) + OM3 (2) + OP1 (1) + OP4 (1) = 10 points - Oncogenic

assertion_summary: TCF3::HLF fusion or t(17;19)(q22;p13.3) are essential diagnostic criteria for an emerging subtype of B lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma referred to as B lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma with TCF3::HLF fusion
assertion_description: TCF3::HLF is a rare gene fusion detected in B lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma. The fusion is formed by a translocation of chromosomes 17q and 19q, t(17;19)(q22;p13.3). The translocation can either be Type 1 fusing TCF3 exon 16 to HLF exon 4 and includes inserted non-template and intronic sequences, or Type 2 fusing TCF3 exon 15 to HLF exon 4. Professional guidelines (WHO) list TCF3::HLF as an essential diagnostic criteria for B lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma with TCF3::HLF fusion (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: UBTF-TD frequently found in relapsed pediatric AML
assertion_description: UBTF-TD frequently found in relapsed pediatric AML

assertion_summary: MEF2D rearrangements are essential diagnostic criteria for an emerging subtype of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma referred to as B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with MEF2D rearrangement.
assertion_description: MEF2D rearrangements occur as primary alterations in approximately 4% of pediatric and up to 10% of adult B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL) cases. These rearrangements result in fusions of MEF2D with various partner genes, of which BCL9 and HNRNPUL1 are the most common, and CSF1R, DAZAP1, HNRNPUL1, SS18, HNRNPH1, and FOXJ2 are less frequently observed. MEF2D is the 5' partner, and fusions preserve its DNA binding and dimerization domain. MEF2D-rearranged B-ALLs are characterized by a distinct immunophenotype, older age at diagnosis, and poor outcome. Professional guidelines (WHO) list MEF2D rearrangements as an essential diagnostic criterion for the provisional subtype of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with MEF2D rearrangement, under B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with other defined genetic alterations (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With CEBPA Mutation
assertion_summary: CEBPA mutations, including biallelic (CEBPA-dm) and isolated bZip mutations, are diagnostic criteria for a subtype of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) designated as AML with CEBPA mutation.
assertion_description: CEBPA ( CCAAT Enhancer Binding Protein Alpha) mutations are primary oncogenic drivers in 5% of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cases in children and 5–11% of AML cases in adults. Two main types of mutations are typically observed: isolated mutations in the C-terminal DNA-binding basic leucine zipper (bZip) region and biallelic (CEBPA-dm) mutations, where one mutation occurs in the bZip region and the other in the N-terminal transactivation domain. CEBPA bZip and biallelic mutations are essential diagnostic markers that inform risk stratification and guide treatment decisions. Professional guidelines (WHO) list the presence of bi-allelic mutations in CEBPA, or a single mutation located in the bZIP region as diagnostic criteria for AML with CEBPA mutation.

assertion_summary: VPS18::NTRK3 e4::e1 is classified as a benign NTRK fusion.
assertion_description: The intrachromosomal VPS18::NTRK3 e4::e1 was reported in a single osteosarcoma case. NTRK3 is the 3’ partner (FG1), but the fusion contained a premature stop codon predicted to prevent the full translation of the NTRK tyrosine kinase domain (TKD). RNA sequencing demonstrated a lack of NTRK3 expression and immunohistochemistry for pan‐TRK was negative in the tumor sample, indicating a lack of detectable protein (FSN). The FG3 assessment for fusion gene structure was not met and both independent assessments for fusion expression (RNA and protein) were negative. Therefore, given the limited evidence (FG1+FSN) indicates VSP18::NTRK3 e4::e1 is classified as a benign NTRK fusion.

assertion_summary: VPS18::NTRK3 e4::e18 is classified as a NTRK fusion of uncertain significance
assertion_description: The intrachromosomal VPS18::NTRK3 e4:e18 was detected in a single colorectal cancer case. NTRK3 is the 3’ partner (FG1). This fusion only includes two exons (18 & 19) of the NTRK3 tyrosine kinase domain (TKD), which consists of exons 14-19. Since the fusion junctions are not predicted to lead to a chimeric protein retaining the entire TKD, FG2 and FG3 for gene structure do not apply. No evidence assessing RNA or protein expression was presented to support the benign classification. The fusion unlikely has an activated NTRK, but the fusion's potential impacts on tumor biology through alternative means are unknown. Therefore, with only the code of FG1 applied, VPS18::NTRK3 e4:e18 is classified as a fusion of uncertain significance.

assertion_summary: The t(8;16)(p11;p13) translocation and the resulting KAT6A::CREBBP fusion are critical diagnostic markers for a distinct high-risk subtype of pediatric acute myeloid leukemia (AML) recognized as an emerging molecular entity (AML with KAT6A::CREBBP fusion) in the WHO classification.
assertion_description: The t(8;16)(p11;p13) chromosomal translocation and the resulting KAT6A::CREBBP fusion are key diagnostic markers in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), identified in cases with distinctive clinical features such as leukemia cutis and a poor prognosis. In children, the peak incidence of this AML subtype is in the neonatal period. Gene expression profiling reveals upregulation of genes like HOXA and RET, similar to KMT2A-rearranged AML. Professional guidelines (WHO) list KAT6A::CREBBP fusion as an essential diagnostic criterion for emerging molecular subtype of AML with KAT6A::CREBBP fusion under AML with other defined genetic alterations (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: NUTM1 rearrangements are essential diagnostic criteria for a distinct subtype of pediatric B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) with NUTM1 rearrangement.
assertion_description: NUTM1 rearrangements are primary oncogenic drivers in 3-5% of pediatric B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) cases. NUTM1 rearrangements are enriched in infant KMT2A-negative B-ALL. These rearrangements occur with different 5' partner genes, including SLC12A6, CUX1, IKZF1, and ACIN1, and are mutually exclusive with other primary B-ALL-associated genetic alterations. Professional guidelines (WHO) list NUTM1 rearrangements as an essential diagnostic criterion for the subtype of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with NUTM1 rearrangement (WHO Classification of Tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: IGH::IL3 is an essential diagnostic criteria for a rare subtype of B lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma referred to as B lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with IGH::IL3 fusion.
assertion_description: IGH::IL3 is a rare gene fusion detected in B lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma. The fusion is typically formed by a translocation of chromosomes 5 and 14 in which the IGH enhancer region (14q32.1) is juxtaposed to the vicinity of the IL3 gene (5q31.1) and results in increased production of interleukin-3 (IL3). B lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with IGH::IL3 fusion often presents with eosinophilia and seems to have a predominance for males. Professional guidelines (WHO) list IGH::IL3 as an essential diagnostic criteria for B lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with IGH::IL3 fusion (WHO Classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: Zenocutuzumab-zbco (BIZENGRI), a bispecific HER2- and HER3-directed antibody is indicated for the treatment of adults with advanced, unresectable or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring a NRG1 gene fusion with disease progression on or after prior systemic therapy, or, adults with advanced, unresectable or metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma harboring a NRG1 gene fusion with disease progression on or after prior systemic therapy.
assertion_description: The FDA granted accelerated approval to zenocutuzumab-zbco (Bizengri, Merus N.V.) for 1) adults with advanced, unresectable, or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring a neuregulin 1 (NRG1) gene fusion with disease progression on or after prior systemic therapy, 2) or advanced, unresectable, or metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma harboring a NRG1 gene fusion with disease progression on or after prior systemic therapy. This represents the first FDA approval of a systemic therapy for patients with NSCLC or pancreatic adenocarcinoma harboring an NRG1 gene fusion (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/761352s001lbl.pdf). *This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate and duration of response. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial(s)

assertion_summary: DUX4 rearrangements are essential diagnostic criteria for a distinct subtype of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with DUX4 rearrangements.
assertion_description: DUX4 rearrangements are primary oncogenic drivers in 5–7% of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL) cases, particularly in adolescents and young adults (AYA). DUX4 rearrangements involve the insertion of the DUX4 gene into the IGH locus, resulting in overexpression of DUX4 under the control of the IGH enhancer. These rearrangements are frequently associated with co-occurring ERG deletions (55–63%) and are mutually exclusive with other primary B-ALL-associated genetic alterations. Professional guidelines list DUX4 rearrangements as an essential diagnostic criterion for the subtype of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with DUX4 rearrangements (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

disease: Large B-cell Lymphoma With IRF4 Rearrangement
assertion_summary: IRF4 gene rearrangement is a diagnostic criterion for a subtype of large B-cell lymphoma referred to as large B-cell lymphoma with IRF4 rearrangement.
assertion_description: IRF4 rearrangement is detected in a subset of large B-cell lymphomas. The rearrangement juxtaposes the IRF4 oncogene next to one of the immunoglobulin (IG) loci, most frequently IGH, and leads to overexpression of MUM1 (protein encoded by IRF4). IRF4 rearranged large B-cell lymphoma is predominantly detected in children and adolescents. Professional guidelines (WHO) list IRF4 gene rearrangement and/or IRF4 expression as a diagnostic criterion for large B-cell lymphoma with IRF4 rearrangement (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: The presence of the RBM15::MRTFA fusion or t(1;22)(p13;q13) is a diagnostic criterion for a subtype of acute megakaryoblastic leukemia (AMKL) predominantly occurring in non-Down syndrome infants.
assertion_description: The RBM15::MRTFA fusion is a rare genetic alteration identified in acute megakaryoblastic leukemia (AMKL). The fusion results from the translocation t(1;22)(p13;q13), predominantly observed in non-Down syndrome infants. The RBM15::MRTFA fusion gene combines RBM15 and MRTFA, encoding a chimeric protein that disrupts normal transcriptional processes. Professional guidelines (WHO) list RBM15::MRTFA as a diagnostic criterion for AMKL with RBM15::MRTFA fusion (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: JAK2 fusions are diagnostic for a subset of BCR::ABL1 (Philadelphia)–like B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL).
assertion_description: BCR::ABL1 (Philadelphia/Ph)–like B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) is a high-risk leukemia subtype driven by kinase and cytokine receptor signaling activation. This subtype harbors rare JAK2 fusions involving partner genes such as ATF7IP, BCR, EBF1, ETV6, PAX5, PPFIBP1, SSBP2, STRN3, TERF2, and TPR, leading to JAK2 overexpression and constitutive kinase activation. Professional guidelines (WHO) recognize Ph-like B-ALL as a distinct diagnostic entity, with JAK2 fusions listed as one of its defining molecular features (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: The presence of the PML::RARA fusion or t(15;17)(q24.1;q21.2) is a key diagnostic marker for acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL), a subtype of acute myeloid leukemia (AML).
assertion_description: The PML::RARA fusion is a critical genetic alteration in acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL), a subtype of acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The fusion arises from the translocation t(15;17)(q24.1;q21.2), leading to the formation of the PML::RARA fusion gene. This gene encodes a chimeric protein that blocks myeloid differentiation, resulting in the accumulation of abnormal promyelocytes in the bone marrow. PML::RARA fusion detection is an essential diagnostic criterion for APL and is listed in professional guidelines (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukaemia With FUS::ERG Fusion
assertion_summary: The presence of the t(16;21)(p11;q22) translocation resulting in the FUS::ERG fusion gene is a diagnostic criterion for a subtype of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), particularly in pediatric patients.
assertion_description: The FUS::ERG fusion is the result of a chromosomal translocation involving 16p and 21q, t(16;21)(p11;q22), which fuses the 5' portion of the FUS (FUS RNA Binding Protein) gene in 16p11 with the 3' portion (including the ETS domain) of the ERG (ETS Transcription Factor ERG) gene in 21q22. The fusion is expressed from the derivative chromosome 21. The FUS::ERG fusion is considered a key diagnostic marker for a specific subtype of AML, particularly common in pediatric patients. Professional guidelines (WHO) list FUS::ERG fusion or t(16;21)(p11;q22) as an essential diagnostic criteria for the AML with FUS::ERG subtype of AML with other defined genetic alterations (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: NR4A3 nuclear immunoreactivity, which is driven by a recurrent translocation t(4;9)(q13;q31), is considered a diagnostic criterium for acinic cell carcinoma.
assertion_description: NR4A3 overexpression driven by a recurrent translocation t(4;9)(q13;q31) that juxtaposes active enhancer regions from the SCPP gene cluster to the region upstream of NR4A3 has been identified in acinic cell carcinomas of the salivary gland and sinonasal (civic.eid:12030, civic.eid:12336). NR4A3 positive nuclear immunohistochemical staining is considered a sensitive and specific marker for the t(4;9)(q13;q31) in acinic cell carcinoma (civic.eid:12828, civic.eid:12336, civic.eid:12337, civic.eid:12816). Professional guidelines (WHO) list NR4A3 nuclear immunoreactivity associated with NR4A3 fusions as a diagnostic criterium for acinic cell carcinoma (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: TFCP2 fusion is a diagnostic marker for a subset of spindle cell/sclerosing rhabdomyosarcoma (SC/S-RMS).
assertion_description: The TFCP2-related gene fusions are rare genetic alterations identified in spindle cell and sclerosing rhabdomyosarcoma (SC/S-RMS). These fusions, involving either EWSR1 or FUS, are predominantly observed in bone tumors, especially in the craniofacial skeleton. The TFCP2 fusion gene encodes a chimeric protein that disrupts normal transcriptional regulation. Tumors with TFCP2 fusions show characteristic spindle cell and epithelioid morphology and frequently overexpress ALK, MYOD1, and keratins. Professional guidelines (WHO) recognize TFCP2 fusions as a defining feature of this aggressive rhabdomyosarcoma subtype, aiding in its diagnosis (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

molecular_profile: SMARCB1 LOSS OF NUCLEAR PROTEIN EXPRESSION
assertion_summary: Biallelic SMARCB1 genetic alterations leading to loss of nuclear protein expression, in the context of histologically hypercellular tumour with cribriform strands and ribbons, are considered essential diagnostic criteria for cribriform neuroepithelial tumor (CRINET).
assertion_description: SMARCB1 loss of nuclear expression is an essential molecular alteration in cribriform neuroepithelial tumor (CRINET), a rare non-rhabdoid childhood brain cancer with a distinct histological appearance including cribriform strains and ribbons. Loss of SMARCB1 expression is caused by biallelic inactivation through a combination of mechanisms including deletions of chromosome 22q, SMARCB1 sequence mutations or single-gene deletions of either germline or somatic origin, and loss of heterozygosity. Loss of nuclear SMARCB1 is an essential diagnostic criterion for this newly recognized provisional disease entity in the professional guideline (WHO classification of tumor series, 5th ed. vol. 6; 2021). It should be noted that CRINET has an overlapping methylation profile with atypical teratoid / rhabdoid tumor, AT/RT-TYR subtype, and similarly demonstrates tyrosinase immunopositivity. Therefore, its distinction from AT/RT-TYR has not been fully delineated in the current WHO Classification (5th ed. vol. 6; 2021).

assertion_summary: FOXP1::ABL1 is an oncogenic fusion associated with B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma, BCR::ABL1 like
assertion_description: The FOXP1::ABL1 fusion is composed of part of the FOXP1 (Forkhead box P1) gene at the 5′ end (N-terminus of the fusion protein) and part of the ABL1 (ABL proto-oncogene 1, non-receptor tyrosine kinase) gene at the 3′ end (C-terminus of the fusion protein) (FG1, civic.EID:7253). ABL1 is considered the key partner that defines the functional and oncogenic effects of the fusion protein. ABL1 is a cytoplasmic tyrosine kinase, and constitutive activation caused by the fusion results in a kinase-activated (BCR::ABL1-like) expression signature. The published breakpoint joins exon 19 of FOXP1 to exon 4 of ABL1 (FOXP1::ABL1), resulting in an in-frame transcript that retains the entire ABL1 kinase domain (FG2, FG3, civic.EID:7253). The fusion arises from a reciprocal translocation, t(3;9)(p12;q34), and has been identified by RT-PCR, Sanger sequencing, and next-generation sequencing. FOXP1 is critical for the transcriptional regulatory network of B-cell lymphopoiesis and may also function as a tumor suppressor gene. Absence or deficiency of FOXP1 during early B-cell development may impair the transition from the pro-B-cell stage to the pre-B-cell stage. The FOXP1::ABL1 fusion protein results in constitutive tyrosine kinase activation and may further disrupt the critical cellular functions of these two genes. The FOXP1::ABL1 fusion has been documented in at least four pediatric and young adult patients with B-lymphoblastic leukemia (CA1, civic.EID:7253, civic.EID:7651, civic.EID:11615), some of whom were subsequently diagnosed with the BCR::ABL1-like (Ph-like) subtype (GS, civic.EID:7651, civic.EID:11615). Two patients had tyrosine kinase inhibitors (dasatinib) added to their chemotherapy regimens, and one achieved MRD-negative bone marrow status at the end of consolidation (CV, civic.EID:7292). Collectively, FG1 + FG2 + FG3 + CA1 + GS + CV support an Oncogenic classification for FOXP1::ABL1 under the ClinGen BCR::ABL1-like SC-VCEP fusion oncogenicity rules.

assertion_summary: ETV6::RUNX1 fusions are considered essential diagnostic criteria for B-lymphoblastic Leukemia/lymphoma With ETV6::RUNX1 fusion.
assertion_description: ETV6::RUNX1 fusion resulting from a recurrent cytogenetic cryptic t(12;21)(p13;q22) translocation has been identified in a subset of pediatric B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL). This fusion juxtaposes ETV6 on chromosome 12 with RUNX1 on chromosome 21, producing a chimeric transcription factor that disrupts normal hematopoietic differentiation. Professional guidelines (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 9) list ETV6::RUNX1 as an essential diagnostic criterion for B-ALL with ETV6::RUNX1 fusion.

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With NUP98 Rearrangement
assertion_summary: NUP98 rearrangements or fusions are considered essential diagnostic criteria for acute myeloid leukemia with NUP98 rearrangement.
assertion_description: NUP98 fusions are detected in a subset of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients. NUP98 fusions in AML involve the N-terminal portion of NUP98 and the C-terminal portion of multiple different fusion partners. NSD1 is the most common fusion partner with NUP98::NSD1 frequently associated with FLT3 ITD and predominately detected in pediatric AML patients. The NUP98::KDM5A fusion can be detected in the acute megakaryoblastic leukemia (AMKL), which is a rare subtype of AML. Professional guidelines (WHO) list detection of NUP98 rearrangement or a specific NUP98 fusion product as an essential diagnostic criteria for acute myeloid leukemia with NUP98 rearrangement (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: NUP214::ABL1 is an oncogenic fusion associated with BCR::ABL1 like B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma.
assertion_description: The NUP214::ABL1 fusion is a recurrently observed fusion with published breakpoints that include exons 32, 33, or 34 of NUP214 joined to exon 3 of ABL1 (NUP214::ABL1), resulting in a transcript that is in frame and contains the entire ABL1 kinase domain (FG1, FG2, FG3). The fusion results from a reciprocal translocation t(9;9)(q34;q34), an intrachromosomal duplication, or episomal NUP214::ABL1 amplification and has been identified by RT-PCR, Sanger sequencing, and NGS. The NUP214::ABL1 fusion has been documented in more than three pediatric/young adult patients with B-lymphoblastic leukemia (CA1), some of whom were further diagnosed with BCR::ABL1 (Ph)-like subtype by expression profiling (GS). An in vitro functional activity study using the patients’ leukemic samples showed downstream activation of ABL1 with increased phosphorylation of the ABL1 target CRKL, and the in vivo study on mice harboring the NUP214::ABL1 fusion when treated with dasatinib significantly reduced the leukemic burden (FS). Collectively, FG1+FG2+FG3+CA1+FS+GS, results in an oncogenic classification for NUP214::ABL1 via the ClinGen Ph-like SC-VCEP fusion oncogenicity rules.

assertion_summary: IG::MYC rearrangements or fusions are considered essential diagnostic criteria for B-lymphoblastic leukemia with MYC rearrangement, a subcategory of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with other defined genetic alterations in WHO classification.
assertion_description: IG::MYC fusions are detected in a subset of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL/LBL) cases. These fusions result from aberrant V(D)J recombination, most commonly involving IGH::MYC, and are associated with an immature B-cell phenotype. NRAS/KRAS mutations are frequently observed, while typical Burkitt lymphoma mutations are absent. The IGH::MYC fusion can co-occur with IGH::BCL2 in rare cases. Pediatric overlap cases may show mixed features of Burkitt-like morphology with precursor immunophenotype and KRAS/FBXO11 mutations. Professional guidelines (WHO) list IG::MYC rearrangement as an essential diagnostic criteria for B-lymphoblastic leukemia with MYC rearrangement, classified under B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with other specified genetic abnormalities in WHO classification of tumors series (5th ed.; vol. 11).

phenotypes: Late onset,Childhood onset,Late young adult onset,Middle age onset,Juvenile onset,Intermediate young adult onset
assertion_summary: EPOR rearrangements are diagnostic for the BCR::ABL1-like subtype of B-lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma
assertion_description: The EPOR gene encodes the erythropoietin receptor, a member of the cytokine receptor family. EPOR rearrangements, including insertion of EPOR distal to the enhancer of either IGH or IGK or truncation of the cytoplasmic tail of EPOR result in abnormal EPOR activation and increased downstream JAK/STAT asignaling. These EPOR rearrangements are included in the set of genetic alterations sufficient for diagnosis of B-lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma with BCR::ABL1-like features, an entity associated with a poor treatment response and high relapse rate which accounts for ~5-9% of B-ALL cases. JAK/STAT pathway activation offers Ruxolitinib (JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor) as a treatment option (AALL1521/INCB18424-269) COG AALL1521 phase II clinical trial).

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With MECOM Rearrangement
assertion_summary: Approximately 4% of AML patients show MECOM rearrangements which serve as a biomarker for this subtype of AML that shows aggressive progression and poor prognosis and is distinctly defined under the 5th WHO Classification for hematologic malignancies.
assertion_description: AML with inv(3)/t(3;3)(q21q26) is a distinct WHO-recognized entity. It is characterized by its aggressive course and poor prognosis. In this subtype of AML, translocation of GATA2 enhancer (located at 3q21) to MECOM (located at 3q26) leads to overexpression of the MECOM isoform EVI1 and monoallelic expression of GATA2, and lack of expression of full-length transcript MDS-EVI1. Besides the classical inv(3)/t(3;3)(q21q26) rearrangement, a number of atypical 3q26/MECOM rearrangements with poor treatment response in AML have been reported in literature. Since atypical 3q26 AMLs are difficult to diagnose given their cytogenetic complexity of and heterogeneity, the importance of routine molecular diagnosis to identify this subgroup of AML cases is highlighted. Use of MECOM FISH to identify 3q26/ MECOM rearrangements routinely for AML diagnostics, and quantitative EVI1 and MDS-EVI1 mRNA expression analysis are important to evaluate role of enhancer hijacking in EVI1 deregulation. It is proposed that both atypical 3q26/MECOM and inv(3)/t(3;3)(q21q26) be classified together as a single entity of 3q26 rearranged AMLs.

assertion_summary: Alteration of chromosome 19 miRNA cluster (C19MC) is a primary diagnostic criterion for embryonal tumors with multilayered rosettes (ETMRs).
assertion_description: The embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes (ETMR) is a rare, aggressive central nervous system (CNS) tumor that affects children younger than four years old. Approximately 90% of ETMRs harbor alterations in the miRNA cluster on chromosome 19q13.4 (C19MC), which is the largest miRNA cluster in the human genome. These alterations include focal amplification and gene fusions involving partner genes such as TTYH1 and, more rarely, MYO9B and MIRLET7BHG, leading to the upregulation of C19MC and contributing to ETMR tumorigenesis. Professional guidelines recognize C19MC alterations as essential for diagnosing C19MC-altered ETMR (WHO classification of tumor series, 5th edu.; vol 6).

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With MLL Rearrangement
assertion_summary: KMT2A rearrangements are considered essential diagnostic criteria for acute myeloid leukemia with KMT2A rearrangement.
assertion_description: KMT2A rearrangements are detected in a subset of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients. KMT2A fusions in AML typically involve the N-terminal portion of KMT2A and the C-terminal portion of multiple different fusion partners. MLLT3 is the most common fusion partner. Professional guidelines (WHO) list KMT2A rearrangement as an essential diagnostic criteria and identification of the KMT2A fusion partner as a desirable diagnostic criterion for AML with KMT2A rearrangement (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: COL1A1-PDGFB fusion is a diagnostic criterion for dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP).
assertion_description: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP) and its variants, including the pigmented Bednar tumor, are defined by the presence of a COL1A1::PDGFB fusion, resulting from the translocation t(17;22)(q22;q13). This fusion consistently involves exon 2 of PDGFB and a variable breakpoint within exons 6-49 of COL1A1. Professional guidelines (WHO) list the detection of the COL1A1::PDGFB fusion as a diagnostic criterion for DFSP (WHO Classification of Tumours of Soft Tissue and Bone, 5th Edition).

assertion_summary: The FLT3 p.V16L missense variant is classified as likely benign for FLT3-associated myeloid neoplasm (SBS1).
assertion_description: The NM_004119.3(FLT3):c.46G>C missense variant (rs62636526) results in a substitution of valine with leucine at codon 16 (p.Val16Leu). The variant is present in gnomAD v4.1 at an overall MAF of 0.04116% based on 649 heterozygotes and 4 homozygotes (highest MAF in African/African American population: 0.8122%, 598+8/74616 alleles); the total filtering allele frequency in the African/African American population is 0.7586%. The variant was introduced into a normal cell line (VAF=4.1%) that was used to test the performance of a sequencing assay (PMID: 24142049, Supplementary Table 4C). The germline variant was identified in at least 1/690 patients with myeloid malignancy but not assessed amongst 38821 HRC controls (PMID: 31911633, Supplementary Table 5). The germline variant has also been described in other individuals either without cancer or at least without hematologic malignancy (PMID: 24728327, PMID: 31118516, PMID: 38542393). The missense predictor ClinPred (0.042) does not support a deleterious effect. The splicing algorithm SpliceAI does not show any significant score changes. In summary, this variant has an oncogenic classification of likely benign based on the following ClinGen/CGC/VICC criteria (PMID: 35101336) applied, as specified by the ClinGen FLT3 SC-VCEP (Version 1): SBS1.

assertion_summary: The FLT3 p.G73E missense variant is classified as a VUS for FLT3-associated myeloid neoplasm (OP4).
assertion_description: The NM_004119.3(FLT3):c.218G>A missense variant results in a substitution of glycine with glutamic acid at codon 73 (p.Gly73Glu). The variant is absent from gnomAD v4.1 (>20x coverage). The variant of unclear origin was reported in a patient with CML (PMID: 32943879, Supplementary Table 2). It was also identified in various solid tumors (PMID: 22588877/PMID: 23550210/PMID: 37668528; PMID: 26950094; PMID: 36219477; PMID: 39659251; PMID: 25303977). The missense predictor ClinPred (0.017) does not support a deleterious effect. The splicing algorithm SpliceAI does not show any significant score changes. In summary, this variant has an oncogenic classification of VUS based on the following ClinGen/CGC/VICC criteria (PMID: 35101336) applied, as specified by the ClinGen FLT3 SC-VCEP (Version 1): OP4.

assertion_summary: The FLT3 p.Q338E missense variant is classified as a VUS for FLT3-associated AML (OP4).
assertion_description: The NM_004119.3(FLT3):c.1012C>G missense variant results in a substitution of glutamine with glutamic acid at codon 338 (p.Gln338Glu). The variant is absent from gnomAD v4.1 (>20x coverage). The variant has not been reported in hematologic malignancy, but it was identified in various solid tumors (PMID: 22588877/PMID: 23550210/PMID: 37668528). The missense predictor ClinPred (0.258) does not support a deleterious effect. The splicing algorithm SpliceAI does not show any significant score changes. In summary, this variant has an oncogenic classification of VUS based on the following ClinGen/CGC/VICC criteria (PMID: 35101336) applied, as specified by the ClinGen FLT3 SC-VCEP (Version 1): OP4.

assertion_summary: The t(12;16)(q13;p11) rearrangement generating FUS::DDIT3 fusion transcripts is a molecular diagnostic criterion for myxoid liposarcoma (MLS).
assertion_description: The myxoid liposarcoma (MLS, also known as MLPS) and its hypercellular round cell subtype are rare adipocyte-derived soft tissue sarcoma, accounting for 20-30% of liposarcoma. While this disease entity is more common in adults, it can affect individuals of any age and is the most prevalent liposarcoma subtype among children and adolescents. The molecular hallmark of this disease involves DDIT3 (CHOP, GADD153) translocations, with the t(12;16)(q13;p11)-driven FUS::DDIT3 fusions being more prevalent. The rare t(12;22)(q13;q12) translocation producing EWSR1::DDIT3 is found in 3% of cases. These adipocyte-specific chromosomal rearrangements contribute to MLS tumorigenesis by blocking normal adipocyte differentiation. Professional guidelines recognize DDIT3 rearrangement (FUS::DDIT3 or EWSR1::DDIT3 fusions) as desirable diagnostic criterion for MLS (WHO classification of tumor series, 5th ed.; vol 6; NCCN v1.2025).

assertion_summary: AR-V7 is associated with resistance to Abiraterone and Enzalutamide in patients with metastatic prostate cancer.
assertion_description: AR-V7 is an alternatively spliced version of the androgen receptor that was identified in LNCaP derivative cell lines which gained the ability to grow in an androgen depleted medium. The AR-V7 isoform consists of the first three exons of AR, along with a cryptic exon in place of exons 4 through 9. This isoform retains the N terminal transactivation domain, and the DNA binding domain of AR, but loses the hinge region and ligand binding domain, which suggests that this isoform has the capacity to transactivate downstream targets even in the absence of ligand. AR-V7 was expressed in androgen independent cell lines, and more frequently occurs in the setting of AR gene amplification. Expression of AR-V7 in androgen dependent cells induced androgen independence, and knockdown of AR-V7 in androgen independent cells inhibited androgen independent growth. AR-V7 shows increased capacity to translocate to the nucleus in an androgen independent manner. AR-V7 isoforms are found in castration-resistant prostate cancer, salivary duct carcinoma and breast carcinoma. AR-V7 is associated with resistance to Abiraterone and Enzalutamide in patients with metastatic prostate cancer.

disease: B-lymphoblastic Leukaemia/lymphoma With Other Defined Genetic Alterations
assertion_summary: ZNF384 rearrangements are considered essential diagnostic criteria for B-ALL with other defined genetic alterations /B-ALL with ZNF384 rearrangements.
assertion_description: ZNF384 rearrangements are detected in a subset of B-lymphoblastic leukemia patients. ZNF384 fusions typically involve the N-terminal portion of partner genes fused to ZNF384's C-terminus, with TCF3 and EP300 being the most frequent partner genes. These fusions define a distinct subgroup characterized by weak CD10 and aberrant CD13/CD33 expression. Professional guidelines (WHO) list ZNF384 rearrangements as an essential diagnostic criterion for the subtype of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with ZNF384 rearrangement, within the category of B-ALL with other defined genetic alterations (WHO Classification of Tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: KMT2A rearrangements are considered essential diagnostic criteria for B lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with KMT2A rearrangement.
assertion_description: KMT2A rearrangements are detected in a subset of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL) patients, especially infants. KMT2A fusions typically involve the N-terminal portion of KMT2A and the C-terminal portion of various fusion partners, with AFF1, MLLT1, and MLLT3 being most common. Professional guidelines (WHO and ICC) list KMT2A rearrangement as an essential diagnostic criterion for B-ALL with KMT2A rearrangement (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: The ZEB2::PDGFRB is likely oncogenic for Ph-Like B-ALL
assertion_description: The ZEB2::PDGFRB has appeared in 2 individuals with Ph-like B-ALL (CA2). In one patient it appears together with a different fusion PAX5::BZW1. PDGFRB appears as the 3' partner (FG1, civic.eid:12482). In one patient, the reported breaekpoint was in exon 9 of PDGFRB, ahead of the kinase domain (FG2, civic.eid:12480), and both fusion partners were reported in frame (FG3, civic.eid:12482). Functional evidence is given in a meeting abstract with minimal detail (FS, civic.eid:12481).

assertion_summary: ETV6::ABL2 is of uncertain significance in hematological cancer
assertion_description: ETV6::ABL2 has been found in hematological cancers, and at least 4 cases are reported in the literature, 2 AML, one B-ALL and one T_ALL. Multiple reports show ETV6 exons 1 to 5 fused to either base pair 362 or 425 of ABL2 (FG1), in frame (FG3). Both fusion isoforms contain the ETV6 HLH domain as well as the SH3, SH2, and tyrosine kinase domains from ABL2 (FG2). One report describes a patient derived cell line with ETV6::ABL2 and also has R399H mutation on the intact ETV6 allele, that is growth factor independent, but this is not strong enough to meet functional criteria for the Ph-Like SC-VCEP oncogenicity classification. One patient with the fusion was reported to not respond to standard chemotherapy. None of the patients are explicitly described as Ph-Like ALL. Together these findings support criteria FG1 + FG2 + FG3, indicating the fusion is of uncertain significance.

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With Mutated NPM1
assertion_summary: NPM1 exon 11 mutation, resulting in disruption of the nucleolar localization signal and creation of a cytoplasmic localization signal, is a diagnostic criterion for a subtype of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with mutated NPM1.
assertion_description: NPM1 mutations are detected in a large subset of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients, particularly those with normal cytogenetics. These mutations typically consist of small insertions in the terminal coding exon of NPM1 (NM_002520.7 exon 11; historically refferd to as exon 12), resulting in elongation of the protein, disruption of the C-terminal nucleolar localization signal, and aberrant cytoplasmic localization (NPMc+). Professional guideline (WHO) recognize AML with mutated NPM1 as a distinct diagnostic entity, with the presence of an NPM1 mutation listed as an essential diagnostic criterion and FLT3 mutation status as a key prognostic determinant (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

disease: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With Inv(16)(p13.1q22) Or T(16;16)(p13.1;q22)
assertion_summary: CBFB::MYH11 is considered an essential diagnostic criterion for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with CBFB::MYH11.
assertion_description: CBFB::MYH11 is detected in a distinct subset of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients, historically classified as AML with inv(16)(p13q22) or t(16;16)(p13;q22). This rearrangement results in fusion of the CBFB gene on chromosome 16q22 with MYH11 on chromosome 16p13, producing the CBFB::MYH11 fusion transcript. Professional guidelines (WHO) recognize AML with CBFB::MYH11 as a distinct diagnostic entity, with the presence of the CBFB::MYH11 fusion serving as an essential diagnostic criterion (WHO classification of tumors' series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: SRF rearrangement is a diagnostic criterion for myofibroma and myopericytoma.
assertion_description: Myofibromas and myopericytomas harboring SRF gene fusions are a rare and diagnostically challenging entity that occurs mostly in children and young adults. SRF fusions typically involve the N-terminal portion of SRF and the C-terminal portion of various fusion partners, with RELA being the most common. Professional guidelines (WHO) list detection of SRF rearrangement as a diagnostic criterion for cellular cases of myofibroma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: BCR::ABL1 fusion is a diagnostic criterion for Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML).
assertion_description: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML) is a well-defined myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by the t(9;22)(q34;q11.2) forming the BCR::ABL1 fusion. The fusion is expressed from the derivative chromosome 22, known also as Philadelphia (Ph) chromosome. This fusion results in a constitutively active BCR::ABL1 tyrosine kinase, representing the initiating and defining molecular event in CML pathogenesis. Professional guidelines (WHO) list detection of BCR::ABL1 fusion as a diagnostic criterion for CML (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: IGH::CRLF2 rearrangement resulting in CRLF2 overexpression, often accompanied by JAK-STAT pathway mutations, is a diagnostic criterion for B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL), BCR::ABL1 (Ph)-like subtype.
assertion_description: B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL), BCR::ABL1 (Ph)-like subtype, is a high-risk leukemia occurring predominantly in adolescents and young adults (AYA). It is characterized by activation of cytokine receptor-like factor 2 (CRLF2) through either IGH::CRLF2 or P2RY8::CRLF2 gene fusions, resulting in CRLF2 overexpression. These rearrangements often co-occur with activating mutations in the JAK-STAT signaling pathway, most commonly JAK2. Professional guidelines (WHO) list detection of CRLF2 gene rearrangements or overexpression, often accompanied by JAK-STAT pathway alterations, as diagnostic criterion for B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL), BCR::ABL1 (Ph)-like (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: PAX3::FOXO1 fusion is a diagnostic criterion for alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma.
assertion_description: Alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma (ARMS) is an aggressive soft tissue malignancy of children and adolescents that is defined by specific gene fusions, most commonly the PAX3::FOXO1. This fusion, resulting from a t(2;13)(q35;q14) translocation, is a primary molecular driver and a highly specific diagnostic marker for this tumor. Its detection is critical for distinguishing ARMS from histologic mimics, particularly the fusion-negative embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma. Professional guidelines (WHO) list the PAX3::FOXO1 fusion as a diagnostic criterion for alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma (WHO Classification of Tumours of Soft Tissue and Bone, 5th Edition).

disease: Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion
assertion_summary: The t(20;22)(q13.2;q12.2) translocation generating the EWSR1::NFATC2 fusion transcript is a diagnostic criterion for a subset of (small) round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions.
assertion_description: The round cell sarcoma (RCS) with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions is a rare undifferentiated sarcoma. It is characterized by gene fusion of a FET family gene EWSR1 or FUS joining with a downstream non-ETS family transcription factor such as NFATC2. The EWSR1::NFATC2 RCSs have a predilection for bones (mainly involved in the metaphysis or diaphysis of long bones) over soft tissue (4:1) with a strong male predominance (5:1). Together with FUS::NFATC2 RCSs, these tumors affect adolescents and adults with a median age of 32.3 years at presentation. The EWSR1::NFATC2 fusion typically results from an unbalanced translocation t(20;22)(q13;q12) and is amplified, which can be detected by EWSR1 break-apart FISH probes. Several fusion variants have been identified and may occur between exons 6-10 of EWSR1 and exons 3-4 of NFATC2. The resulting EWSR1::NFATC2 chimeric protein shows an uncontrolled nuclear localization and activation of NFATC2 to rewire the transcriptome and epigenome of the as yet identified cells of origin. Of significance, professional guidelines recognize ETMR1::NFATC2 gene fusions a diagnostic criterion for a subset of round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions (WHO classification of tumor series, 5th edu.; vol 6).

assertion_summary: PAX7::FOXO1 fusion is a diagnostic criterion for alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma.
assertion_description: PAX7::FOXO1 fusion–positive alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma represents a molecularly defined and diagnostically distinct subtype that predominantly affects children and young adults. The fusion event, which joins the DNA-binding domain of PAX7 with the transactivation domain of FOXO1, serves as the principal oncogenic driver. Professional guidelines (WHO) list the detection of PAX7::FOXO1 fusion as a diagnostic criterion for alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma (WHO Classification of Tumours, 5th Edition; Soft Tissue and Bone Tumours).

assertion_summary: MYOD1 p.L122R mutation is a diagnostic criterion for spindle cell/sclerosing rhabdomyosarcoma.
assertion_description: Spindle cell and sclerosing rhabdomyosarcomas harboring MYOD1 p.L122R mutations are a distinct and often aggressive entity that occurs across pediatric and adult age groups. The MYOD1 p.L122R mutation is a recurrent hotspot mutation that serves as a primary oncogenic driver. In a study of 49 rhabdomyosarcoma cases, all 10 cases that were positive for L122R were either spindle cell or sclerosing subtypes of RMS (civic.EID:8193), and L122R is found at high frequencies in these subtypes (civic.EID:11582, civic.EID:11585). Professional guidelines (WHO) list the detection of MYOD1 mutation as a diagnostic criterion for spindle cell/sclerosing rhabdomyosarcoma (WHO Classification of Tumors, 5th Edition; Soft Tissue and Bone Tumors).

assertion_summary: SS18::SSX1 fusion is a diagnostic criterion for synovial sarcoma.
assertion_description: Synovial sarcomas harboring SS18::SSX1 gene fusions are a molecularly defined and diagnostically distinct entity that occurs across a wide age range and in various anatomical sites. The SS18::SSX1 fusion, resulting from the characteristic t(X;18) translocation, juxtaposes the N-terminal portion of SS18 with the C-terminal portion of SSX1 and is the most common fusion variant. Professional guidelines (WHO) list the detection of SS18::SSX1 fusion as a diagnostic criterion for synovial sarcoma (WHO Classification of Tumors, 5th Edition; Soft Tissue and Bone Tumors).

assertion_summary: AML patients with FLT3 D835Y are sensitive to gilteritinib
assertion_description: Gilteritinib is approved for use in relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia with D835 tyrosine kinase domain (TKD) mutations, including D835Y. In a Phase 3 trial, patients with FLT3 TKD mutations showed improved overall survival when treated with gilteritinib over chemotherapy (civic.EID:7728, civic.EID:12622). Ba/F3 cells transformed with FLT3 D835Y respond to gilteritinib treatment (civic.EID:8106), and patient derived AML cells with D835Y have responded to to drug (civic.EID:8108). An AML patient with D835Y mutation, and no other FLT3 mutations, responded with remission to gilteritinb treatment (civic.EID:12620).

assertion_summary: ZMIZ1::ABL1 is oncogenic in B-ALL
assertion_description: The ZMIZ1::ABL1 fusion has appeared in at least 17 cases of B-ALL not tested for Ph-Like B-ALL signature (civic.eid:9151, civic.eid:12638), and in at least 9 cases confirmed for Ph-Like B-ALL signature, and 1 case of B-ALL that did not show the Ph-Like signature (CA1, GS, civic.eid:12635, civic.eid:12615, civic.eid:11619, civic.eid:9077, civic.eid:9152). ABL1 appears as the 3 prime partner, in frame, and reported fusions are between ZMIZ1 exon 18 and ABL1 exon 2, containing the ABL1 tyrosine kinase domain (FG1, FG2, FG3). Functional evidence for oncogenicity is reported in Ba/F3 cells (FS, civic.eid:11117). Response to dasatinib and chemotherapy was reported in an 11 year old patient with the fusion (CV, civic.eid:11119). Ph-Like Oncogenicity codes met: FG1, FG2, FG3, CA1, GS, FS, CV, indicating an oncogenic fusion.

disease: Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion
assertion_summary: The t(16;20)(p11.2;q13.2) translocation generating the FUS::NFATC2 fusion transcript is a diagnostic criterion for a subset of (small) round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions.
assertion_description: The round cell sarcoma (RCS) with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions is a rare undifferentiated sarcoma. It is characterized by gene fusion of a FET (FUS/EWS/TAF15, previously TET [FUS (TLS)/EWS/TAF15]) family gene EWSR1 or FUS joining with a downstream non-ETS family transcription factor such as NFATC2. The FUS-NFATC2 RCSs have been found exclusively in the long bones. Together with EWSR1-NFATC2 RCSs, these tumors have a strong male predominance (M:F, 5:1) and affect adolescents and adults with a median age of 32.3 years (aged 12-67 years) at presentation. The FUS::NFATC2 fusion results from the translocation t(16;20)(p11.2;q13.2) and has not shown amplification as EWSR1::NFATC2. Of significance, professional guidelines recognize FUS::NFATC2 gene fusions as a diagnostic criterion for a subset of round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions (WHO classification of tumor series, 5th ed.).

assertion_summary: TFE3 rearrangement is a diagnostic criterion for PEComas.
assertion_description: TFE3-rearranged perivascular epithelioid cell tumors (PEComas) are a rare and diagnostically challenging subset of PEComas that occur across a wide age range and multiple anatomic sites. TFE3 fusions typically involve the TFE3 gene and various partners, most commonly ASPSCR1, SFPQ, or NONO, resulting in strong nuclear TFE3 expression and distinctive epithelioid clear-cell morphology. Professional guidelines (WHO) list detection of TFE3 rearrangement as a diagnostic criterion for cellular cases of PEComas (WHO classification of tumurs series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: Urothelial cancer with FGFR3 N540K shows resistance to erdafitinib.
assertion_description: Two patients with FGFR3-driven urothelial cancer treated with FGFR inhibitors, including erdafitinib, were found to acquire the FGFR3 N540K mutation at disease progression, which was not detected in pretreatment samples (civic.EID:12703, civic.EID:12704). In one case, the mutation emerged following erdafitinib treatment, and in another, it was detected after sequential treatment with erdafitinib and futibatinib (civic.EID:12703, civic.EID:12704). Functional studies using Ba/F3 models showed that expression of FGFR3 N540K in the context of an FGFR3 driver fusion resulted in reduced sensitivity to FGFR inhibitors, including erdafitinib and futibatinib, as indicated by increased IC50 values compared to the driver alone (civic.EID:12706). Biochemical analyses demonstrated that FGFR3 N540K exhibits increased kinase activity, enhanced association with Cdc37/Hsp90 complexes, and reduced thermal stability relative to wild-type FGFR3 (civic.EID:10389).

assertion_summary: RET M918T is sensitive to selpercatinib in medullary thyroid cancer
assertion_description: RET M918T occurs in the kinase domain of RET, and is found in both germline and somatic RET mutations in medullary thyroid cancer (civic.EID:12711). M918T induces transformation of cells which are sensitive to treatment by selpercatinib (civic.EID:11867, civic.EID:11876). M918T is the most prevalent RET mutation found in patients enrolled in medullary thyroid cancer trials (civic.EID:8851, civic.EID:12708), and the only RET mutation reported in cancerhotspots V2. Patients with M918T have improved progression free survival when treated with selpercatinib over physician’s choice of vandetanib or cabozantinib (civic.EID:12598). Selpercatinib is approved for use in medullary thyroid cancer patients with RET mutations including M918T over 2 years of age based on the results of phase 1/2 (civic.EID:12056, civic.EID:12708) and LIBRETTO-531 phase 3 trials (civic.EID:12157).

assertion_summary: RET E632_L633del is sensitive to selpercatinib in medullary thyroid cancer
