assertion_description: RET E632_L633del occurs in the cysteine rich domain of RET, and has been found as a somatic mutation in medullary thyroid cancer. E632_L633del induces transformation of cells which are sensitive to treatment by selpercatinib (civic.EID:12712). The variant has been reported not to be responsive to selpercatinib in a single patient (civic.EID:12714), and to be less sensitive in HEK293 cells than wildtype RET (civic.EID:12715). Other findings have shown response to Selpercatinib in at least 10 patients with E632_L633del (civic.EID:11875, civic.EID:12716) Selpercatinib is approved for use in medullary thyroid cancer patients with RET mutations over 2 years of age based on the results of phase 1/2 (civic.EID:12056) and LIBRETTO-531 phase 3 trials (civic.EID:12157).

assertion_summary: RET M918T is likely oncogenic in medullary thyroid cancer
assertion_description: Published sequencing studies have shown that RET mutations are very common in medullary thryoid carcinoma (MTC) and M918T is the most common specific variant, especially in the MEN2B clinical subtype of familial disease (civic.EID:78) but also in sporadic cases(civic.EID:12800). M918T mutations may predict worse outcomes (civic.EID:74). Biochemical and functional characterization demonstrates that the M918T mutation leads to functional activation of RET relative to wild-type through multiple complementary mechanisms, including increased ATP affinity (>10-fold) and complex stability, reduced conformational rigidity, and the promotion of ligand-independent dimerization and autophosphorylation (civic.EID:12805). Exogenous expression has been shown to induce transformation of Ba/F3 cells (civic.EID:11723), and drive colony formation in NIH3T3 cells (civic.EID:12709, OS2). RET M918T occurs in the region of the tyrosine kinase domain which is associated with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 B (OM1). RET M918T is predicted to be deleterious (CHASMplus score 0.314 > VECS gene-specific cutoff of 0.22, OP1). Eleven instances of the variant occur in cancerhotspots.org (V2): 6 Thyroid, 4 Adrenal Gland, 1 Breast (OP3). The variant is absent in gnomAD database (v4.1.0, OP4). Together these criteria indicate that M918T is likely oncogenic, with a score of 9.

assertion_summary: FGFR1 Amplification is associated with poor prognosis in breast cancer
assertion_description: FGFR1 Amplification is associated with poor clinical outcomes. In a large breast cancer cohort of 503 assessable patients, FGFR1 amplification was observed in 33 cases (6.6%) and was enriched in the more aggressive luminal B subtype, seen in 69.7 percent of amplified versus 32.6 percent in non-amplified tumors. In this study observed outcome differences did not achieve statistical significance, but there was a trend toward poorer distant metastasis-free survival in patients with FGFR1 amplification [HR=2.08; 95% CI 0.98 to 4.39, P=0.05) (civic.eid:12487). A similar association was observed in the H120 and METABRIC study cohorts of ER-positive breast cancer. In H210 FGFR1 amplification was observed in a higher percentage of luminal B (16.3%, N=17/103) vs luminal A (6.6%, N=6/92) cases and conferred a significant hazard ratio for relapse (HR = 1.96, 95% CI 1.031-3/72, P=0.038). In METABRIC (N=635) the percentage of cases with FGFR amplification was higher in luminal B than in luminal A cases (11.1% vs. 5.5%, P=0.001) and the median relapse-free survival was shorter for cases with amplification than for those without (12.2 vs 21.1 years) (civic.eid:12497). In a separate study of 100 metastatic breast cancer patients, FGFR1 amplification was found in 20 percent of the cohort and associated with decreased median overall survival of 32 versus 54 months (log-rank p=0.0018) (civic.eid:12532). A retrospective study of ctDNA samples from the PALOMA-3 trial (N=401) in patients with advanced ER+ breast cancer found that in both univariable and multivariable analyses gain of FGFR1 was associated with poorer progression-free survival in both treatment groups; there was no interaction with treatment randomization (civic.eid:12486).

assertion_summary: MAML2 rearrangement is a diagnostic criterion for salivary Gland Mucoepidermoid Carcinoma.
assertion_description: Salivary gland mucoepidermoid carcinomas (MECs) harboring CRTC1::MAML2 or CRTC3::MAML2 fusions are a distinct molecular subtype, representing a significant proportion of these tumors. These fusions typically involve the N-terminal portion of a CRTC family gene (CRTC1 or CRTC3) and the C-terminal portion of MAML2, with CRTC1::MAML2 being the most common. Professional guidelines (WHO) list MAML2 rearrangements as a diagnostic criterion for the subtype of salivary gland mucoepidermoid carcinoma (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: NCOA2 fusion is a diagnostic criterion for a subset of spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma (SCRMS).
assertion_description: VGLL2- and NCOA2-rearranged infantile spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma is a distinct and prognostically favorable entity that occurs almost exclusively in infants under one year of age. VGLL2 or NCOA2 fusions occur with different partner genes, including TEAD1, SRF, and CITED2. Professional guidelines (WHO) list VGLL2 or NCOA2 rearrangements as a diagnostic criterion for the subtype of SCRMS (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: H3-3A G34W is a diagnostic criterion for bone giant cell tumor.
assertion_description: Giant cell tumor of bone (GCT) is a locally aggressive and rarely metastasizing neoplasm, accounting for approximately 5% of all primary bone tumors. Driver mutations affecting H3F3A at codon p.G34—most commonly p.G34W (also reported as p.G35W)—are highly specific to GCT and are not observed in other bone tumors. These mutations are present in the majority of cases, reported in up to 92% and 96% of GCTs in different studies (civic.EID:6469, civic.EID:12749). H3F3A mutations are restricted to glycine 34 substitutions, with rare variants such as G34L, G34R, and G34M also described. While highly specific, sensitivity may vary depending on the detection method, with lower rates reported using Sanger sequencing (civic.EID:12750). The World Health Organization (WHO) classification of tumours recognizes the detection of H3F3A p.G34W as a diagnostic criterion for GCT (WHO Classification of Tumours, 5th edition, Volume 3: Soft Tissue and Bone Tumours).

assertion_summary: MALAT1::GLI1 fusion is a diagnostic criterium for gastroblastoma.
assertion_description: Gastroblastoma is a rare gastric tumor composed of epithelial and spindle cell components that occurs in both children and adults (civic.EID:12080, civic.EID:12753, civic.EID:12754, civic.EID:12755). Professional guidelines (WHO) list MALAT1::GLI1 fusion as a diagnostic criterium for gastroblastoma (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

disease: Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion
assertion_summary: The cryptic intrachromosomal inversion within chromosome 22q12.2 generating the EWSR1::PATZ1 fusion transcript is a diagnostic criterion for a subset of (small) round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions.
assertion_description: The round cell sarcoma (RCS) with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions is a rare undifferentiated sarcoma. It is characterized by gene fusions involving a FET (FUS/EWS/TAF15, previously TET [FUS (TLS)/EWS/TAF15]) family gene (EWSR1 or FUS) joined with a downstream non-ETS family transcription factor such as PATZ1. The EWSR1::PATZ1 RCSs occur in the deep soft tissue with a predilection for thoracoabdominal regions and affect individuals with ages ranging from 1 to 81 years (mean of 42 years) at presentation. This gene fusion results from a cryptic paracentric inversion within chromosome 22q12.2, enabling co-directional transcription of EWSR1 and PATZ1 with variable breakpoints located within exons 7-9 of EWSR1 and exon 1 of PATZ1. The resulting chimeric protein joins the transcriptional activation domain of EWSR1 and the DNA-binding zinc fingers of PATZ1. Consequently, this rearrangement converts the transcriptional repressor PATZ1 to a transcriptional activator by the removal of its N-terminal transcriptional repressing BTB/POZ domain. Diagnostically, EWSR1::PATZ1 fusion can be identified by sequencing, but this rearrangement is not detectable by conventional karyotyping and is likely missed by FISH. Of significance, professional guidelines recognize EWSR1::PATZ1 gene fusions as a diagnostic criterion for a subset of round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions (WHO classification of tumor series, 5th ed.).

assertion_summary: RET E632_L633del is likely oncogenic in medullary thyroid carcinoma
assertion_description: RET E632_L633del occurs in the cysteine rich domain of RET which is associated with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 A (OM1). The deletion causes an in frame alteration to protein length (OM2). Exogenous expression has been shown to induce transformation of Ba/F3 cells (civic.EID:12713), and drive colony formation in NIH3T3 cells (civic.EID:11873). Increased autophosphorylation and dimer formation were seen in anti-RET immunoprecipitates from NIH3T3 cells expressing E632_L633del or wild type RET (civic.EID:12817, OS2). The variant is absent in the gnomAD database (OP4). The variant was seen in 13 thyroid cancer patients reported in COSMIC as of February 2025 (OP3). Together these criteria indicate that RET E632_L633del is oncogenic, with a score of 10.

assertion_summary: RET P628_L633del has uncertain significance in medullary thyroid carcinoma
assertion_description: RET P628_L633del occurs in the cysteine rich domain of RET which is associated with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 A (OM1). The deletion causes an in frame alteration to protein length (OM2). The variant is absent in gnomAD database (OP4). Together these criteria classify RET P628_L633del as a variant of unknown significance, with a score of 5. Literature reports of P628_L633del were not found, but it is approved for treatment with selpercatinib in medullary thyroid carcinoma (civic.EID:12157)

assertion_summary: RET P628_L633del is approved for selpercatinib in medullary thyroid cancer
assertion_description: RET P628_L633del is a deletion in the cysteine-rich domain of RET. Selpercatinib is approved for the treatment of patients aged ≥2 years with RET mutation–positive medullary thyroid cancer, based on results from phase 1/2 studies (civic.EID:12056) and the phase 3 LIBRETTO-531 trial (civic.EID:12157). However, no published data specifically report the response of RET P628_L633del to selpercatinib in medullary thyroid cancer.

assertion_summary: FOSB fusions are a diagnostic criterion for Pseudomyogenic Hemangioendothelioma.
assertion_description: Pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma (PHE) is a rare endothelial tumor that predominantly affects children and young adults. The genetics of PHE is not fully characterized. However, recent studies have identified SERPINE1::FOSB (civic.eid:11785), WWTR1::FOSB (civic.eid:12752), and ACTB::FOSB (civic.eid:12779) fusions that support the diagnosis of PHE. The World Health Organization (WHO) classification of tumours recognizes the detection of FOSB fusions as a diagnostic criterion for PHE (WHO Classification of Tumours, 5th edition, Volume 3: Soft Tissue and Bone Tumours).

assertion_summary: TYK2 rearrangements are considered diagnostic criterion for B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with BCR::ABL1-like features.
assertion_description: TYK2 gene rearrangements are a rare, recurrent, and diagnostic finding in B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma subtype with BCR::ABL1-like features. These fusions juxtapose a partner gene's (commonly MYB) N-terminus with the C-terminal tyrosine kinase domain of TYK2, leading to its constitutive, oncogenic activation. Professional guidelines (WHO) list TYK2 rearrangements as a diagnostic criterion for B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with BCR::ABL1-like features (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: LYN rearrangements are considered diagnostic criteria for B-lymphoblastic Leukemia/lymphoma With BCR::ABL1-like Features.
assertion_description: LYN gene rearrangements are a rare, recurrent, and diagnostic finding in the B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma subtype with BCR::ABL1-like features. These fusions juxtapose a partner gene's (commonly NCOR1) N-terminus with the C-terminal tyrosine kinase domain of LYN, leading to its constitutive, oncogenic activation (civic.eid:12801, civic.eid:12802, civic.eid:12809). Professional guidelines (WHO) list rearrangements involving kinase genes—including LYN— as a diagnostic criterion for B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with BCR::ABL1-like features (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: EZH2 Y646N is likely oncogenic in follicular lymphoma
assertion_description: EZH2 Y646N (frequently reported as Y641N in the literature) is a recurrent somatic variant in follicular lymphoma (civic.EID:433, civic.EID11111). Functional studies demonstrate that this variant alters EZH2 enzymatic specificity, showing increased H3K27 trimethylation, variably increased/decreased activity against monomethylated, and decreased/unchanged activity against unmethylated substrates compared to wild-type, for a net gain-of-function effect (civic.EID:EID9412, civic.EID:9518, civic.EID:9520, EID11011, OS2). Additionally, inhibition of EZH2 in Y646N-mutated lymphoma cell lines results in reduced proliferation, cell cycle arrest, and apoptosis, supporting an oncogenic role in driving lymphomagenesis (civic.EID:11013, OS2). The Y646N variant is located in the catalytic SET domain (OM1), is predicted to be a driver mutation (CHASMplus score 0.297-0.317 > VECS gene-specific cutoff of 0.28, OP1), is observed in cancerhotspots.org (V2): 7 Lymph, 5 Skin, 1 Other (OP3), and is absent from population databases (gnomAD database v4.1.0, OP4). Together these criteria indicate that Y646N is likely oncogenic, with a score of 9.

assertion_summary: FLT3 D835Y has an oncogenicity classification of Oncogenic based on the following FLT3 SC-VCEP-specified codes of the ClinGen/CGC/VICC criteria: OS2+OS3+OP1+OP4.
assertion_description: FLT3 c.2503G>T p.(Asp835Tyr) has demonstrated the ability to induce ligand-independent cell proliferation in 32D cells and Ba/F3 cells, leading to constitutive FLT3 activation and phosphorylation of downstream pathway molecules (OS2). This variant is located in COSMIC, cBioPortal and published peer-reviewed literature with variants at the same residue in at least 15 hematologic malignancy samples, and the same amino acid change in at least 5 myeloid malignancy samples with at least 3 samples having somatic status confirmed (OS3). The missense predictor ClinPred supports an oncogenic effect with a score of 1.0 (OP1). This variant is absent from gnomAD v4.1.0 and is in a region with > 20x coverage (OP4).

assertion_summary: EWSR1::TFCP2 gene fusion is a diagnostic criterion for intraosseous spindle cell/sclerosing rhabdomyosarcoma (SCSRMS).
assertion_description: Spindle cell/sclerosing rhabdomyosarcoma (SCSRMS) is a rare type of rhabdomyosarcoma characterized by fascicular spindle cell and/or sclerosing morphology. Three subtypes are recognized: congenital/infantile SCSRMS, which typically affects patients under 12 years and is associated with VGLL2, NCOA2, or CITED2 gene fusions; MYOD1-mutant SCSRMS, which is more aggressive and shows a decreased male-to-female ratio; and intraosseous SCSRMS, defined by EWSR1 or FUS fused to TFCP2, which primarily arises in bone in adolescents and young adults (civic.eid:12825, civic.eid:12826, civic.eid:12827). The intraosseous subtype often displays variable spindle and epithelioid morphology and may show cytokeratin or ALK positivity in a subset of tumors. Clinically, intraosseous SCSRMS typically presents as a rapidly growing, painless mass with aggressive behavior and frequent metastases. Detection of the EWSR1::TFCP2 gene fusion by FISH or targeted RNA sequencing serves as a key molecular diagnostic criterion for this subtype (civic.eid:12825, civic.eid:12826, civic.eid:12827). Professional guidelines list these gene rearrangements and fusions as a diagnostic criterion for intraosseous SCSRMS (WHO classification of tumor series, 5th ed. volume 3).

assertion_summary: EWSR1::ATF1 in-frame gene fusion is a diagnostic criterion for clear cell sarcoma (CCS)
assertion_description: Clear cell sarcoma (CCS) is a malignant mesenchymal tumor of the deep soft tissue found typically in the lower extremities of young adults (civic.eid:12829). Cytogenetic studies have shown that CCS often has a recurrent chromosomal translocation: t(12;22)(q13;q12) (civic.eid:12829, civic.eid:12830, civic.eid:8265). Further, reverse transcriptase (RT)-PCR performed on RNA from fresh, frozen, or FFPE tumor tissue confirms the presence of an in-frame gene fusion between Exon 8 of EWSR1 and codon 65 of ATF1 (civic.eid:12830). This RT-PCR assay can be used as a molecular diagnostic test for CCS. The World Health Organization (WHO) classification of tumors recognizes the detection of EWSR1::ATF1 as a diagnostic criterion for CCS (WHO Classification of Tumors, 5th edition, Volume 3: Soft Tissue and Bone Tumors).

assertion_summary: This variant p.Tyr572Cys is classified as oncogenic based on the FLT3 SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.
assertion_description: The FLT3 (NM_004119.3) variant, p.Tyr572Cys, resulting from c.1715A>G, occurs within the juxtamembrane domain (OM1). The variant has been reported at a residue with at least 15 hematologic malignancy samples, and p.Tyr572Cys has been reported in at least 5 myeloid malignancy samples with at least 3 samples having somatic status confirmed (OS3; civic.eid:13041, civic.eid:13040, cBioPortalv7.0.0, COSMICv104). The c.1715A>G variant is observed at groupmax filtering allele frequency of 0.002977% in the East Asian population (OP4) in the Genome Aggregation Database (v4.1) indicating it is not a common polymorphism. Computational analyses predict that the p.Tyr572Cys variant is deleterious (ClinPred), and neither impacts a nearby canonical splice site nor creates a cryptic splice site (SpliceAI) (OP1). Functional analysis with p.Tyr572Cys variant in Ba/F3 cell lines shows ligand-independent FLT3 receptor constitutive activation, activation of intracellular signaling, and cellular proliferation (OS2; civic.eid:12785, civic.eid:12791, civic.eid:12792, civic.eid:12795). This variant p.Tyr572Cys has a cumulative score of 12 and is classified as oncogenic based on the FLT3 SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.

assertion_summary: MET Splice Site (c.3028+1G>T) is likely oncogenic in NSCLC
assertion_description: MET c.3028+1G>T is a somatic variant in NSCLC. MET c.3028+1G>T has been shown to lead to MET exon 14 skipping (civic.EID:12831, civic.EID:1185, civic.EID:12839, OS2, OM2). Functional studies demonstrate that MET exon 14 skipping prevents the essential Tyr1003 residue for MET-product ubiquitation (civic.EID:11221, civic.EID:12840, OS2) which leads to enhanced HGFR oncogenic signaling and decreased degredation. c.3028+1G>T is reported in literature to be in the juxtamembrane domain, however it is not contained in Pfam and UniProt domains [partial OM1]. It is predicted with SpliceAI to be oncogenic with a donor loss delta score of 0.94 (internal cutoff >0.70) [OP1], and is absent from gnomAD population databases [OP4]. These evidence codes added up to a score of 9 resulting in a classification of likely oncogenic.

assertion_summary: A FOS or FOSB rearrangement is a diagnostic criterion for osteoblastoma and osteoid osteoma.
assertion_description: Osteoblastoma and osteoid osteoma are benign bone tumors that predominantly affect adolescents and young adults. Whole-genome sequencing and cytogenetic studies have shown that these tumors are characterized by FOS rearrangements in the majority of cases, with FOSB rearrangements present in a smaller subset (civic.eid:11596, civic.eid:11597, civic.eid:11787). The rearrangements typically retain the 5' end of FOS or FOSB, including the dominant transactivation and bZIP domains, and involve various 3' fusion partners such as ANKH, RUNX2, and others (civic.eid:11596, civic.eid:11787). FOS immunohistochemistry shows strong nuclear expression in nearly all tumors with FOS rearrangements, and FISH can confirm these genetic alterations, aiding in differentiation from more aggressive osteoblastic osteosarcomas (civic.eid:11596, civic.eid:11786, civic.eid:11597). Professional guidelines (WHO) list a FOS or FOSB rearrangement as a diagnostic criterion for osteoblastoma and osteoid osteoma (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).

assertion_summary: The EWSR1::CREB1 fusion represents the defining molecular feature of angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma (AFH).
assertion_description: The EWSR1::CREB1 fusion represents the defining molecular feature of angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma (AFH), supported by multi‑platform evidence demonstrating consistent detection of the canonical EWSR1 exon 7–CREB1 exon 7 fusion across cohorts (civic.EID :12855). This fusion aids in distinguishing AFH from clear cell sarcoma and other EWSR1‑rearranged mimics (civic.EID:12852). Although most EWSR1::CREB1‑positive AFH tumors show indolent clinical behavior, a documented case of widely metastatic, fatal disease confirms that this fusion, while diagnostically definitive, does not uniformly confer a favorable prognosis (civic.EID:12853). The World Health Organization (WHO) classification of tumors recognizes the detection of EWSR1::CREB1 as a diagnostic criterion for AFH (WHO Classification of Tumors, 5th edition, Volume 3: Soft Tissue and Bone Tumors).

assertion_summary: Mutations in H3-3A at K28M residue in the setting of a diffuse glioma in a midline location, combined with loss of H3 K28 trimethylation, is a diagnostic criterion for Diffuse Midline Glioma, H3 K27-altered (CNS WHO Grade 4)
assertion_description: Mutations in H3-3A at the K28M residue in the setting of a diffuse glioma in a midline location, combined with loss of H3 K28 trimethylation, are one of the diagnostic criteria for Diffuse Midline Glioma, H3 K27-altered (CNS WHO Grade 4). K28M mutations (often called K27M in the literature) are recurrent somatic missense SNVs in H3-3A, encoding the replication-independent histone variant H3.3 (civic.EID:9792, civic.EID:6450, civic.EID:10605, civic.EID:6453). Accompanying SNVs are frequent in TP53, ATRX and ACVR1, in addition to CNVs in PDGFRA, KIT and KD2. The presence of the variant must be accompanied by other essential diagnostic criteria: a diffuse glioma in a midline location (thalamus, brainstem, spinal cord, cerebellum), with loss of H3 p.K28me3. H3-3A p.K28M and H3 K28me3 loss may be assessed by immunohistochemistry. The WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition (2021) designates an H3 p.K28M/I variant as an essential diagnostic criterion of Diffuse Midline Glioma, H3 K27-altered, CNS WHO Grade 4 (civic.EID:8626).

assertion_summary: The p.Tyr527del variant is classified as likely oncogenic based on the FLT3 SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.
assertion_description: The FLT3 (NM_004119.3) variant, p.Tyr572del, resulting from c.1714_1716del, is an in-frame deletion within the juxtamembrane domain (OM1,OM2), and has not been reported as an acquired variant in individuals with hematological malignancies (cBioPortalv7.0.0, COSMICv104). The c.1714_1716del variant is also absent from the Genome Aggregation Database(v4.1) indicating it is not a common polymorphism (OP4). Computational analyses were not performed as this is not a missense variant. Functional analysis with p.Tyr572del variant in Ba/F3 cell lines shows ligand-independent FLT3 receptor constitutive activation, activation of intracellular signaling, and cellular proliferation (OS2; civic.eid:12858). This variant has a cumulative score of 9 and is classified as likely oncogenic based on the FLT3 SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.

assertion_summary: MET c.3028+1G>T is sensitive to capmatinib in non-small cell lung cancer
assertion_description: MET c.3028+1G>T is a somatic variant in NSCLC. MET c.3028+1G>T has been shown to lead to MET exon 14 skipping (civic.EID:12831, civic.EID:1185, civic.EID:12839). In preclinical studies, H596 cells harboring mutant c-MET due to exon 14 deletion were shown to be sensitive to capmatinib (INCB28060) inhibiting phospho-c-MET in in-vitro ELISA studies (civic.EID:12866). Patients resistant to crizotinib with MET alterations (including MET exon 14 skipping and MET amp) showed a disease control rate of 80% on capmatinib, with several of them with stable disease lasting 6+ months (civic.EID:11458). Capmatinib is approved for use in non-small cell lung cancer with MET exon 14 skipping based on results of the GEOMETRY mono-1 trial (civic.EID:8847).

assertion_summary: PAX5 fusions with different partner genes, excluding PAX5::JAK2 and PAX5::ZCCHC7, represent a diagnostic criterion for B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) with PAX5 alterations (PAX5alt).
assertion_description: B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) with PAX5 alterations (PAX5Alt) is a recently described subtype classified within B-ALL/lymphoma (B-ALL/LBL) with other defined genetic alterations (civic.EID:12867, civic.EID:12869). PAX5 is a B-lineage–specific transcription factor and a master regulator of B-cell development. A variety of PAX5 alterations have been identified in PAX5Alt B-ALL, including PAX5 fusions with different partner genes (excluding PAX5::JAK2 and PAX5::ZCCHC7), non–p.P80R point mutations, and focal intragenic amplifications (civic.EID:12867). More than two dozen translocation partners have been reported, all producing in-frame fusion proteins, with PAX5::ETV6 being the most frequently described (civic.EID:12867, civic.EID:12869). Professional guidelines list the presence of PAX5 fusions (except PAX5::JAK2 and PAX5::ZCCHC7) as a diagnostic criterion for PAX5Alt B-ALL (WHO Classification of Tumours Series, 5th edition, Vol. 11).

assertion_summary: VGLL2 fusion is a diagnostic criterion for a subset of spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma (SCRMS).
assertion_description: Infantile spindle cell and sclerosing rhabdomyosarcoma (SCSRMS) is a rare subtype of rhabdomyosarcoma that occurs in children under one year of age (civic.eid:12870, civic.eid:11565, civic.eid:11568, civic.eid:12871). While histopathologic analysis identifies a monomorphic spindle cell pattern resembling infantile fibrosarcoma in these tumors (civic.eid:11565, civic.eid:11568), molecular studies confirm recurrent VGLL2 fusions, most commonly VGLL2::NCOA2 and VGLL2::CITED2 (civic.eid:12870, civic.eid:11565, civic.eid:11568, civic.eid:12871). These fusions can be detected using RNA sequencing, FISH, targeted DNA sequencing, or RT-PCR, and serve as a molecular diagnostic test for infantile SCSRMS (civic.eid:12870, civic.eid:11565, civic.eid:11568, civic.eid:12871). The presence of VGLL2 fusions defines a distinct, clinically favorable infantile SCSRMS subgroup and enables molecular distinction from embryonal and alveolar RMS subtypes (civic.eid:12870, civic.eid:11565, civic.eid:11568, civic.eid:12871). Professional guidelines (WHO) list VGLL2 rearrangements as a diagnostic criterion for the subtype of SCSRMS (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: PAG1::ABL2 is oncogenic in Ph-Like B-ALL
assertion_description: Fusion between the tumor suppressor PAG1 and tyrosine kinase ABL2 has been reported in at least two cases of Ph-like B-ALL (GS, CA2), in frame, with an intact tyrosine kinase domain, and ABL2 as the 3 prime partner (FG1, FG2, FG3, civic.EID:12872, civic.EID:9721). Functional studies showed that PAG1::ABL2 induced IL3 independent growth in Ba/F3 cells, and that in human and mouse hematopoietic cells, PAG1 was expressed at a higher level that ABL2, indicating a mechanism for increased and unregulated expression of ABL2 kinase when fused to PAG1 and driven by its promoter (FS). Collectively, FG1+FG2+FG3+CA2+GS results in an Oncogenic classification for PAG1::ABL2 via the ClinGen BCR::ABL1-like Somatic Cancer Variant Curation Expert Panel (SC-VCEP) fusion oncogenicity rules.

assertion_summary: Tazemetostat has been withdrawn for treatment of follicular lymphoma with EZH2 A682G
assertion_description: EZH2 A682G (occasionally reported as A677G in the literature) is a recurrent somatic variant in the catalytic SET domain observed in follicular lymphoma (civic.EID:11111). Clinical studies show that A682G persists across multiple tumor sites, correlates with elevated circulating tumor DNA, aggressive disease, resistance to immunochemotherapy, and poor outcomes, supporting its oncogenic role (civic.EID:12875). Cohort sequencing studies demonstrate that A682G is a recurrent somatic variant in follicular lymphoma (civic.EID:12876). Additionally, RNA-seq analysis of a diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) case demonstrated preferential mutant allele expression of A682G, indicating positive selection and a functional role in tumorigenesis (civic.EID:12904). Functional studies of nearby SET domain hotspot mutations reveal gain-of-function enzymatic activity, increased H3K27 trimethylation, and transcriptional repression, indicating a shared mechanism for oncogenic SET domain mutations (OS2; civic.EID:12408). The A682G variant is located in the catalytic SET domain (OM1), observed in cBioPortal: 3 Lymph, 6 Others (OP3), and absent from population databases (gnomAD v4.1.0, OP4). Together, these criteria indicate that A682G is likely oncogenic, with a score of 8. After accelerated FDA approval in 2020, Tazemetostat (Tazverik) was voluntarily withdrawn from all markets and indications on March 9, 2026, after an independent data monitoring committee identified cases of secondary hematologic malignancies in the SYMPHONY-1 trial. In addition, the FDA issued a Drug Alert detailing the increased rate of hematologic secondary primary malignancies (SPMs) associated to the drug. It was reported that 18 out of 318 (5.7%) of patients treated with Tazemetostat developed hematologic SPMs, with no SPM events in the control arm. Most of the SPMs were myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukemia.

assertion_summary: Tazemetostat has been withdrawn for treatment of follicular lymphoma with EZH2 A682G
assertion_description: EZH2 A682G (occasionally reported as A677G in the literature) is a somatic mutation located in the SET domain of EZH2 and is associated with oncogenic activity in follicular lymphoma. assertion_summary: IDH1 R132L is a susceptible IDH1 mutation that confers sensitivity to ivosidenib in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and is detected by the FDA-approved Abbott RealTime IDH1 companion diagnostic assay.
assertion_description: IDH1 R132L is a somatic missense mutation at the conserved R132 residue of IDH1, conferring neomorphic gain-of-function activity that drives accumulation of the oncometabolite D-2-hydroxyglutarate (2-HG), leading to epigenetic dysregulation and blocked myeloid differentiation. IDH1 R132L is one of five susceptible IDH1 R132 variants (R132C, R132G, R132H, R132L, R132S) detected by the FDA-approved Abbott RealTime IDH1 companion diagnostic and specifically named in the ivosidenib prescribing information. Clinical evidence supporting sensitivity to ivosidenib includes phase 1 study in R/R AML (CR+CRh rate 30.4%; PMID:29860938) and the phase 3 AGILE trial in newly diagnosed AML, in which ivosidenib plus azacitidine significantly improved OS versus placebo plus azacitidine (median 24.0 vs 7.9 months; HR 0.44; PMID:35443108), with long-term follow-up confirming a median OS of 29.3 months (PMID:40706052). Based on FDA approval of ivosidenib for IDH1-mutated AML (monotherapy 2018; combination with azacitidine 2022) and NCCN Category 1 recommendation for the newly diagnosed setting, IDH1 R132L confers Tier I – Level A classification under AMP/ASCO/CAP 2017 guidelines.

assertion_summary: IDH1 R132L is oncogenic variant in acute myeloid leukemia.

Like all R132 substitutions, R132L abrogates normal isocitrate-to-α-ketoglutarate catalysis and confers a neomorphic gain-of-function, enabling NADPH-dependent reduction of α-ketoglutarate to the oncometabolite D-2-hydroxyglutarate (D-2HG). Elevated D-2HG competitively inhibits α-KG-dependent dioxygenases, driving a hypermethylation phenotype that impairs cellular differentiation and promotes tumorigenesis. IDH1 R132L meets criteria for Oncogenic classification is based on: OS2 (hotspot residue with recurrent somatic mutation across tumor types and robust functional evidence), OS3 (159 cases on COSMIC v103; 38 in haematopoietic / lymphoid tumours), OP1 (predicted to be a driver mutation by multiple computational predictors ), and OP4 (absent from population databases (gnomAD database v4.1.0). Together these criteria indicate that IDH1 R132L oncogenic with a score of 10.

assertion_summary: KIT D816V is likely oncogenic in systemic mastocytosis.
assertion_description: KIT D816V is a somatic variant observed in systemic mastocytosis and related hematologic malignancies. Functional studies demonstrate that this variant induces ligand-independent activation of KIT, leading to constitutive autophosphorylation, cytokine-independent proliferation, and persistent activation of downstream signaling pathways including JAK/STAT, PI3K, MAPK/ERK, and JNK, consistent with a gain-of-function oncogenic effect (civic.EID:12411, civic.EID:12916, civic.EID:12913, civic.EID:12914, OS2). Structural and computational analyses further show that D816V destabilizes the inactive conformation of the kinase domain, promoting a shift toward the active state and enhancing kinase activity, providing a mechanistic basis for constitutive signaling and transformation (civic.EID:12917, civic.EID:12915, OS2). The D816V variant is located within the protein tyrosine kinase catalytic domain (OM1), is predicted to be a driver mutation CHASMplus score 0.696-0.711 >VECS gene-specific cutoff of 0.38, OP1), and is extremely rare in population databases (gnomAD v4.1.0 allele frequency 0.000001860, OP4). KIT D816V is a recurrent hotspot variant in systemic mastocytosis, with one large clinical series identifying D816V in 417 of 456 (91%) consecutively diagnosed systemic mastocytosis patients (PMID: 26067933), and its recurrent detection has been independently demonstrated in additional prospective patient cohorts (PMID: 41399928) (OS3). Together, these criteria indicate that KIT D816V is oncogenic, with a score of 12.

assertion_summary: EGFR T790M is likely oncogenic in lung non-small cell carcinoma.
assertion_description: EGFR T790M is a recurrent variant in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with evidence of functional and oncogenic effects. Functional studies show increased EGFR kinase activity, including enhanced autophosphorylation and downstream signaling such as MAPK activation, consistent with a gain-of-function effect (OS2; civic.EID:12922, civic.EID:12923). In cellular models, T790M alone produces modest proliferative and transforming activity, but contributes to increased growth and ligand-independent signaling in epithelial systems (OS2; civic.EID:12922, civic.EID:12924). When combined with activating EGFR mutations (e.g., L858R or exon 19 deletions), T790M strongly enhances kinase activation, constitutive signaling, and oncogenic transformation, including anchorage-independent growth and tumor formation (OS2; civic.EID:12923, civic.EID:12924). In vivo mouse models further demonstrate that T790M can drive lung adenocarcinoma formation and that resulting tumors remain dependent on EGFR signaling and are resistant to EGFR inhibitors such as erlotinib (OS2; civic.EID:12925). The T790M variant is located in a well-established cancer hotspot region (OS3), is predicted to be a driver mutation (CHASMplus score 0.571-0.733 >VECS gene-specific cutoff of 0.64, OP1). Together, these criteria indicate that EGFR T790M is likely oncogenic with a score of 9.

assertion_summary: MET c.2999_3028+4del is approved for capmatinib use in non-small cell lung cancer
assertion_description: MET c.2999_3028+4del is a somatic variant in NSCLC predicted to cause exon 14 skipping mutation. In preclinical studies, H596 cells harboring mutant c-MET due to exon 14 deletion were shown to be sensitive to capmatinib (INCB28060) inhibiting phospho-c-MET in in-vitro ELISA studies (civic.EID:12866). Patients resistant to crizotinib with MET alterations (including MET exon 14 skipping and MET amp) showed a disease control rate of 80% on capmatinib, with several of them with stable disease lasting 6+ months (civic.EID:11458). Capmatinib is approved for use in non-small cell lung cancer with MET exon 14 skipping based on results of the GEOMETRY mono-1 trial (civic.EID:8847). Literature reports for MET c.2999_3028+4del were not found, although it is predicted to cause MET exon 14 skipping according to FDA documentation.

assertion_summary: BRAF V600E mutant anaplastic thyroid carcinoma is sensitive to dabrafenib and trametinib combination therapy.
assertion_description: Combination therapy with dabrafenib (a BRAF inhibitor) and trametinib (a MEK inhibitor) demonstrates consistent clinical activity in BRAF V600E-mutated anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (ATC), supporting the association between this variant and response to MAPK pathway inhibition. Clinical evidence from the phase II ROAR basket study demonstrated meaningful objective responses and durable survival outcomes in BRAF V600E-mutant patients treated with this combination (civic.EID:10785). These findings are supported by a systematic review and meta-analysis reporting high pooled response rates and improved survival outcomes across multiple studies of BRAF V600E-mutated ATC treated with dabrafenib plus trametinib (civic.EID:12960). Real-world retrospective data further demonstrated improved response rates and survival compared with non-targeted therapies in BRAF V600E-mutant patients receiving this regimen (civic.EID:12957). Additional multi-institutional retrospective evidence confirmed high objective response rates and improved survival associated with targeted therapy in BRAF V600E-mutant ATC (civic.EID:12959). A single-patient case report also described a durable complete response to dabrafenib plus trametinib in metastatic BRAF V600E-mutated ATC, further supporting the therapeutic sensitivity of this variant (civic.EID:12958). Collectively, these evidence items consistently support the predictive role of BRAF V600E for response to dabrafenib and trametinib in ATC.

assertion_description: Myoepithelial tumors outside of the salivary glands are biologically different from those arising in the salivary glands. They can involve a wide variety of deep and superficial soft tissue locations, bone and also the skin. EWSR1 rearrangement has been identified in ~45% of cases. More than half of EWSR1 positive myoepithelial tumors occurred in children and young adults in one study civic.eid:12926. Several gene partners have been described including POU5F1, PBX1, ZNF444, KLF15, ATF1, KLF17 which contributes to the biologic and histologic heterogeneity observed across cases civic.eid:12926, civic.eid:12927, civic.eid:12929, civic.eid:12930, civic.eid:12931. Professional guidelines (WHO) list detection of EWSR1 rearrangements as a diagnostic criterium for myoepithelial tumors of soft tissue (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

assertion_summary: EWSR1 fusions with various partner genes, including POU5F1, PBX1, ZNF444, KLF15, ATF1, and KLF17, represent a diagnostic criterion for myoepithelial tumors of soft tissue.
assertion_description: Myoepithelial tumors arising outside the salivary glands are biologically distinct from their salivary gland counterparts. They can occur in a wide range of deep and superficial soft tissue sites, as well as in bone and the skin (civic.EID:12926). EWSR1 rearrangements are identified in approximately 45% of cases and are particularly enriched in pediatric and young adult patients (civic.EID:12926). Multiple fusion partners have been reported, including POU5F1, PBX1, ZNF444, KLF15, ATF1, and KLF17, contributing to the notable histologic and biologic heterogeneity observed across cases (civic.EID:12927). Histologic patterns are variable, encompassing epithelioid, spindle, clear cell, and small round cell morphologies, and tumors may show benign or malignant behavior (civic.EID:12929). Rare fusions, such as EWSR1::KLF15 and EWSR1::ZNF444, highlight the importance of integrating molecular testing with morphology and immunohistochemistry to accurately classify these tumors and inform prognosis (civic.EID:12930). Professional guidelines list the presence of EWSR1 rearrangements as a diagnostic criterion for myoepithelial tumors of soft tissue (civic.EID:12931).
