assertion_summary: CNTRL::ABL1 is an oncogenic fusion associated with B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma.
assertion_description: The CNTRL::ABL1 fusion has been reported in at least two patients with B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL). The published breakpoints resulted in in-frame fusion transcripts that retained the ABL1 SH2 domain, tyrosine kinase domain, and F-actin binding region. Consistent with other oncogenic ABL-class rearrangements, ABL1 serves as the 3′ fusion partner and contributes the intact kinase domain to the predicted fusion protein (FG1, FG2, FG3, civic.EID:13001). The fusion has been identified in independent leukemia cases and detected using next-generation sequencing-based approaches with orthogonal molecular confirmation (CA2, civic.EID:13001, civic.EID:13002). In addition, a patient with CNTRL::ABL1-positive BCR-ABL1-like B-ALL achieved a rapid and deep remission following dasatinib treatment, supporting clinical sensitivity to ABL-directed tyrosine kinase inhibition (CV, civic.EID:13001). Collectively, FG1+FG2+FG3+CA2+CV support an Oncogenic classification for CNTRL::ABL1 via the ClinGen BCR::ABL1-like SC-VCEP fusion oncogenicity rules.

assertion_summary: AGGF1::PDGFRB is oncogenic in B-ALL
assertion_description: The AGGF1::PDGFRB fusion has appeared in one case of B-ALL, and one case of T-ALL (civic.EID:13004). In the case of B-ALL, the fusion of AGGF1 exons 1-6 and PDGFRb exons 11-23 had the kinase as the 3 prime partner, was in frame, and contained the complete kinase domain (FG1, FG2, FG3, civic.EID:13007). The coiled-coil domain of AGGF1 was proposed to form dimers of the fusion, inducing autophosphorylation of the kinase. AGGF1::PDGFRB induced cytokine independent growth in Ba/F3 and primary murine bone marrow cells, as well as growth pathway activation (FS, civic.EID:13004, civic.EID:13007). A chemotherapy refractory, 4 year old B-ALL patient with AGGF1::PDGFRB fusion responded to imatinib therapy with complete remission, before progression (CV, civic.EID:13008). The presence of the codes FG1, FG2, FG3, FS, and CV results in an Oncogenic classification for AGGF1::PDGFRB via the ClinGen BCR::ABL1-like SC-VCEP fusion oncogenicity rules

assertion_summary: BRAF V600E is oncogenic in anaplastic thyroid carcinoma.
assertion_description: BRAF V600E is a recurrent somatic variant in anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (ATC) (civic.EID:13014, civic.EID:13015). Functional studies demonstrate that BRAF V600E activates MAPK signaling, promotes thyroid tumorigenesis in vivo, and is associated with invasive and poorly differentiated thyroid tumor phenotypes (civic.EID:13013). Additionally, pharmacologic inhibition of BRAF V600E in BRAF V600E-positive ATC models suppresses ERK signaling, reduces tumor growth, proliferation, migration, and metastatic burden, and increases apoptosis, supporting a critical role for BRAF V600E in maintaining the malignant phenotype (civic.EID:13011, civic.EID:13012, OS2). BRAF V600E is predicted to be a driver mutation (CHASMplus score 0.966 >VECS gene-specific cutoff of 0.63, OP1), is a recurrent hotspot variant in cancerhotspots.org with 897 variants reported at codon V600, including 833 occurrences of the V600E amino acid substitution (OS3), and is absent from population databases (gnomAD database v4.1.0, OP4). Together, these criteria indicate that BRAF V600E is oncogenic, with a score of 10.

assertion_summary: FGFR3 V555M is classified as a Variant of Uncertain Significance according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.
assertion_description: In vitro studies are equivocal as to whether the V555M variant affects normal FGFR3 function in a manner consistent with oncogenic activation. Purified recombinant FGFR3 protein harboring the V555M variant exhibits increased kinase activity and catalytic efficiency compared with wild-type FGFR3 (civic.EID:12988, civic.EID:12989). However, NIH3T3 cells expressing FGFR3 V555M do not exhibit increased cell proliferation, anchorage-independent growth, or morphological transformation, while saturation mutagenesis studies support only weak oncogenic activation (civic.EID:12990, civic.EID:12882) (OS2_Moderate). The V555M variant has a score of 0.727 from the REVEL in silico prediction tool (OP1). The FGFR3 c.1663G>A (p.V555M) variant is present in the gnomAD database at a minor allele frequency of less than 0.0001 (Grpmax Filtering AF, 95% confidence = 0.00000079 in Non-Finnish European) [OP4]. These codes lead to an Oncogenicity score of 4 (OS2_Moderate [2]; OP1 [1]; OP4 [1]). Therefore, the FGFR3 V555M variant is classified as a Variant of Uncertain Significance according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications. .

assertion_summary: FGFR3 G697C is classified as Likely Benign according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.
assertion_description: Functional studies are equivocal but largely indicate that the G697C variant does not affect normal FGFR3 function in a manner consistent with oncogenic activation. Although one study reported increased FGFR3 autophosphorylation and membrane localization in oral squamous cell carcinoma cells (civic.EID:10837), multiple independent studies demonstrated no MAPK activation, cellular transformation, anchorage-independent growth, or proliferative advantage compared with wild-type FGFR3 (civic.EID:10838, civic.EID:10839, civic.EID:12848) (SBS2). The G697C variant has a score of 0.878 from the REVEL in silico prediction tool (OP1). The FGFR3 c.2089G>T (p.G697C) variant is absent in the gnomAD database (OP4). These codes lead to an Oncogenicity score of -2 (OP1 [1]; OP4 [1]; SBS2 [-4]). Therefore, the FGFR3 G697C variant is classified as Likely Benign according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.

assertion_summary: EGFR L858R is sensitive to dacomitinib in lung non-small cell carcinoma.
assertion_description: EGFR L858R is a recurrent activating mutation located in the tyrosine kinase domain of EGFR that predicts response to dacomitinib in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Preclinical studies demonstrated that EGFR L858R is sensitive to dacomitinib, with inhibition of EGFR signaling and downstream Akt phosphorylation in engineered cell models (civic.EID:4285), and greater sensitivity to dacomitinib than to gefitinib in NSCLC H3255 cells and Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR L858R (civic.EID:2627). Clinical evidence from a pooled subset analysis of the randomized ARCHER 1009 and A7471028 trials demonstrated longer progression-free survival and overall survival with dacomitinib compared with erlotinib in patients harboring common activating EGFR mutations, including exon 19 deletions and L858R (civic.EID:4860). These findings are further supported by the phase III ARCHER 1050 trial, in which dacomitinib significantly improved progression-free survival compared with gefitinib, with prespecified subgroup analyses demonstrating similar benefit in patients with EGFR exon 19 deletion and EGFR L858R mutations (civic.EID:11239).

assertion_summary: EGFR L858R is likely oncogenic in lung non-small cell carcinoma.
assertion_description: EGFR L858R is a recurrent somatic activating mutation located in the activation loop of the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain and is one of the most common EGFR mutations identified in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Functional and biochemical studies demonstrate that EGFR L858R increases EGFR kinase activity through multiple complementary mechanisms, including enhanced and sustained ligand-induced receptor autophosphorylation (civic.EID:13024), constitutive kinase activation resulting from destabilization of the inactive kinase conformation and an approximately 50-fold increase in catalytic activity compared with wild-type EGFR (civic.EID:13026), and constitutive activation of downstream STAT5, ERK1/2, ERK5, and AKT signaling pathways (civic.EID:13025). Exogenous expression of EGFR L858R induces interleukin-3-independent transformation of Ba/F3 cells (civic.EID:13025), promotes increased invasion of NSCLC cells and malignant pleural effusion formation through activation of the CXCL12-CXCR4 signaling axis (civic.EID:13029), and enhances cell survival by increasing Akt and STAT5 signaling, conferring resistance to apoptosis while mutation-specific knockdown induces extensive apoptosis in NSCLC cells harboring endogenous EGFR L858R (civic.EID:13030, OS2). EGFR L858R is predicted to be a driver mutation (CHASMplus score 0.835-0.87 >VECS gene-specific cutoff of 0.64, OP1), is a recurrent hotspot variant in cancerhotspots.org with 144 variants reported at codon 858, all representing the L858R amino acid substitution (OS3), and is absent from population databases (gnomAD database v4.1.0, OP4, OP4). Together, these criteria indicate that EGFR L858R is oncogenic, with a score of 10.

assertion_summary: BRAF V600E-mutant melanoma is sensitive to vemurafenib.
assertion_description: Clinical and preclinical evidence consistently demonstrate that BRAF V600E predicts response to vemurafenib in melanoma. The phase III BRIM-3 trial demonstrated significantly improved overall survival, progression-free survival, and objective response rates with vemurafenib compared with dacarbazine in patients with BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic melanoma (civic.EID:1409). Extended follow-up of BRIM-3 confirmed durable survival benefits (civic.EID:1398), while the phase II trial demonstrated durable objective responses with vemurafenib monotherapy in patients with BRAF V600-mutant metastatic melanoma (civic.EID:1410). These findings are supported by preclinical studies demonstrating selective inhibition of MAPK signaling and tumor regression in BRAF V600E-mutant melanoma models following vemurafenib treatment (civic.EID:3746). Acquired resistance has been associated with the emergence of the p61BRAF(V600E) splice variant, which restores MAPK signaling despite BRAF inhibition (civic.EID:9702). Collectively, these evidence items support the predictive role of BRAF V600E for response to vemurafenib in melanoma.

assertion_summary: BRAF V600E-mutant melanoma is sensitive to encorafenib plus binimetinib.
assertion_description: Clinical evidence demonstrates that BRAF V600E predicts response to encorafenib plus binimetinib in melanoma. In the phase III COLUMBUS trial, encorafenib plus binimetinib significantly improved progression-free survival compared with vemurafenib in patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma harboring BRAF V600E or V600K mutations (civic.EID:7287). These findings are supported by a multicenter phase Ib/II study in BRAF inhibitor-naïve metastatic melanoma, in which 89% of patients had BRAF V600E and treatment with encorafenib plus binimetinib produced a confirmed objective response rate of 73%, a disease control rate of 96%, and a median progression-free survival of 11.0 months (civic.EID:13042). Collectively, these evidence items support the predictive role of BRAF V600E for sensitivity to encorafenib plus binimetinib in melanoma.

assertion_summary: The ERBB2 variant G292R is of uncertain significance.
assertion_description: The ERBB2 G292R variant is a rare variant that has been observed in cancers of the hepatobiliary and urinary tracts; it is not prevalent in breast cancer. This variant is located in the extracellular cysteine-rich domain C1 that is critical for dimerization (civic.EID:12118) (OM1). Functional data from in vitro assays of cell growth and focus formation are limited, and results have been mixed (civic.EID:12116, civic.EID:12117, civic.EID:12118)(OS2_Moderate). CHASMplus scores do not indicate that this is a deleterious mutation (scores between 0.377-0.567 do not reach the VECS gene-specific cutoff of 0.68 for ERBB2). No instances are reported in cancerhotspots (V2). The variant is absent in the gnomAD database (v4.1.0, OP4). In the absence of stronger functional data, these criteria indicate that G292R remains a Variant of Unknown Significance (VUS), with a score of 5.

assertion_summary: The ERBB2 V777L variant is likely oncogenic.
assertion_description: The ERBB2 V777L variant is found in breast cancer and at low frequency in other solid tumors; it may or may not be associated with gene amplification (civic.EID:12103). It displays greater tyrosine kinase activity than wild-type in multiple in vitro kinase assays (civic.EID:12103). It induces anchorage-independent growth and tumor formation in xenografts when stably over-expressed in cultured murine NCI-H508 colon cancer cells (civic.EID:4452) NIH-3T3 cells and MCF10A human breast epithelial cells (civic.EID:12103, civic.EID:12104 (OS2). This variant is located in the ATP-binding site of the tyrosine kinase catalytic domain (OM1). ERBB2 V777L is predicted to be deleterious (CHASMplus scores between 0.761-0.803 exceed the VECS gene-specific cutoff of 0.68 for ERBB2, OP1). Seventeen instances of the variant occur in cancerhotspots.org (V2), 6 in breast, 4 in colon, and 7 in other cancer types (OP3). The variant is absent in the gnomAD database (v4.1.0, OP4). Together these criteria indicate that V777L is likely oncogenic, with a score of 9.

assertion_summary: BRAF V600E-mutant melanoma is sensitive to atezolizumab, cobimetinib, and vemurafenib combination therapy.
assertion_description: Clinical evidence supports the predictive role of BRAF V600E for response to combination therapy with atezolizumab, cobimetinib, and vemurafenib in melanoma. A phase Ib study demonstrated durable antitumor activity with the triplet regimen in patients with BRAF V600-mutated metastatic melanoma (civic.EID:13043). The phase III IMspire150 trial demonstrated significantly prolonged progression-free survival compared with cobimetinib and vemurafenib alone (civic.EID:11238), while an exploratory biomarker analysis confirmed benefit in the centrally confirmed BRAF V600E subgroup (civic.EID:13045). Updated follow-up from IMspire150 demonstrated durable progression-free survival benefit, although overall survival was not significantly improved (civic.EID:13046). Additional phase II evidence demonstrated intracranial activity in patients with BRAF V600-mutated melanoma and CNS metastases (civic.EID:13044). Collectively, these evidence items support the predictive role of BRAF V600E for sensitivity to atezolizumab, cobimetinib, and vemurafenib in melanoma.

assertion_summary: The KRAS A146P variant is likely oncogenic.
assertion_description: KRAS codon A146 variants are rare, occurring in 1-5% of colorectal cancers and very rarely in other solid tumors. The KRAS A146P variant is the least frequent variant at codon A146, which resides within the conserved GTPase/RAS domain (OM1). This variant displays increased ERK2 activation relative to wild-type, induces IL3-independent transformation in BaF3 cells (civic.EID:12168), and causes focus formation in 3T3 cells (civic.EID:13018) (OS2). KRAS A146P is predicted to be deleterious by in silico models (ChasmPlus score of 0.89, which is above the VECS gene-specific threshold of 0.75 for KRAS; OP1). This variant is found in five samples in cancerhotspots.org (V2): 2 bowel, 1 lung, 1 testis, and 1 other (OP3). The variant is absent in the gnomAD database (v4.1.0, OP4). Together these criteria indicate that A146P is likely oncogenic, with a score of 9.

assertion_summary: BRAF V600E is oncogenic in melanoma.
assertion_description: BRAF V600E (reported as V599E in earlier publications) is a recurrent somatic variant in melanoma. Functional studies demonstrate that BRAF V600E constitutively activates MAPK signaling through increased kinase activity and ERK phosphorylation, disrupts the inactive kinase conformation, and promotes cellular transformation compared with wild-type BRAF (civic.EID:13053, civic.EID:13055, OS2). Additional cellular, animal, and patient-derived studies demonstrate that BRAF V600E promotes melanocyte transformation, melanoma initiation, invasion, and metastatic progression, while sustained expression in primary human melanocytes induces oncogene-induced senescence, indicating that additional cooperating alterations are required for complete malignant transformation (civic.EID:13052, civic.EID:13054, civic.EID:13056, OS2). BRAF V600E is predicted to be a driver mutation (CHASMplus score 0.966 >VECS gene-specific cutoff of 0.63, OP1), is a recurrent hotspot variant in cancerhotspots.org with 897 variants reported at codon V600, including 833 occurrences of the V600E amino acid substitution (OS3), and is absent from population databases (gnomAD database v4.1.0, OP4). Together, these criteria indicate that BRAF V600E is oncogenic, with a score of 10.

assertion_summary: LRRC71::NTRK1 is classified as a Likely Oncogenic NTRK fusion.
assertion_description: The LRRC71::NTRK1 fusion has been reported in three published adult cancer cases, including uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma, lung adenocarcinoma, and lung squamous cell carcinoma. In each reported case, NTRK1 is the 3′ partner gene (FG1). Additionally, one study demonstrated that the fusion joins LRRC71 exon 1 to NTRK1 exons 8–17, preserving the NTRK1 tyrosine kinase domain (TKD) (FG2). Although LRRC71 is a novel 5′ fusion partner, its occurrence in multiple independent cancer cases supports CA3. No published studies have demonstrated that the fusion is in-frame, functionally characterized the fusion, demonstrated RNA or protein expression of the fusion, or shown a clinical response to TRK inhibitor therapy. Collectively, the application of FG1 + FG2 + CA3 results in a Likely Oncogenic classification for LRRC71::NTRK1 via the ClinGen NTRK SC-VCEP fusion oncogenicity rules.

assertion_summary: DPP10::NTRK3 is classified as a NTRK fusion of uncertain significance.
assertion_description: The DPP10::NTRK3 fusion was identified in a single case of malignant melanoma. NTRK3 is the 3′ partner gene (FG1), and the reported fusion junction occurs upstream of and preserves the NTRK3 tyrosine kinase domain (FG2). However, the exact breakpoint is not clearly defined because the text and figure are not fully consistent, and RNA-based analysis was not performed to confirm an expressed, in-frame fusion transcript. The fusion has not been reported recurrently in more than three individuals, DPP10 is not an established recurrent 5′ fusion partner in cancer, and conventional malignant melanoma is not considered an NTRK fusion-associated tumor type. No functional studies, RNA or protein expression evidence, or clinical response to NTRK-targeted therapy were reported. Therefore, with only FG1 + FG2 applied, DPP10::NTRK3 is classified as a fusion of uncertain significance via the ClinGen NTRK SC-VCEP fusion oncogenicity rules.

assertion_summary: CCDC171::NTRK1 is classified as a Likely Oncogenic NTRK fusion.
assertion_description: The CCDC171::NTRK1 fusion has been reported in one case of undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma. The study identified CCDC171 as the 5′ fusion partner and NTRK1 as the 3′ fusion partner (FG1). The reported fusion structure places NTRK1 as the 3′ partner, consistent with preservation of the kinase-containing region (FG2). The fusion was detected by whole-exome RNA sequencing (FS2). The exact exon-level breakpoint and reading frame were not reported, and no fusion-specific functional studies or clinical responses to TRK inhibition were described. The authors noted that the biological significance of NTRK fusions in complex-genomic sarcomas remains uncertain. Based on the available evidence, FG1 + FG2 + FS2 supports the classification of CCDC171::NTRK1 as a Likely Oncogenic NTRK fusion under the ClinGen NTRK SC-VCEP framework.

assertion_summary: KHDRBS1::NTRK1 is classified as a Likely Oncogenic NTRK fusion.
assertion_description: The KHDRBS1::NTRK1 fusion has been reported in one case of unclassified mesenchymal sarcoma. KHDRBS1 is the 5′ fusion partner and NTRK1 is the 3′ fusion partner (FG1). The reported fusion joins KHDRBS1 exons 1–8 to NTRK1 exons 12–17, retaining the NTRK1 tyrosine kinase domain (FG2). The patient demonstrated a complete and durable clinical response to crizotinib, with complete regression of metastatic disease and no evidence of disease progression during approximately 45 months of follow-up (CV). However, the fusion has only been reported in a single case, and no published studies have demonstrated that the fusion transcript is expressed and in-frame, functionally characterized the fusion, or demonstrated fusion-specific RNA or protein expression. Based on the available evidence, FG1 + FG2 + CV supports the classification of KHDRBS1::NTRK1 as a Likely Oncogenic NTRK fusion under the ClinGen NTRK SC-VCEP fusion oncogenicity framework.

assertion_summary: BRAF V600E is oncogenic in colorectal cancer.
assertion_description: BRAF p.V600E is a recurrent somatic variant in colorectal cancer and an early driver of the serrated neoplasia pathway. Functional studies demonstrate that BRAF p.V600E constitutively activates MAPK signaling and promotes epithelial dedifferentiation, tumor initiation, and colorectal transformation in patient-derived organoid and mouse models compared with wild-type BRAF (civic.EID:13065, civic.EID:13071, OS2). Additional cellular, animal, and patient-derived studies demonstrate that BRAF p.V600E promotes serrated tumorigenesis, malignant progression, and cooperation with additional genetic alterations or inflammatory stimuli, consistent with a gain-of-function oncogenic effect (civic.EID:13066, civic.EID:13069, OS2). BRAF V600E is predicted to be a driver mutation (CHASMplus score 0.966 >VECS gene-specific cutoff of 0.63, OP1), is a recurrent hotspot variant in cancerhotspots.org with 897 variants reported at codon V600, including 833 occurrences of the V600E amino acid substitution (OS3), and is absent from population databases (gnomAD database v4.1.0, OP4). Together, these criteria indicate that BRAF V600E is oncogenic, with a score of 10.

assertion_summary: H3-3B K28M is Likely Oncogenic
assertion_description: The H3-3B K28M mutation has the same amino acid change as an established oncogenic variant at the canonical hotspot for histone mutant glioma (OS1, 4 points). It is located in a conserved residue affecting epigenetic modification (OM1, 2 points). The variant is absent in gnomAD v4.1.1 (OP1, 1 point). K28M in H3-3B () was not found to be reported in literature searches, while rare instances of K27M in H3-3A were reported.

assertion_summary: IDH1 R132H is sensitive to ivosidenib in acute myeloid leukemia.
assertion_description: IDH1 R132H is a missense mutation affecting the conserved R132 residue of IDH1 that predicts response to ivosidenib in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Preclinical studies demonstrated that ivosidenib suppresses 2-hydroxyglutarate production and induces myeloid differentiation in AML models harboring IDH1 R132 mutations (civic.EID:12903). Clinical evidence from phase I studies demonstrated durable clinical activity of ivosidenib monotherapy in patients with relapsed or refractory and newly diagnosed IDH1 R132-mutated AML, including durable remissions, mutation clearance, and prolonged overall survival (civic.EID:13075, civic.EID:13076, civic.EID:13077). Collectively, these findings support the sensitivity of AML harboring IDH1 R132H to ivosidenib.

assertion_summary: This variant p.Q771P has a cumulative score of -2 and is classified as likely benign based on the FLT3 SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.
assertion_description: The FLT3 (NM_004119.3) variant, p.Q771P, resulting from c.2312A>C, occurs within the tyrosine kinase domain (OM1), and has been reported as an acquired variant in 1 individual with a hematological malignancy (civic.EID:XXXX). This c.2312A>C variant is found in the African/African-American population with an allele frequency of 0.4237% (318/75058 alleles, including 1 homozygote) and a filtering allele frequency of 0.3854% in the Genome Aggregation Database (v4.1.1) (SBS1). Computational analyses predict that the p.Q771P variant is tolerated (ClinPred score=0.062), and neither impacts a nearby canonical splice site nor creates a cryptic splice site (SpliceAI). This variant p.Q771P is classified as likely benign based on the FLT3 SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications (Version 1).

assertion_summary: This variant p.S684P has a cumulative score of 2 and is classified as a variant of uncertain significance based on the FLT3 SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.
assertion_description: The FLT3 (NM_004119.3) variant, p.S684P, resulting from c.2050T>C, occurs within the tyrosine kinase domain (OM1), and has not been reported as an acquired variant in individuals with hematological malignancies. This c.2050T>C variant is found in the non-Finnish European population with an allele frequency of 0.01951% (220/1127488 alleles) and a filtering allele frequency of 0.01737% in the Genome Aggregation Database (v4.1.1). Computational analyses predict that the p.S684P variant is not damaging (ClinPred score=0.255), and neither impacts a nearby canonical splice site nor creates a cryptic splice site (SpliceAI). This variant p.S684P is classified as a variant of uncertain significance based on the FLT3 SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications (Version 1).

assertion_summary: KRAS G12C-positive metastatic colorectal cancer is resistant to cetuximab-based therapy when cetuximab is administered without a KRAS G12C inhibitor.
assertion_description: Somatic KRAS G12C is an established negative predictive biomarker for response to cetuximab-based therapy in metastatic colorectal cancer when cetuximab is administered without a KRAS G12C inhibitor. Variant-specific clinical data from 16 patients with KRAS G12C-positive colorectal cancer treated primarily with cetuximab plus irinotecan demonstrated one partial response, stable disease in six patients, and progressive disease in nine patients; median progression-free survival and overall survival were 11 and 24 weeks, respectively (civic:EID3967). These findings are consistent with multiple clinical studies of broader KRAS exon 2 or codon 12/13-mutant colorectal cancer populations demonstrating absent or markedly reduced response and shorter progression-free and overall survival following cetuximab-containing therapy (e.g., civic:EID3968, civic:EID3969, civic:EID3970). A small cetuximab-monotherapy subgroup reported in civic:EID3963 did not demonstrate statistically significant differences in progression-free or overall survival between KRAS-mutant and KRAS wild-type tumors; however, this subgroup included only 30 patients. FDA-authorized companion diagnostics for cetuximab, including the therascreen KRAS RGQ PCR Kit, assess KRAS codon 12/13 status and specifically detect G12C. Cetuximab monotherapy and cetuximab administered with conventional chemotherapy are FDA-labeled for KRAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer, whereas adagrasib plus cetuximab has a separate indication for previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic colorectal cancer. Collectively, the regulatory and clinical evidence supports classification of this molecular profile–disease–therapy relationship as AMP/ASCO/CAP Tier I – Level A. This assertion does not apply to cetuximab administered in combination with a KRAS G12C inhibitor, such as adagrasib.

assertion_summary: FGFR3 R248C is Likely Oncogenic
assertion_description: Expression of FGFR3 carrying the R248C variant in HEK293 cells resulted in increased phospho-ERK (civic.EID:8320). In Addition, R248C induced IL3 and FGF1 independent growth in Ba/R3 cells, and colony formation, transformation, as well as increased growth in 3T3 cells (civic.EID:10387, civic.EID:12841, civic.EID:7940, OS2) Data indicate R248C may not activate FGFR3 via a dimerization mechanism (civic.EID:10511). The cancerhotspots dataset contains fewer than 50 samples with a somatic variant at this codon, with the R248C variant present in 31 samples (OM3). The R248C variant has a score of 0.86 from the REVEL in silico prediction tool (OP1). R248C is absent in the gnomAD database v4.11 (OP4). Together these codes (OS2, OM3, OP1, OP4) give a score of 8, and indicate R248C is likely oncogenic using ClinGen FGFR3 SC-VCEP modified ClinGen/CGC/VICC oncogenicity criteria.

assertion_summary: FGFR3 A391E is Likely Oncogenic
assertion_description: The A391E substitution was shown to activate FGFR3 through ligand-independent dimerization, and has dominant activation effects on hetero and homodimers containing the mutation (civc.EID:10513, civc.EID:10395, civc.EID:10654). A391E was associated with transformation and faster growth over wild type in 3T3 cells (civc.EID:12849, OS2). The A391E variant has a score of 0.716 from the REVEL in silico prediction tool (OP1). A391E is absent in the gnomAD database v4.11 (OP4). Together these codes (OS2, OP1, OP4) give a score of 6, and indicate A391E is likely oncogenic using ClinGen FGFR3 SC-VCEP modified ClinGen/CGC/VICC oncogenicity criteria.

assertion_summary: Urothelial Cancer with FGFR3 R248C is sensitive to erdafitinib
assertion_description: Erdafitinib is approved for use in adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma with FGFR3 R248C alterations based on a Phase 3 trial of 266 patients with prior treatments. In this trial, 25 patients had FGFR3 R248C mutation, and 4 had FGFR3 R248C together with a different FGFR2 or FGFR3 alteration.

assertion_summary: KRAS G12C-positive metastatic colorectal cancer is resistant to panitumumab-based therapy when panitumumab is administered without a KRAS G12C inhibitor.
assertion_description: Somatic KRAS G12C is an established negative predictive biomarker for response to panitumumab-based therapy in metastatic colorectal cancer when panitumumab is administered without a KRAS G12C inhibitor. In a randomized phase III biomarker analysis of 427 patients with chemotherapy-refractory metastatic colorectal cancer, the KRAS-mutant cohort derived no progression-free survival benefit from panitumumab monotherapy compared with best supportive care (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.73–1.36; median progression-free survival 7.4 versus 7.3 weeks), whereas the KRAS wild-type cohort benefited from panitumumab (HR 0.45, 95% CI 0.34–0.59; median progression-free survival 12.3 versus 7.3 weeks). No objective responses were observed among panitumumab-treated patients with KRAS-mutant tumors, compared with a 17% response rate among patients with KRAS wild-type tumors (civic:EID2253). The assay used in this study detected seven KRAS codon 12/13 variants, including G12C, although treatment outcomes were reported for the pooled KRAS-mutant cohort rather than separately for G12C. An accepted Level A guideline-derived Evidence Item identifies activating KRAS mutations as predictive of resistance to the alternative anti-EGFR antibodies panitumumab or cetuximab in colorectal cancer (civic:EID5345). FDA-approved companion diagnostics for conventional panitumumab treatment, such as the CRCdx RAS Mutation Detection Kit, identify RAS wild-type colorectal cancers by testing KRAS and NRAS exons 2, 3, and 4. Current FDA labeling indicates panitumumab with FOLFOX for first-line treatment and panitumumab monotherapy following progression on fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-containing chemotherapy only for RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer. Panitumumab has a separate indication in combination with sotorasib for previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer. Collectively, the clinical, guideline, and regulatory evidence supports classification of this molecular profile–disease–therapy relationship as AMP/ASCO/CAP Tier I – Level A. This assertion does not apply to panitumumab administered in combination with a KRAS G12C inhibitor, such as sotorasib.

assertion_summary: KRAS A146P-positive metastatic colorectal cancer is resistant to cetuximab-based therapy.
assertion_description: Somatic KRAS A146P is a negative predictive biomarker for the response to cetuximab treatment in metastatic colorectal cancer. In a retrospective analysis of patients with irinotecan-refractory metastatic colorectal cancer treated with cetuximab combined with irinotecan, the evidence item that corresponds to A146P profile was taken from one patient who had a tumor mutant for KRAS codon 146 and did not respond. Among patients without BRAF mutation, no response was observed in any of eight patients with tumors having a mutation in KRAS codon 61 or 146, while 22 out of 60 patients with wild-type tumors at both codons responded (0% vs 37%, p=0.047). Patients with codon 61/146 mutation had a shorter median progression free survival (3.8 vs 5.3 months; reported HR 0.45; p=0.023), but there was no significant difference in overall survival (9.7 vs 14.8 months; p=0.320) (civic:EID2225). Civic:EID3856 and civic:EID13017 refer to the same cohort of patients described by Loupakis et al. and therefore cannot be regarded as separate studies. The publication describes the individual case as a codon 146 mutation, not as A146P-specific outcome. The submitted evidence civic:EID13023 provides relatively low weight support because of KRAS A146P detection in circulating tumor DNA prior to cetuximab- or panitumumab-based anti-EGFR re-challenge therapy, however, without isolation of individual treatment assignment and outcome. On the contrary, the submitted preclinical evidence civic:EID12068 demonstrated cetuximab sensitivity in an engineered model with KRAS A146P in HT29 cells. Such a conflicting D-level evidence derived from a short-term experiment in engineered cell line viability and has less value in comparison with the clinical and regulatory evidence related to KRAS exon 4 codon 146 mutation. The FDA labeling declares that cetuximab is not indicated for patients with metastatic colorectal cancer with KRAS or NRAS exon 4 codon 146 mutation and limits the use of standard cetuximab in RAS wild-type diseases, which includes cetuximab with FOLFIRI for first line therapy, cetuximab with irinotecan after irinotecan refractory, and cetuximab monotherapy in subsequent lines. Thus, the classification of the molecular profile-disease-therapy combination is AMP/ASCO/CAP Tier I – Level A.

assertion_summary: FGFR3 P449S is classified as Likely Benign according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.
assertion_description: In vitro studies indicate that the P449S variant does not affect normal FGFR3 function in a manner consistent with oncogenic activation. Introduction of the P449S variant into NIH/3T3 cells does not result in biochemical activation of the FGFR3 protein (civic.EID:13089) (SBS2_Supporting). The P449S variant is present in the gnomAD database v4.1 at a minor allele frequency greater than 0.001 (0.58%; gnomAD v4.1.0 Grpmax Filtering AF, 95% confidence) (SBS1). These codes lead to an Oncogenicity score of -5 (SBS2_Supporting [-1]; SBS1 [-4]). Therefore, FGFR3 P449S is classified as Likely Benign according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.

assertion_summary: FGFR3 G380R is classified as Likely Oncogenic according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.
assertion_description: In vitro studies indicate that the G380R variant affects normal FGFR3 function in a manner consistent with oncogenic activation. Functional experiments demonstrate increased phosphorylation compared to wild-type (civic.eid:10368, civic.eid:10416) increased FGFR3 dimer stability (civic.eid:10396), ligand independent dimerization (civic.eid:10403) and proliferation studies (using the MANO method) demonstrate increased cell proliferation compared to wild type (civic.eid:12847) (OS2). FGFR3 G380R is identified as a statistically enriched hotspot in the cancerhotspots database. The cancerhotspots dataset contains fewer than 50 samples with a somatic variant at this codon, but the G380R variant is present in ten or more samples (OM3). The G380R variant has a score of 0.696 from the REVEL in silico prediction tool which is close but does not meet the required 0.7 threshold. Both c.1138G>A and c.1138G>C that lead to G380R are absent in the gnomAD database or present at a minor allele frequency of less than 0.0001 (Grpmax Filtering AF, 95% confidence) (OP4). These codes lead to an Oncogenicity score of 7 (OS2 [4]; OM3 [2]; OP4 [1]). Therefore, FGFR3 G380R is classified as a Likely Oncogenic according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.

assertion_summary: FGFR3 G65R is classified as Benign according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.
assertion_description: Functional studies testing the G65R variant were not identified. The G65R variant has a score of 0.04 from the REVEL in silico prediction tool (SBP1). The c.193G>A variant is present in the gnomAD database at a minor allele frequency of greater than 0.001 (has a value of 2.1% Grpmax Filtering AF, 95% confidence) (SBS1). These codes lead to an Oncogenicity score of -9 (SBVS1 [-8]; SBP1 [-1]). Therefore, FGFR3 G65R is classified as a Benign according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.

assertion_summary: FGFR3 R805Q is classified as Likely Benign according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.
assertion_description: In vitro studies indicate that the R805Q variant does not affect normal FGFR3 function in a manner consistent with oncogenic activation. Introduction of the R805Q variant into Ba/F3 or MCF10A cells does not result in increased cell proliferation (civic.EID:12968)[SBS2_Supporting]. The R805Q variant has a score of less than 0.3 (0.25) from the REVEL in silico prediction tool [SBP1]. The R805Q variant is absent in the gnomAD database or present at a minor allele frequency of less than 0.0001 (Grpmax Filtering AF, 95% confidence = 0.0000146 Non-Finnish European) [OP4]. These codes lead to an Oncogenicity score of -1 (SBS2_Supporting [-1]; SBP1 [-1]; OP4 [1]). Therefore, FGFR3 R805Q is classified as Likely Benign according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.

assertion_summary: IDH1 R132H is sensitive to olutasidenib in acute myeloid leukemia.
assertion_description: IDH1 R132H is a recurrent missense mutation affecting the catalytic arginine residue of IDH1 that predicts response to olutasidenib in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Clinical evidence from a phase 2 trial demonstrates that olutasidenib monotherapy produces objective responses in patients with relapsed or refractory IDH1 R132H-mutated AML, although response rates are lower than those observed for other IDH1 R132 substitution variants and may be influenced by concurrent genomic alterations (civic.eid:13079). Additional studies in patients with IDH1 R132-mutated AML support the overall clinical activity of olutasidenib monotherapy in this molecular subgroup (civic.eid:13078, civic.eid:13080, civic.eid:13091). Collectively, these findings support the sensitivity of IDH1 R132H-mutated AML to olutasidenib.

assertion_summary: FGFR3 A500T is classified as Likely Benign according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.
assertion_description: In vitro studies indicate that the A500T variant does not affect normal FGFR3 function in a manner consistent with oncogenic activation. Purified protein in vitro auto-phosphorylation assays showed that compared to wild type, A500T does not significantly increase auto-phosphorylation (civic.id:13090). A500T was classified as Neutral in a saturation mutagenesis study (civic.eid:13092). A500T is absent in the cancerhotspots database and present at only a few counts in CBioPortal and Cosmic (in both cases not observed in urothelial cancers). The A500T variant has a score of 0.16 from the REVEL in silico prediction tool (SBP1). The GNOMAD frequency (0.039%, Grpmax Filtering AF, 95% confidence) does not meet criteria for any code. These codes lead to an Oncogenicity score of -1 (SBP1 [-1]). Therefore, FGFR3 A500T is classified as a Likely Benign according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.

assertion_summary: FGFR3 L164V is classified as Likely Benign according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.
assertion_description: No functional data was found for FGFR3 L164V in any high throughput or other experimental studies (this amino acid position is not within the kinase domain, where these assays are often focused). L164V was absent from cancerhotspots and CBioPortal. The L164V variant has a score of 0.218 from the REVEL in silico prediction tool (SBP1). The c.490C>G variant is present in the gnomAD database at a minor allele frequency of greater than 0.001 (0.0058 or 0.58%; Grpmax Filtering AF, 95% confidence) (SBS1). These codes lead to an Oncogenicity score of -5 (SBP1 [-1]; SBS1 [-4]). Therefore, FGFR3 L164V is classified as a Likely Benign according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.

assertion_summary: FGFR3 T450M is classified as Benign according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.
assertion_description: The T450M variant has been reported in the literature (civic.eid:12595, civic.eid:12596) but no published functional data could be found, including in existing high throughput studies. T450M is absent in the cancerhotspots database and present at only a few counts in CBioPortal and Cosmic (in both cases not observed in urothelial cancers). The T450M variant has a score of 0.117 from the REVEL in silico prediction tool (SBP1). The c.1349C>T variant is present in the gnomAD database at a minor allele frequency of greater than 0.01 (0.01984 or 1.984%, Grpmax Filtering AF, 95% confidence) (SBVS1). These codes lead to an Oncogenicity score of -9 (SBP1 [-1]; SBVS1 [-8]. Therefore, FGFR3 T450M is classified as a Benign according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.

assertion_summary: BRAF V600K-mutant melanoma is sensitive to vemurafenib.
assertion_description: Clinical evidence supports the predictive role of BRAF V600K for response to vemurafenib in melanoma. In the phase III BRIM-3 trial, patients with BRAF V600K metastatic melanoma treated with vemurafenib had significantly improved overall survival and progression-free survival compared with dacarbazine (civic.EID:1399). Phase II evidence also demonstrated responses to vemurafenib among patients with BRAF V600K metastatic melanoma (civic.EID:4177). Additional case reports describe clinical and radiological responses to vemurafenib, including responses in patients with cerebral metastases and a sustained complete radiological response (civic.EID:4179; civic.EID:1400). Preclinical studies further support the sensitivity of BRAF V600K-mutant melanoma cells to vemurafenib (civic.EID:4173). Collectively, these findings support the predictive role of BRAF V600K for sensitivity to vemurafenib in melanoma.

assertion_summary: FGFR3 K650E is classified as Oncogenic according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.
assertion_description: In vitro and in vivo studies indicate that the K650E variant affects normal FGFR3 function in a manner consistent with oncogenic activation. Functional studies demonstrate substantially increased FGFR3 kinase activity and autophosphorylation compared with wild-type FGFR3, as well as increased cell proliferation and cellular transformation (civic.EID:10086, civic.EID:10393, civic.EID:12845). In vivo studies further demonstrate rapid transformation of hematopoietic cells and tumor formation in mice expressing K650E (civic.EID:10370) (OS2). The cBioPortal contains fewer than 50 samples with a somatic variant at this codon, with the K650E variant present in ten or more samples (OM3). The p.K650N variant, which affects the same codon as the p.K650E variant, has been determined to be Likely Oncogenic, indicating that the p.K650E variant also may be oncogenic (OM4). The p.K650E variant has a score of 0.837 from the REVEL in silico prediction tool (OP1). The FGFR3 c.1948A>G variant is absent in the gnomAD database (OP4). These codes lead to an Oncogenicity score of 10 (OS2 [4]; OM3 [2]; OM4 [2]; OP1 [1]; OP4 [1]). Therefore, the FGFR3 p.K650E variant is classified as Oncogenic according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.

assertion_summary: FGFR3 N540K is classified as Uncertain Significance according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.
assertion_description: In vitro studies indicate that the N540K variant affects normal FGFR3 function in a manner consistent with oncogenic activation. NIH3T3 colony formation assays demonstrate a transformed phenotype with increased colony formation and elevated phospho-ERK/ERK signaling compared to wild-type (civic.eid:12702), and saturation mutagenesis screening classified N540K as potentially activating based on increased growth factor-independent proliferation (civic.eid:12881). Functional studies show increased autophosphorylation and kinase activity compared to wild-type (civic.eid:10084, civic.eid:10389) (OS2). The N540K variant is absent from the cancerhotspots, CBioPortal and Cosmic databases and the REVEL score associated with this variant (0.693) does not meet the 0.7 threshold. Both c.1620C>G and c.1620C>A variants are absent in the gnomAD database or present at a minor allele frequency of less than 0.0001 (Grpmax Filtering AF, 95% confidence) (OP4). These codes lead to an Oncogenicity score of 5 (OS2 [4]; OP4 [1]). Therefore, FGFR3 N540K is classified as Uncertain Significance according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.

assertion_summary: FGFR3 K650N is classified as Likely Oncogenic according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.
assertion_description: In vitro studies indicate that the K650N variant affects normal FGFR3 function in a manner consistent with oncogenic activation. Functional studies demonstrate increased FGFR3 kinase activity and autophosphorylation compared with wild-type FGFR3, as well as significantly increased cell proliferation and transforming activity (civic.EID:10087, civic.EID:12846, civic.EID:10377) (OS2). The p.K650N variant is present in the cancerhotspots dataset in fewer than 10 samples (OP3). The p.K650E variant, which affects the same codon as the p.K650N variant, has been determined to be Likely Oncogenic, indicating that the p.K650N variant also may be oncogenic (OM4). The FGFR3 c.1950G>C variant is absent in the gnomAD database (OP4). These codes lead to an Oncogenicity score of 8 (OS2 [4]; OM4 [2]; OP3 [1]; OP4 [1]). Therefore, the FGFR3 p.K650N variant is classified as Likely Oncogenic according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.

assertion_summary: FGFR3 G370C is classified as Likely Oncogenic according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.
assertion_description: In vitro studies indicate that the G370C variant affects normal FGFR3 function in a manner consistent with oncogenic activation. Functional studies demonstrate ligand-independent FGFR3 dimerization, increased basal receptor phosphorylation, constitutive MAPK activation and c-fos transcriptional activity, as well as significantly increased cell proliferation and transforming activity compared with wild-type FGFR3 (civic.EID:13141, civic.EID:12843) (OS2). The cBioPortal contains fewer than 50 samples with a somatic variant at this codon, with the G370C variant present in ten or more samples (OM3). The FGFR3 c.1108G>T variant is absent in the gnomAD database (OP4). These codes lead to an Oncogenicity score of 7 (OS2 [4]; OM3 [2]; OP4 [1]). Therefore, the FGFR3 p.G370C variant is classified as Likely Oncogenic according to the FGFR SC-VCEP Oncogenicity specifications.
